Bằng chứng sửa tận gốc có hiệu quả: Wazuh đỏ 10/67 lượt trước #398, 0/96 lượt sau. Test chập chờn mới vẫn sinh từ code mới (INV19 từ #421, Mirror từ #401, #432 lộ khi PR bỏ `-race`), nên cần guard chặn kiểu test này (D-374). Rà main: 33 chỗ so thời gian trôi + 10 `time.Sleep` trong test; không có test hiệu năng thuần. Tham khảo: Google Testing Blog, [Flaky Tests at Google and How We Mitigate Them](https://testing.googleblog.com/2016/05/flaky-tests-at-google-and-how-we.html) (~16 % test có chập chờn, 84 % lần chuyển xanh→đỏ dính test chập chờn; cách ly + chạy lại để phát hiện, không để cho qua); Luo et al., [An Empirical Analysis of Flaky Tests](https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/2635868.2635920) (FSE 2014: chờ bất đồng bộ ~45 %, tranh chấp ~20 %, thứ tự test ~12 %); Go [`testing/synctest`](https://pkg.go.dev/testing/synctest) (đồng hồ giả trong bubble, chuẩn từ Go 1.25); GitHub Docs [Managing a merge queue](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/configuring-pull-request-merges/managing-a-merge-queue) (queue kiểm bản ghép nên PR không cần đuổi `main`). **Không chọn:** một AI làm hết (ít xung đột nhưng chậm; nút cổ chai là cổng CI chập chờn và sức chạy CI miễn phí, không phải số AI); chạy lại test đỏ cho qua (che lỗi thật, INV19 có thể là lỗi sản phẩm khi box bận); bỏ các test thời gian (chúng giữ bất biến an toàn: không treo, hết hạn → "không rõ", chống giữ slot); `make check` -race bắt buộc (cần khe việc nặng, D-370). | 2026-11-12 |
| D-375 | **Bằng chứng sửa test chập chờn đo rẻ (sửa D-373 (3)).** Chỉ chạy đúng test đó (`-run '^TestX$'`); trước khi sửa: ép tải tới khi đỏ hoặc hết 5 phút (N/M, hoặc giải thích cơ chế); sau khi sửa: test chuyển sang `testing/synctest` hoặc chờ theo trạng thái → 20 lần xanh là đủ (tất định theo cấu trúc, không còn phụ thuộc đồng hồ); test vẫn dùng đồng hồ thật → 0/100 lần trong tối đa 10 phút. Không lặp `-race` cả gói chỉ để lấy số. | kien 2026-11-12: subagent sửa test chập chờn dùng phần lớn thời gian để chạy test. Đo: gói `modules/response` chạy `-race` ~120 s mỗi lượt, nên "0/≥100 lần" cho cả gói là hàng giờ máy cho mỗi bản sửa (agent chạy hơn 1,5 giờ, phần lớn là các lượt đo tải với `yes` đốt CPU, đẩy load Mac lên 72). Một test riêng lẻ chạy 1–3 s, 100 lần là vài phút. Test trên đồng hồ giả của `synctest` không đọc đồng hồ thật nên không thể chập chờn vì tốc độ máy; lặp lại chỉ còn để bắt lỗi thứ tự. Tham khảo: Go [`testing/synctest`](https://pkg.go.dev/testing/synctest); `go test -run`/`-count` ([cmd/go testflag](https://pkg.go.dev/cmd/go#hdr-Testing_flags)). **Không chọn:** bỏ hẳn bằng chứng (D-373 cần nó để biết bản sửa thật sự hết chập chờn); giữ 0/≥100 cho cả gói (quá đắt). | 2026-11-12 |
| D-376 | **Cổng merge nhanh: danh sách bỏ qua + `-race` chỉ ở lượt hằng ngày (sửa D-371, D-375).** (1) `scripts/ci/skip-tests.txt`, mỗi dòng `kind TestName package lý-do ngày-thêm`: `slow` = chỉ chạy ở lượt hằng ngày (lý do ghi thời gian chạy), `flaky` = cách ly, lý do là URL issue `KNT048/vedette`, tối đa 7 ngày (quá hạn: `ci skip` không bỏ qua nữa, test quay lại cổng, guard đỏ tới khi sửa hoặc xoá dòng). `go run ./scripts/ci skip` in mẫu `-skip '^(A\|B…)$'`; `make test-go-shard` truyền nó cho cả hai lệnh `go test` khi `SKIPTESTS=1` (mặc định), `ci.yml` đặt `SKIPTESTS` rỗng chỉ ở `schedule`; `make check-fast` luôn bỏ qua. `-skip` là cờ cache được, nên cache của `main` vẫn phục vụ. Guard `scripts/ci/skip_test.go`: mọi dòng parse được, kind đúng, flaky có issue và ≤ 7 ngày, không trùng tên (`-skip` khớp tên ở mọi gói), test còn tồn tại trong gói (`func TestX(` trong `<gói>/*_test.go`). Gieo 28 test chậm 4–83 s (chờ đồng hồ thật, chạy lại cả bộ, hoặc 2000 thiết bị qua đường quan sát). (2) `-race` chỉ ở lượt hằng ngày; pull request, merge queue **và push lên `main`** chạy không race, nên cache test không race mà `main` lưu phục vụ được hàng đợi (D-365). (3) Agent không ngồi chờ test: chạy `check-fast` một lần, push, CI là cổng; không lặp/ép tải để "chứng minh" chập chờn (bỏ phần đo của D-375); test hỏng vì chính nó → người làm PR sửa trong PR đó, không thì supervisor thêm dòng `flaky` kèm issue; test mới tối giản, kiểm chức năng, mục tiêu < 1 s, > 3 s thì vào danh sách `slow` hoặc viết lại. | kien 2026-11-12: "các loại test cho agent ngồi chờ, bỏ hết... tối ưu nó sao cho tăng tốc test nhanh nhất... sau này, viết test sao cho đạt chức năng là được, tối giản". Đo trên run `main` 43163388980: `-race` làm `modules/ai` 180 s so với 17 s không race, `modules/response` 107 so với 4, `modules/inventory` 91 so với 6, `cmd/vedette` 232 so với 61 — hàng đợi giữ `-race` (D-371) nên mỗi PR vẫn trả giá 4–8 lần ở bước cuối. Race vẫn bị bắt ở hai lượt xáo thứ tự hằng ngày (D-365), trong vòng một ngày sau khi merge. **Giới hạn chấp nhận:** một race hoặc một test chậm bị hỏng có thể vào `main` và chỉ lộ ở lượt hằng ngày (issue `flaky` tự mở, D-365). Push lên `main` chạy không race để cache test nó lưu cùng cờ với hàng đợi (giữ `-race` ở push thì `main` chỉ lưu cache bản race và hàng đợi luôn chạy nguội, D-371). **Không chọn:** giữ `-race` ở hàng đợi (4–8 lần chậm hơn cho mọi PR); giữ `-race` ở push lên `main` (cache không khớp hàng đợi, xem trên); chạy test chậm theo gói riêng (`-run` từng gói phức tạp hơn một mẫu `-skip`); `t.Skip` theo biến môi trường trong từng test (rải khắp mã, không có hạn, không guard); cách ly không hạn (Google/Shopify đều buộc chủ sở hữu và hạn). **Nguồn:** Google Testing Blog [Flaky Tests at Google and How We Mitigate Them](https://testing.googleblog.com/2016/05/flaky-tests-at-google-and-how-we.html) (TAP tách test chập chờn khỏi cổng, báo chủ sở hữu); Google [Test Sizes](https://testing.googleblog.com/2010/12/test-sizes.html) (test nhỏ chạy mọi lúc, test lớn chạy theo lịch); Shopify Engineering [The Unreasonable Effectiveness of Test Retries](https://shopify.engineering/unreasonable-effectiveness-test-retries-android-monorepo-case-study) (test chập chờn không được chặn cổng; Vedette chọn cách ly có hạn thay cho chạy lại, để không che lỗi thật); GitHub Engineering [Reducing flaky builds by 18x](https://github.blog/engineering/engineering-principles/reducing-flaky-builds-by-18x/) (tự nhận diện test chập chờn, giữ build xanh, giao issue cho tác giả commit); Go [`go help testflag`: -skip](https://pkg.go.dev/cmd/go#hdr-Testing_flags) (Go 1.20+; -skip nằm trong các cờ cache được); Go [Data Race Detector](https://go.dev/doc/articles/race_detector). | 2026-11-12 |
| D-377 | **Khôi phục sao lưu trên hộp luôn chụp dữ liệu hiện tại trước; cài hệ điều hành chụp trước nhưng không tự đặt lại (S-CORE-1, S-CORE-7).** (1) **Restore** (mới, Settings → Data → Backups on this box): danh sách bản trình hỗ trợ giữ (`GET /core/data/backups`, từ `GET /v1/state/backups` của host) và `POST /core/data/restore {backup_id, confirm_data_loss}` (202, một run). Không có `confirm_data_loss: true` → 409 `confirm_required` (cùng kiểu Rollback, D-104, D-340). `core` gọi `backup.restore` với bản chụp **kèm khoá** của dữ liệu hiện tại (`snapshotter.create(withKey=true)`, cùng đường `act` + chụp của `os.install` và chuyển phiên bản, không có máy thứ hai); host giữ nó thành bản `pre_restore` hiện trong cùng danh sách, và tự đặt lại nó khi bản khôi phục không khoẻ (`reverted`, host-api §6.12, đã có ở host). Hộp thoại nói cái gì mất (mọi thứ ghi sau ngày của bản) và cái gì còn (bản Before restore), nút chỉ bật sau "I understand". (2) **`os.install`**: chụp trước đã có (D-53, D-87: bản `pre_os_update`); lần cài hỏng **không** tự đặt lại dữ liệu, vì apt không đụng dữ liệu của Vedette và đặt lại làm mất những gì ghi trong lúc cài; người dùng khôi phục tay bản "Before operating system update" từ danh sách ở (1) nếu cần. (3) Theo run qua lần `core` bị dừng và đổi DB: run của host là bản ghi; bản sao của `core` (`core_setting` `data.restore`) nằm trong DB cũ, nên lần đọc đầu tiên của mỗi tiến trình hỏi host `backup.restore` mới nhất và ghi kết thúc (một dòng `data.restore_done`) vào DB đang chạy (INV-36). Không có lượt khởi động riêng (mỗi lần khởi động tốn một yêu cầu host); trang Data hỏi lại run khi nối lại sau khởi động. Host không cần lệnh mới: `BackupRestore` và `StateBackups` đã có trong `host/client`. **Không chọn:** khôi phục không chụp trước (mất trắng dữ liệu từ bản sao lưu tới giờ, không đường về); tự đặt lại dữ liệu sau `os.install` hỏng (mất dữ liệu ghi trong lúc cài, mà gói đã cài thì apt không gỡ); xác nhận bằng gõ tên tổ chức như Delete all data (khôi phục có đường về, nên một ô "I understand" như Rollback là đủ). | Tham khảo: OPNsense lưu bản cấu hình hiện tại vào lịch sử trước mỗi lần thay đổi và khôi phục ([Backup & Restore](https://docs.opnsense.org/manual/backups.html)); pfSense giữ lịch sử cấu hình, khôi phục một bản thì bản đang chạy vẫn nằm trong lịch sử ([Configuration History](https://docs.netgate.com/pfsense/en/latest/backup/restore-config-history.html)); Home Assistant tạo bản sao lưu trước khi cập nhật, khôi phục là việc tay ([Backups](https://www.home-assistant.io/common-tasks/general/#backups)); Proxmox VE `vzdump`/restore ghi đè máy đích và khuyên sao lưu trước, apt không có hoàn tác ([Backup and Restore](https://pve.proxmox.com/wiki/Backup_and_Restore)). Vedette chọn như pfSense/OPNsense: bản hiện tại tự vào danh sách trước khi bị thay, nên mỗi lần khôi phục đều quay lại được; và như Home Assistant/Proxmox với cập nhật hệ điều hành: sao lưu trước, không tự hoàn tác. | 2026-11-12 |
| D-378 | **SSO tới IdP sau CA nội bộ: quản trị viên dán chứng chỉ CA (PEM) trong Settings → Users → SSO; hộp tin nó chỉ cho các lời gọi tới IdP, cộng thêm vào gốc hệ thống; không có "bỏ kiểm chứng chỉ" (S-CORE-3).** (1) Trường **Identity provider CA certificate** (tuỳ chọn) trong form SSO: 1..5 chứng chỉ PEM `CERTIFICATE`, tổng ≤ 64 KB, mỗi cái phải là CA (`basicConstraints CA:TRUE`), chưa hết hạn; không có gì khác ngoài các khối PEM (khoá riêng dán nhầm → từ chối). Sai → 400 `invalid_ca` dưới chính ô đó. Lưu dạng PEM chuẩn hoá trong `oidc_config.ca_pem` (không phải bí mật: chứng chỉ công khai; GET trả lại nguyên văn kèm tên chủ thể và ngày hết hạn của từng cái). PUT không có `ca_pem` = giữ; `""` = gỡ (nút Remove). (2) **Phạm vi tin cậy**: chỉ HTTP client của module `auth-oidc` (discovery, token, JWKS, tức mọi lời gọi tới IdP), `RootCAs` = gốc hệ thống + các CA này; các lời gọi khác của hộp (feed, AI, cập nhật) không đổi. Lưu cấu hình bỏ bộ nhớ đệm discovery, nên Test connection và lần đăng nhập kế tiếp dùng ngay CA mới. (3) **Không** có tuỳ chọn bỏ kiểm chứng chỉ (security.md; Jenkins/Grafana có nó và tài liệu của họ cảnh báo chỉ dùng thử). (4) **Không chọn TOFU** (ghim lần đầu như Wazuh pull, D-33): ở D-33 hộp tự gọi một máy trong lab và quản trị viên so dấu vân tay; với IdP, chứng chỉ lá của IdP nội bộ thường xoay vòng ngắn (ACME nội bộ, Keycloak sau reverse proxy), ghim lá sẽ hỏng âm thầm ở lần xoay kế tiếp, còn ghim lần đầu không chứng minh gì nếu đường mạng lúc đó bị chặn giữa. CA là thứ quản trị viên đã có (cùng tệp họ cài cho trình duyệt) và không đổi khi lá xoay. (5) Thông báo `discovery_failed` "the box does not trust the identity provider's certificate" thêm gợi ý dán CA ở ô này. Luồng dữ liệu rời hộp không đổi (cùng IdP), `PRIVACY.md` không đổi. **Không chọn:** cài CA vào kho tin cậy của hệ điều hành (GitLab `trusted-certs`, Rancher `privateCA`): rộng hơn cần (mọi lời gọi của hộp tin CA đó), cần shell trên appliance, và mất khi cài lại; một ô "skip verify". | Tham khảo: Argo CD `oidc.config.rootCA`, PEM CA chỉ cho lời gọi tới OIDC provider ([User management](https://argo-cd.readthedocs.io/en/stable/operator-manual/user-management/#configuring-a-custom-root-ca-certificate-for-communicating-with-the-oidc-provider)); HashiCorp Vault `oidc_discovery_ca_pem` ([JWT/OIDC auth API](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/api-docs/auth/jwt#oidc_discovery_ca_pem)); Grafana generic OAuth `tls_client_ca` và `tls_skip_verify_insecure` ([Generic OAuth](https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/setup-grafana/configure-security/configure-authentication/generic-oauth/)); GitLab cài CA vào `/etc/gitlab/trusted-certs` cho cả hộp ([Custom certificates](https://docs.gitlab.com/omnibus/settings/ssl/#install-custom-public-certificates)); Rancher `privateCA` cho cả cụm ([Private CA](https://ranchermanager.docs.rancher.com/getting-started/installation-and-upgrade/resources/add-tls-secrets)); Jenkins OpenID Connect plugin dựa vào kho JVM và có ô tắt kiểm chứng chỉ ([oic-auth](https://plugins.jenkins.io/oic-auth/)). Vedette chọn như Argo CD/Vault: CA dán trong cấu hình SSO, chỉ cho IdP; không skip verify. | 2026-11-12 |
| D-380 | **Sensor thụ động có card mặc định: chưa ai chọn card thì nghe trên card quản trị của hộp, không cần cấu hình (S-INV-1, #471).** (1) **Quy tắc**: card đã chọn (cổng SPAN trong Settings → Box network, hay card `SetInterface` lưu) luôn thắng; không có lựa chọn (`sp_sensor.interface` NULL, kể cả sau khi tắt SPAN) thì sensor nghe trên **card quản trị** mà vedette-host báo: card quản trị đã cấu hình, không có thì card giữ default route, không có nữa thì card duy nhất có địa chỉ (cùng hàm `mgmtIface` của trang Box network), và chỉ khi nó là card thật của hộp (`cardsOf`: không bao giờ loopback, cầu nối container `vedette0`, veth, docker, bridge); card đó là link ảo (default route trên `wg0`, `br0`) thì lấy card thật duy nhất có IPv4, hai card trở lên thì không chọn. (2) **Không lưu mặc định**: nó được tính ở mỗi lần nhìn (`GET /config` long-poll, `GET /inventory/sensors`), nên đổi card quản trị thì sensor theo trong ≤ ~10 s và lần chọn sau của quản trị viên thắng; host trục trặc thì giữ câu trả lời cuối, sensor không ngừng nghe. (3) **Bản chỉ container** (không có host, D-168): mặc định lấy từ heartbeat của sensor: trong các card đang lên có IPv4 toàn cục, đúng một card có dây thì chọn nó; không có card có dây mà đúng một card không dây (`wl*`, `ww*`) thì chọn card đó; hai ứng viên trở lên là không rõ, không chọn (sensor chờ quản trị viên), không đoán. (4) Tên card từ host hay sensor là dữ liệu không tin cậy: qua `sensorlink.ValidIfaceName` ở biên trước khi gửi cho sensor. (5) `vedette0` (cầu nối của chính hộp, D-267) thêm vào luật "liên kết ảo" của sensor và trang Box network, nên không còn hiện là lựa chọn. `GET /inventory/sensors` trả `interface` là card đang nghe (đúng mô tả trong `contract.ts`: "the SPAN port when SPAN is on, else the management port"); hợp đồng API không đổi. **Không chọn:** để trống chờ quản trị viên (Zeek, Security Onion bắt chọn card lúc cài) vì trái S-INV-1 "thụ động chạy không cần cấu hình" và Vedette không phải IDS SPAN-trước; card đầu tiên đang lên (mặc định của tcpdump/libpcap) vì trên hộp có `vedette0` và Wi-Fi nó có thể là cầu nối; khớp dải LAN của trình hướng dẫn vì card quản trị đã là card hộp dùng trên LAN và cần đọc bảng của module khác. | Tham khảo: tcpdump không có `-i` thì lấy giao diện đang lên có số nhỏ nhất, trừ loopback ([tcpdump(1)](https://www.tcpdump.org/manpages/tcpdump.1.html)); Home Assistant tự bật adapter mạng theo default route, người dùng đổi được ([Network integration](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/network/)); Pi-hole nghe trên giao diện đặt lúc cài và đổi được trong Settings ([Interfaces](https://docs.pi-hole.net/ftldns/interfaces/)); Security Onion bắt chọn card quản trị và card giám sát lúc cài ([Configuration](https://docs.securityonion.net/en/2.4/configuration.html)). Vedette chọn như Home Assistant/Pi-hole: card của default route (card quản trị), chọn tay thắng. | 2026-11-12 |

Không suy từ file socket vắng (một appliance có host khởi động chậm sẽ thành "container" tới lần khởi động sau; cùng định nghĩa D-263 "không có host = core chạy không có `-host-socket`"). (2) **Thay D-168 (8)** ("không thêm `install_kind`, GUI học từ 409 `not_appliance`"): học từ 409 nghĩa là trang phải gọi endpoint chắc chắn hỏng rồi mới biết (lượt đi thật thấy mỗi trang 2 lỗi 409 đỏ trong console), và gói setup không biết bỏ honeypot. (3) **Module cần host**: khoá tuỳ chọn `needs_host: true` trong MANIFEST (honeypot, scan-credentialed: container của nó do vedette-host dựng, D-55). Sensor thụ động và scan **không** cần host (chạy bằng `compose.sensors.yaml`, D-168), nên không đánh dấu. (4) **Trang theo kiểu cài, không gọi endpoint của host**: Updates (khối lệnh `docker compose pull` / `up -d`, hệ điều hành là của khách), Data (khối lệnh sao lưu/khôi phục volume `vedette_data` của `INSTALL-CONTAINER.md` §6, không Download backup / Backups on this box), Box network (câu "tự chuẩn bị card"). (5) **Không thử lại câu trả lời dưới 500**: TanStack Query mặc định thử lại mọi lỗi; 409/404/403 của hộp là câu trả lời cuối nên thử lại chỉ cho lỗi mạng và 5xx (một lần). | Tham khảo: Home Assistant Container không có Supervisor nên không có add-on, sao lưu và cập nhật trong giao diện; giao diện chỉ hiện các mục đó khi thành phần `hassio` được nạp, và tài liệu bảo người dùng tự `docker compose pull` rồi `up -d` (https://www.home-assistant.io/installation/#advanced-installation-methods, https://www.home-assistant.io/installation/linux/#docker-compose). Không công tắc "bỏ qua kiểm chữ ký": index, manifest vẫn kiểm bằng khoá nhúng của bản dựng, host kiểm lại. Chọn tệp trong `core_data` thay vì biến môi trường vì unit Quadlet của core do host sinh từ hằng trong mã (D-123): thêm biến là sửa đường khách hàng; tệp đọc mỗi lần dùng nên viết được sau khi cài, không cần khởi động lại. | D-383 | **Trap and decoy state come from what the box did, and the decoy IP is cleared only while every trap is off (S-HP-1, real-install QA 2026-11-12).** (1) Clearing the decoy IP (`PUT /honeypot/config` with an empty `secondary_ip`) is refused with 409 `traps_on` while any trap is on; the box never turns traps off behind the owner's back, and a trap cannot be switched on with no IP (re-checked inside the write transaction). Chosen over "clearing turns the traps off" because the big clouds make the owner release first: an AWS Elastic IP to release must not be associated with a resource, and Azure deletes a public IP only when it is not associated to any IP configuration or network interface, so an explicit order beats an implicit state change. (2) `Trap.state` and `Decoy.state` are `off`, `listening`, `conflict`, `starting`, `stopping`, `failed`: reported from the host (the container runs with the service on and the host holds the address), never inferred from the switch; only the owner's changes (and the module turning on) make a trap `starting`, inventory events do not; `failed` carries the host's plain reason. (3) A refused address is asked again three times, then every 10 minutes, and again when the wanted set changes or the module is turned off, so ten failing decoys cannot use the host's 10 writes a minute. (4) While the inventory has no device in the network the spare-IP hint says "not checked", not "unused". Sources: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/using-instance-addressing-eips-releasing.html, https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/ip-services/virtual-network-public-ip-address | 2026-11-12 |
| D-384 | **The `new_port` trigger ("A new port opens on a public IP") is fed by a bridge in `cmd/vedette`, not marked unavailable; the known-bad destination check shares logs' special-nets list (S-RESP-3).** (1) Nothing published `exposure.port.opened`: exposure publishes only `exposure.snapshot.created` with counts, so a customer's `tpl-newport-msg` rule silently never ran. On each `exposure.snapshot.created` the bridge (`exposurePortsOpened`, subscribed for `response`, reads nothing while `exposure` is off) compares that scan day with the previous scan day of the same target through exposure's own public `Snapshots`/`Diff`/`SnapshotOf`, and publishes one `exposure.port.opened {target_id, date, ip, port, service}` per port that is open now and was not then (payload type `response.PortOpenedEvent`; the exposure module is not edited, D-65). An address spelled differently from the day before (IPv4-mapped) is compared in canonical form and is not new. (2) **The first scan day of a target is the baseline** and opens nothing (a new target does not message every port it already had). (3) **One event per target, day, address and port**: a second scan on the same day replaces that day's snapshot and does not run a rule again for a port already announced; a port that closes and opens again on a later day does. A port that opened while `response` was off is not announced later (SYS-5). (4) At most **20 events per scan** (each is a write to response's event backlog; rules run later in its evaluate job); the rest stay in the Exposure diff and the box log says how many were left out. The bridge detaches from exposure's 5-second publish deadline and uses its own 30 s (as the baseline re-match does), because a port not stored then is never announced. (5) Response checks every field at the edge like the other triggers: target id by the name regex, day `YYYY-MM-DD`, address by `CheckValue(ip)` and the block list's `publishable` (not private, CGNAT, 198.18/15, 6to4…; IPv4 documentation kept, D-88 L4), port 1..65535, service guess one line ≤ 60 after `cleanLine` (a banner). `device` stays empty: no source maps a public address to the device behind NAT. (6) **A pre-approved rule never acts on the new port's own address** (`heldForAuto`: an address or range value covering `ip` waits for a person): it is the customer's own public address or whatever a name of theirs resolves to (shared hosting, a dangling record someone took over). A message about it is not an action on it. (7) `iocEvent` now refuses a destination that `signature.PublicDest` of logs refuses (CGNAT 100.64/10 such as a Tailscale peer, documentation, 198.18/15 benchmarking, 6to4, NAT64…): response imports the stdlib-only `modules/logs/signature` package read-only, so one list decides "public" for both the hit and the rule. **Limit:** exposure has no scan `Runner` yet (#115, D-131 (3)), so a real box makes no snapshot and the trigger has no events until that lands; the bridge then works with no further change. A change of the box's time zone can put a scan on a day older than the newest snapshot, which may announce a port again under that day (rare, accepted). | **Why a bridge and not "unavailable":** the trigger, its fields, the template and the GUI already exist and match the mock; marking it unavailable needs a new contract field, a mock and a rule-editor change (a GUI story) for a gap the bridge closes in the binary, which already adapts module ports (responseLogCounts, logsIocEvidence). Top tier: Shodan Monitor's `new_service` trigger fires "whenever Shodan finds a service/port on your network that it hasn't seen before", i.e. against what was seen before, not on every sighting (https://help.shodan.io/command-line-interface/4-network-monitoring; webhook delivery names the trigger, https://help.shodan.io/developer-fundamentals/monitor-webhooks); a SANS ISC write-up notes the noise of uncommon ports on large networks (https://isc.sans.edu/diary/24956), hence the baseline and the per-scan cap. Pre-approval held as for forgeable subjects (D-286 (4), D-336). Not chosen: a diff kept by response (it would read exposure's tables, rules/modules.md); emitting from inside exposure (Emily's module; a deferred line asks her to consider publishing it herself); one event per changed snapshot (a rule could not name the port). Independent Opus review: 1 MEDIUM (pre-approval on the address, fixed as (6)), LOW (special nets, deadline, canonical address, wording) fixed. Sources: deferred feat-response-core.md:10, feat-response-ioc-hits.md:5. | 2026-11-12 |
| D-385 | **Amends D-263 (which stays the rule: without `vedette-host` the latest passive heartbeat decides the sensor's card, with a host D-118) with what D-263 did not cover.** (1) **90 s freshness:** without a host only a heartbeat younger than 90 s counts, the same rule as `online` (`onlineWithin`); an older one is "not reported in the last 90 seconds" (`bad_interface` in `SetInterface`). (2) **The box's own cards (`boxAddresses`, INV-6) follow the same source as `SetInterface`**, replacing D-263's "`netHost.Interfaces` stays for `boxAddresses`": with a host, `Host.HostCards`; without one, the fresh heartbeat's cards, never the core container's own interfaces (on the bridge it sees only its own link, so the real host cards were not excluded and the box could appear as a device). `osInterfaces` is removed from `cmd/vedette`; `netHost.Interfaces` is `HostCards` for `Service.Run` only (never started in production, D-141). (3) When those cards are unknown (configured host with no list yet; no host and no fresh heartbeat) the batch is held with **503 `not_ready`** (new code of the closed sensorlink set, `Retry-After` 5 s); the capture splits batches and blames lone items only on `store_busy`, so `not_ready` is retried whole and never drops an item. Accepted: an older sensor treats `not_ready` like `store_busy`, but sensor and core images ship in one release; a box with a socket path set but no helper holds passive batches (logged; queue max 5000). A compromised sensor can list extra addresses as the box's to hide devices, which it can already do by not reporting them; the list stays bounded by `sensorlink` (≤ 32 cards). | Freshness reuses the protocol's liveness window (`docs/specs/sensor-protocol.md` §6.3), as Prometheus marks a target down after failed scrapes instead of trusting its last sample (https://prometheus.io/docs/concepts/jobs_instances/). "Not yet" kept apart from "this item is bad" follows OTLP, which retries 503 whole and drops only what the server marks rejected (https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/otlp/#failures). Sources of the base rule: D-263. Code: `modules/sensor-passive/backend.go`, `service.go`, `capture/run.go`, `core/sensorlink/errors.go`, `cmd/vedette/sensorpassive.go`. | 2026-11-12 |
| D-386 | **A revoked running release and stale update information are shown, not only logged (S-CORE-2, update-manifest §4.1, §8, §13 (d)).** (1) `UpdatesState.running_revoked` (null or `{version, reason, since, action}`) names a revocation in the newest stored index that hits the release this box runs: kind `release` with the running version, or kind `image_digest` with a digest of the running release's manifest (when that manifest is known). A `key` revocation is not a running-release revocation: the box keeps the software and only stops trusting new documents signed by that key (§8); `advisory_only` stays an advisory. With several hits the one with a warning action wins. (2) Where it shows follows the maintainer's `action`: `block_install_and_warn` and `rollback_if_possible` are a critical banner on **every page** for every signed-in role, linking to Settings → Updates; `block_install` only blocks new installs (for example a build whose upgrade fails on some boxes while boxes already on it are fine), so it is a warning on the Updates page only. This settles §8's "banner on every page" against the action names, which would otherwise make `block_install_and_warn` mean nothing. (3) `UpdatesState.stale_since` is the stored index's `expires_at` once it has passed, null otherwise (no index yet, or current). It is a warning on the Updates page, not on every page, and it never blocks Apply or a bundle (§4.1, D-104): the usual cause is a box that cannot reach GitHub or has the check off, and the page then says which; the freeze-attack case (§13 (d)) looks the same to the box, so the words say newer and withdrawn releases may be missing. Both fields are computed on read from the stored, re-verified index (no new request; the clock decides staleness, so a box whose checks keep failing turns stale by itself). Not in this decision: the admin-channel notice of §8 and the automatic rollback of `rollback_if_possible` (deferred). Top-tier: TUF makes an expired timestamp/snapshot/targets file abort the update and "report the potential freeze attack" rather than fail silently (spec §5.3–5.6); Home Assistant Repairs keeps issue severities and reserves the highest one for real emergencies, the rest stay in the Repairs list; Chrome and Firefox show "can't update" in their own menu or About page, not over every tab. Sources: https://theupdateframework.github.io/specification/latest/, https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/core/platform/repairs, https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/questions/1499917 | 2026-11-12 |
| D-387 | **Container-only: the admin picks the SPAN card among the cards the sensor reported, under Sensors (S-CORE-8 G6, S-CORE-9; the lead decision of `.ai/deferred/feat-container-only.md` slice 5, on top of D-263 and D-385).** (1) **What**: without `vedette-host` Vedette does no host operation for SPAN (no netplan, no promiscuous switch, no address change): the customer prepares the card (`docs/INSTALL-CONTAINER.md`), and Vedette only tells the sensor which card to read. The list offered is the card list of the passive heartbeat (D-263), and the choice is checked against a heartbeat younger than 90 s (D-385); a card with an IPv4 address in that list is refused as a SPAN card (`bad_interface`). (2) **Where**: Devices → Scope and sensors → Sensor on this box → Configure, not Settings → Box network: on this install Box network never calls `/core/network*` (D-381) and its built sentence already sends the admin "choose the card under Sensors"; the list comes from `GET /inventory/sensors` (`interfaces`), which that page already reads. With no card reported yet the dialog says "No card reported yet: start the sensor" and has no Save. On an appliance the dialog stays read-only with the link to Box network (D-56: the host applies the SPAN card). (3) **Route**: `PATCH /inventory/sensors/{id}` `{interface, span}` (the route sensor-passive CONTRACT INV-9 and the `bad_interface` row of API_CONVENTIONS 3.3 already named) answers the updated `Sensor`; it calls `Service.SetInterface`. With a host (appliance), or a configured host that gives no list, it answers **409 `set_in_box_network`** and changes nothing (D-118: only the host decides there). The lead note said "`PUT /core/network/span` without a host"; not taken, because that route answers a whole `NetworkState` (management address, NTP, roles of the box's cards) that has no meaning without a host and would have to be filled with blanks, and its body carries extraction switches, filters and limits that the container-only page cannot read back (no GET of them without a host), so every save would send guesses; `PUT /core/network/span` keeps 409 `not_appliance` without a host. The extraction switches and filters stay the defaults on container-only (all four read, no filter, as on a new appliance) until a story offers them there. (4) **A sensor never heard from** is `status: never_connected` ("Not connected yet"), not `offline` ("Lost contact"): `offline` needs a heartbeat seen once (`sp_sensor.last_seen` set). Found on a real container-only walk with no sensor started (2026-11-12). | Lead decision (slice 5 note) plus D-263, D-385, D-381, D-380. Top-tier: Home Assistant Container leaves the host's devices to the host and only uses what it is given (https://www.home-assistant.io/installation/linux/); Zeek's operator names the capture interface the sensor reads, prepared on the machine beforehand (`interface=` in `node.cfg`, https://docs.zeek.org/en/master/quickstart.html). "Lost contact" for a sensor that never connected sends the admin looking for a fault instead of the missing start step. Code: `modules/sensor-passive/handlers.go`, `service.go`; `web/src/features/inventory/SensorsSection.tsx`, `contract.ts`, `mocks.ts`. | 2026-11-12 |
| D-388 | **Automatic software update: when the box checks and when it installs by itself (S-CORE-2; update-manifest §6, §12).** (1) A `core` job (`software-update`) looks every 10 minutes; a check is due 6 h ± 30 min (drawn per check) after the previous check of this process, or after the stored `last_check` when it has made none, and never at the first tick of a process (core's own update switch restarts it); it is the same check as `POST /core/updates/check` (one `update.check` row, user `system`); nothing at all while update checks are off under Privacy or before first-run setup (no install id: the administrator has not seen Privacy yet). (2) In automatic mode, after a check from the page or the job and at every tick, the release on offer is installed through the Apply run as user `system` only when: the box has a `vedette-host` (container-only never updates itself, §7); now is inside the `os.settings` maintenance window ("any time" counts) with at least 30 minutes of it left; no reboot is scheduled in the next 6 hours; no software, OS or restore run and no purge is busy; the latest check of this process did not fail (a check that fails, such as an index held back to hide a revocation, stops automatic installs until one succeeds: §13), and the last good check is at most 6 h 40 min old and its index not past `expires_at` (the rule that remains after a restart); and **no run to that release was made yet**. A run that failed or was reverted is not tried again automatically (the page shows its error; an administrator can press Update, or a newer release is offered), and a run that ended `done` while the box still runs the older version is not repeated. A rollback makes the mode manual (D-340 (4)); an administrator who turns automatic back on accepts the release again. (3) The "waves" of the page's hint are the rollout cohort of §6: no new rule. | Each automatic run restarts every service and core, takes a snapshot and may put the database back, so a retry loop every 10 minutes is worse than waiting for a person; checks stay at the §12 rate (no extra request to install). Sources: Fedora CoreOS Zincati checks every 5 min with jitter, updates only inside its "periodic" maintenance windows, and abandons a target after `MAX_DEPLOY_ATTEMPTS = 12` failed deploys in a row (https://coreos.github.io/zincati/usage/updates-strategy/ , https://github.com/coreos/zincati/blob/main/src/update_agent/mod.rs); its deploy attempt is a cheap staging step before reboot, ours is the whole run, hence one try. TUF freeze attack: a client must not act on metadata past its expiry (https://theupdateframework.github.io/specification/latest/). Not chosen: retry a failed release every window (repeats a revert and a core restart every day); install from any stored offer whatever its age (a held-back index would hide a revocation); a check at every process start (a restart loop would hammer GitHub, §12). | 2026-11-12 |
| D-389 | **Auth after the real-user walk of 2026-11-12 (S-CORE-3): the sole administrator gets back in from the box console, not with recovery codes; guessable passwords are refused; one wording and one date format.** (1) **`vedette reset-admin <email>`** on the box console (`docker exec vedette-core /vedette reset-admin <email>`; appliance `sudo podman exec ...`), next to the serving process (SQLite WAL takes the second writer; every account fact core checks is read from the database, only the sign-in failure counters stay in its memory, so a running wait of at most 10 min stays): for an active password administrator only, one transaction sets a temporary password (72 h, replaced at sign-in, D-180), turns two-step sign-in off, ends every session, audits `user.console_reset` (actor `console`). It never creates a database (a wrong `-db` is refused). My account shows the command (the email single-quoted for the shell) to administrators while two-step sign-in is on; others are told to ask an administrator. **No recovery codes** in v1: they cover a lost phone but not a forgotten password, need storage, a show-once screen, regeneration and a second sign-in path, while whoever holds the console already holds the database and its key. (2) **Guessable passwords** (setup, password change, the new password after a temporary one) are 400 `weak_password`: a common stem with digits/symbols around or inside it or repeated (`password1234`, `Qwerty123456!`, `P@$$word2024`, product name), 3 or fewer distinct characters, a straight run of digits/alphabet/keyboard alone or with a few other characters (`1234567890!!`, `qwertyuiop2024`), or the letters of the email's name. A hand-kept list of ~30 stems, not a leaked-password corpus (no third-party data, no notice); upgrade path: an embedded NCSC/SecLists top list filtered to 12+ characters. (3) The **login throttle is unchanged**: the walk's script sent 9 wrong passwords for the account (1 + 8, `p5.mjs`), below the limit of 10, so the right one signed in as designed; a test over HTTP now pins 9 → 200 and 10 → 429 with "Try again in 30 seconds." and `Retry-After`, the sign-in page shows that sentence, and the mock throttles too. (4) One term "two-step sign-in" in every message; every date in the app is "12 Nov 2026" / "12 Nov 2026, 20:51" (`lib/format`, as Home and feeds already wrote it); the sessions table shows "Browser on OS" with the raw User-Agent as tooltip. | Self-hosted products put the lost-admin path on the console: Grafana `grafana cli admin reset-admin-password` (https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/cli/), Home Assistant `auth reset` / `hass --script auth change_password` in the container (https://www.home-assistant.io/docs/locked_out/), pfSense console option 3 resets the admin password and re-enables the account (https://docs.netgate.com/pfsense/en/latest/troubleshooting/locked-out.html), GitLab disables an admin's 2FA from the Rails console or `gitlab-rake gitlab:two_factor:disable_for_all_users` (https://docs.gitlab.com/security/two_factor_authentication/); recovery codes are the SaaS answer where the user has no console (GitHub https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/securing-your-account-with-two-factor-authentication-2fa/configuring-two-factor-authentication-recovery-methods). NIST SP 800-63B 5.1.1.2: compare new passwords against commonly used values, repetitive or sequential characters and context-specific words (https://pages.nist.gov/800-63-3/sp800-63b.html). Findings: `vedette-wt/findings-inbox.md` G6. | 2026-11-12 |

Danh mục trigger và mẫu quy tắc được kiểm lúc nạp: trường số thiếu khoảng hay mẫu vi phạm thì hộp không khởi động (fail closed). "At least/at most" và khoảng chỉ nhận số thập phân thường (không khoảng trắng, hex, mũ, NaN/Inf), giống nhau ở hộp, mock và form. (2) **Xoá quy tắc** mở hộp thoại "Delete rule <tên>?" như Connections/Devices; bật/tắt quy tắc báo "Rule <tên> is on/off"; clone báo như cũ. Elastic Security giới hạn risk score 0–100 và từ chối ngoài khoảng ngay trong form ([rules UI](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/security/current/rules-ui-create.html)); Grafana Alerting và GitHub (xoá ruleset/webhook) đều hỏi xác nhận trước khi xoá ([Grafana alert rules](https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/alerting/alerting-rules/), [GitHub rulesets](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-rulesets/managing-rulesets-for-a-repository#deleting-a-ruleset)); lỗi đặt dưới ô có lỗi theo GOV.UK Design System và GitHub Primer ([error message](https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/error-message/), [Primer forms](https://primer.style/ui-patterns/forms)). | D-391 | **Core GUI walk 3 (G12): the SSH allow-list refuses shell characters at save, the user-name pattern says its rule, the box's own certificate refusal is logged once per 10 minutes with a count, the Updates page of a container-only install always shows the running version and the last read of update information, tab strips and filter chips wrap on a phone (S-CORE-2, S-RESP-4, S-CORE-9).** (1) **SSH allow-list**: `core/conn` `checkAllow` refuses `cliban.ShellChars` (`; \| & $ ` < > ( ) \ ! ~ ^`, one copy now in `core/conn/cliban`, used by the reader and the writer too) in an SSH entry with `invalid_allow`; the entry could never run (both refuse these characters on every line) and the HTTP list already refuses them. A command such as `show run \| include ospf` is therefore not allowed; a router pipe needs a different design (deferred, not wanted for v1). (2) **User name**: a value the contract pattern refuses never reached the handler, so the user saw "The field \"username\" is missing or has a value that is not allowed"; `core/server` `fieldRule` gives the same sentence the handler uses. (3) **Log noise**: one browser that does not trust the self-signed certificate wrote 1,662 WARN lines an hour; `cmd/vedette/tlsnoise.go` writes the first `tls: unknown certificate` handshake error, then one per 10 minutes with "and N more"; every other handshake error stays a WARN. Not DEBUG: an operator who wonders why a browser cannot connect still sees the first line. (4) **Updates**: no failed-check field exists in `UpdatesState`, so "never read" carries the cause in words; a real "failed" state needs an API field (deferred). (5) **Phone**: `Segmented` and the Settings tab strip wrap instead of scrolling with no cue; wrapping needs no cue, and nothing is clipped. No outside product was consulted: each change follows a rule the repo already has (the reader and writer shell-character ban, the handler messages, the D-422 style of one honest line). Sources: none. | 2026-11-12 |
| D-392 | **A failed software update check is kept and shown (S-CORE-2; update-manifest §12, §13; D-388).** (1) `UpdatesState.last_check_error` `{at, code, message}` or null: `code` is `update_source_unreachable` or `update_check_failed`, `message` is the box's own fixed sentence for that failure (the message of the 503/502 answer of `POST /core/updates/check`); text received from the network never reaches it (it is only logged). (2) It is stored in `core_setting` `core_updates` after every check that fails with one of those codes (page or periodic job), cleared in the same write that moves `last_check` after a whole good check, kept by a change of channel or mode and by a rollback, and left as it was by a cancelled request. (3) The Updates page of both install kinds shows "Last check failed <when>: <reason>" under the last good check; a container-only box that never had a good check stops guessing the cause. (4) The automatic mode installs nothing while it is set, also after core restarts (before: only an in-memory flag, so a restart forgot the failure and only the 6 h 40 min age rule remained). | A check that silently fails looks like "up to date": the administrator must see that the box is blind, and why, without reading the core log. Sources: Fedora CoreOS Zincati reports every failed Cincinnati update check by a fixed error kind, not by the remote text (`zincati_cincinnati_update_checks_errors_total{kind}`, https://github.com/coreos/zincati/blob/main/src/cincinnati/mod.rs), and its updates strategy keeps checking on its own schedule (https://coreos.github.io/zincati/usage/updates-strategy/); our two codes play the role of its kinds. Not chosen: show the raw transport error (could carry text from a hostile network into the GUI, rules/security.md); keep it only in memory (a restart, which core's own update causes, would hide it and re-allow automatic installs on an offer from before the failure). | 2026-11-12 |
| D-393 | **Container-only: the admin chooses the card the passive sensor listens on among the cards it reported, addressed or not, and SPAN is a separate tick; `Sensor.chosen` tells a choice from the default (S-CORE-8 G6, S-INV-1; extends D-387, keeps D-380, D-263, D-385).** (1) **Problem**: a container-only box with two cards that have an address (no SPAN card) gets no default (D-380: two candidates is not a clear answer), so the sensor listened on no card and the Configure dialog (D-387) offered only a SPAN card: no discovery at all. (2) **What**: Devices → Scope and sensors → Configure on a container-only install has one list **Listen on**: "Automatic" (the D-380 default: with the card it gives now while nothing is chosen, "no card now" when it gives none, and a plain description of the rule once a card is chosen, since the default is not computed then) and every card of the fresh heartbeat (D-385, < 90 s), with or without an address; then a tick **SPAN port** (the card receives the switch's mirrored traffic), offered once a card is chosen and cleared when another card is picked. Save sends `PATCH /inventory/sensors/{id}` `{interface, span}`, which already took a non-SPAN card (INV-9); a SPAN tick on a card with an IPv4 address is still refused (`bad_interface`). "Automatic" saves `interface: null` and the default rule applies again. (3) **`chosen`**: `GET /inventory/sensors` gains `chosen: boolean`, true exactly when `sp_sensor.interface` holds a card (the admin's choice here, or the SPAN port of Box network on an appliance), false when `interface` is the computed default (or null). The dialog starts from it (a choice shows as that card, the default as "Automatic"), so the D-380 default is overridden only by an explicit choice and never saved by accident. A chosen card missing from the last heartbeat stays in the list ("not reported now") so it can be changed. (4) **Appliance unchanged**: the dialog stays read-only with the link to Box network (D-56, D-118). (5) **Names only, no addresses in the list** (ponytail): the GUI shows the card names the sensor reported, and the hint says to run `ip -br address` on the machine to see which card is which. (6) **Links that are not cards are never a card here, on core's side too** (defence in depth, SYS-6): the sensor already leaves loopback, container bridges (`docker0`, `br-…`, `podman0`), veth and VPN links out of its heartbeat (`cmd/vedette-sensor` `osInterfaces`), so the "two cards" of the field report are two real cards, which (2) covers. But the heartbeat is untrusted (an older or compromised sensor could list them), and now that any reported card can be chosen, core applies the same rule: one `sensorlink.VirtualIfaceName` (moved from `virtualName` in `modules/core` and `cmd/vedette-sensor`; loopback, veth, podman, cni, docker, br, virbr, bond, tun, tap, wg, …, `vedette0`, VLAN `.`/`@`) keeps those links out of the default, out of `Sensor.interfaces`, and out of `SetInterface` without a host (`bad_interface`: "not a network card"). Known limit (unchanged by this): a machine whose address sits on a bridge or bond (`br0`, `bond0`) has no listed addressed card; the admin chooses the physical port under it, without SPAN. | Top-tier: Security Onion's setup has the admin pick the management NIC and then the monitor NIC(s) explicitly from the list of NICs, never a guess (https://docs.securityonion.net/en/2.4/first-time-users.html, https://securityonion.readthedocs.io/en/2.4/vmware.html); Zeek is told its card in `node.cfg` (`interface=eth0`) (https://docs.zeek.org/en/master/quickstart.html); ntopng takes `-i <card>` and, without it, listens on the first card of the system, which OPNsense's guide warns may be the wrong one (https://www.ntop.org/guides/ntopng/cli_options/cli_options.html, https://docs.opnsense.org/manual/how-tos/ntopng.html). Chosen: an explicit choice among the real cards (Security Onion, Zeek), with the D-380 default kept for the clear one-card case; not ntopng's "first card" guess (the wrong LAN gives a wrong inventory). Not chosen: listing card addresses in the API (more contract for a hint `ip -br address` gives); a separate "monitor" role list (one sensor, one card, D-24). | 2026-11-12 |
| D-395 | **MCP server reachable on the machine's own 127.0.0.1 on both install kinds: in the container it listens on the unspecified address of the container's own network, and the unit publishes `127.0.0.1:8765` only (mcp-server, S-MCP-1, S-CORE-9; replaces D-234 (3) and the MCP part of D-420 (4); closes `.ai/deferred/feat-mcp-server.md:3`, v1-readiness T9).** (1) **Why it did not work**: core listened on `127.0.0.1:8765` of its container and nothing published 8765. A publish cannot fix that alone: Podman (netavark, rootful and rootless) and Docker forward a published port to the container's own address, never to its loopback. Checked on the Mac's Podman 5 (rootful and rootless, `distroless/static-debian13` read-only, uid 65532): a listener on `127.0.0.1:8765` behind `-p 127.0.0.1:18766:8765` answered nothing (reset / empty reply); a listener on `0.0.0.0:8765` behind `-p 127.0.0.1:18765:8765` answered, and `/run/.containerenv` was present. (2) **What ships**: the core Quadlet unit gets `PublishPort=127.0.0.1:8765:8765` (template change with its legacy entry `core-3`, so boxes migrate at the next core restart, D-316 (10)); `deploy/compose/container-only/compose.yaml` gets `127.0.0.1:8765:8765`. Neither passes `-mcp-listen`: its default (empty) is `0.0.0.0:8765` in a container and `127.0.0.1:8765` elsewhere. Passing the flag was the first draft; the Opus review found that a core image from before this decision refuses `0.0.0.0` and exits, so a migrated unit started on the old image (a reboot or crash before the image step, a rollback rendering the current template with the previous digest, a compose file newer than its image) would have taken 8443 down with it. With the default, an older image under the new unit simply leaves MCP unreachable, as before. Same pattern as the sensor link 8444 (D-113, D-147 (5)). Never a LAN address: both files and their tests (`host/ops` golden units, `deploy/compose/compose_test.go`) pin the `127.0.0.1` host side; core's network stays its own bridge (no host network, which the compose test already enforces). (3) **INV-5 keeps its guard**: an explicit `-mcp-listen` and `mcpserver.New` still refuse every address off loopback, with one exception: the unspecified address (`0.0.0.0`, `[::]`) when the process runs in a container (cmd/vedette sees Podman's `/run/.containerenv` or Docker's `/.dockerenv`; `Config.InContainer`). A named address (a LAN or container IP) is always refused; on a machine without a container the unspecified address is refused, so a bare binary never opens MCP to the LAN. Known limit: a container on the host network (an operator's `network_mode: host`, a toolbox/distrobox) has the marker, so its default is the host's 0.0.0.0, still behind the token; no shipped file does that (compose test, golden units), and the sensor link 8444 has the same property. The dev compose (`deploy/compose/compose.yaml`, bridge, 8765 not published) also defaults to 0.0.0.0 inside its container: only the other dev containers reach it, behind the token. `GET /core/mcp` reports `127.0.0.1:<port>` and `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp` (the host side of the publish, same port), never `0.0.0.0`. (4) **Who else can reach it**: the host itself (as on loopback) and peers on the container network (Vedette's own containers on `vedette-int` / the compose network), always behind the bearer token, the Origin refusal and the rate limits (D-230..D-232); the class "a container on the machine reaches unpublished Vedette ports" is T10's (`fix-docker-forward-drop.md:12`). Docker ≥ 28 drops direct-routed packets to ports published on loopback (INSTALL-CONTAINER already names Docker < 28). (5) **Port held on the host**: the runtime reserves `127.0.0.1:8765` while core runs, whether the module is on or off (off: a connection is refused or reset, POST-1 holds inside the container); a program already on 8765 would stop core starting, so `install.sh` preflight now checks 8443, 8444 **and 8765**, README names it. A box upgraded in place is not re-checked (accepted: the appliance is a dedicated machine, install.sh refuses one with other services). (6) **Page text** (Mlee's mcp-server feature, minimal edit): the appliance text was already true ("this machine only", SSH tunnel or reverse proxy); the container-only text now says the port is on 127.0.0.1 of the machine that runs Docker or Podman, never on the LAN, another machine uses an SSH tunnel to that machine, and an older `compose.yaml` must be updated; INSTALL-CONTAINER section 5 says a release may change the compose files and how to check them. Not chosen: **MCP through the 8443 listener at `/mcp`** (Home Assistant serves `/api/mcp` on its main port with OAuth; GitLab likewise) — it opens MCP to the LAN, against D-234 (2) and the MCP transport's advice to bind local servers to localhost, a product-direction change for kien; **host network for core** (exposes every core listener, 8444 and the syslog ports, on the host's interfaces and drops the container isolation of D-55); **a proxy on the host** (systemd-socket-proxyd or socat into the container namespace: another unit and process for one port); **a flag instead of container detection** (would also open the LAN on a bare binary). Sources: Docker port publishing (a port published on `127.0.0.1` is reachable only from the Docker host; direct routing to unpublished or loopback-published ports blocked from 28.0) https://docs.docker.com/engine/network/port-publishing/ ; Podman Quadlet `PublishPort=` https://docs.podman.io/en/latest/markdown/podman-systemd.unit.5.html ; MCP Streamable HTTP, Security warning (bind local servers to localhost, authenticate) https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports/streamable-http ; Home Assistant MCP Server (served on the main port at `/api/mcp`, OAuth) https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/mcp_server/ ; mcp-grafana (container listens on all addresses, the operator chooses the publish) https://github.com/grafana/mcp-grafana . | 2026-11-13 |
| D-396 | **Docker coexistence, two fixes to the DOCKER-USER rules of D-267 (`host/ops/dockerfwd.go`). (a) The bridges of the box itself:** the `-i vedette0 -o br-+ -j RETURN` of D-267 also matched a bridge of the box named `br-…` (an uplink `br-lan`, `br-ex`): those packets went on to Docker's chains, nothing accepted them, and the containers silently lost the internet. iptables matches an interface only exactly or by a `+` prefix, so Docker's own bridges (`br-` + the first 12 hex digits of the network ID) cannot be matched by a pattern. Decision: keep `br-+` (it covers a Docker network from the moment Docker makes it) and add above the RETURNs one `-s <subnet> -i vedette0 -o <name> -m comment --comment vedette-int -j ACCEPT` for every bridge in `/sys/class/net` named `br-` + 1–12 of `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]`, not of Docker's form (`^br-[0-9a-f]{12}$`), that holds a port which is not a container's veth: a network card (`<port>/device`), a bond (`<port>/bonding`) or a link on top of another (`<port>/lower_*`: a VLAN); Docker's bridges, custom-named ones too (`com.docker.network.bridge.name: br-app`), hold only veths and stay behind `br-+` (review r2 M1); no `+` or `!` ever reaches a rule; at most 32 (past that nothing is changed, one log line). Fail closed: a new uplink bridge has no internet for at most one look (30 s); a new Docker network is never open to Vedette's containers. The host still only checks (`-C`) and inserts (`-I`), never deletes: the ACCEPT of a bridge that is gone matches nothing and `install.sh --uninstall` removes it (its pattern already covers it). **(b) Customer containers to Vedette's unpublished ports: block.** Docker's own accept for traffic leaving its bridges let a customer's Docker container open any port of a Vedette container on `vedette-int` (not only the published 8443, 514, 6514). Decision: a last rule `! -i vedette0 -o vedette0 -m comment --comment vedette-int -j DROP`, below the conntrack `DNAT,ESTABLISHED,RELATED` ACCEPT, so published ports through the box's address and replies still pass; traffic inside `vedette0` (`br_netfilter`) is excluded by `! -i`. It mirrors Docker 28's own default for its networks (a port that is not published is not reachable from outside the network). It changes the outcome only for packets Docker (or a later FORWARD rule) would have accepted; an administrator who wants a direct route puts an ACCEPT above our block, as for every other rule of ours. Also: inserts are refused (state `unexpected`, logged once) when a rule of someone else stands inside our block, since positions are counted inside the block and a DROP above the ACCEPT of replies would cut the GUI (review M2). Order kept: ACCEPTs of the box's bridges, `docker0` RETURN, `br-+` RETURN, conntrack ACCEPT, outbound ACCEPT, DROP. Not covered: a Docker network with a custom bridge name that does not start with `br-` is not protected from Vedette's containers (deferred N2); a bridge of the box named `br-…` whose ports are only taps or veths (a VM bridge) is treated like Docker's (no ACCEPT); IPv6 (`vedette-int` has none); a box without Docker (no FORWARD drop; netavark's own isolation, deferred). Rejected: one RETURN per Docker bridge read from `/sys/class/net` (first draft: a Docker network made by compose is open to Vedette's containers until the next look, and every network churns a rule and a delete; review M1), reading Docker's internal chains (`DOCKER-ISOLATION-STAGE-*` are gone from Docker 28's documented chains), calling the Docker CLI or socket (root-equivalent access the host does not need), documenting instead of blocking (Docker itself blocks the same flow for its own containers since 28.0). | Sources: Docker, [Packet filtering and firewalls](https://docs.docker.com/engine/network/packet-filtering-firewalls/) and [Docker with iptables](https://docs.docker.com/engine/network/firewall-iptables/) (DOCKER-USER is the chain for the administrator; rules match interfaces; firewalld zone `docker` lists every Docker bridge by name); Docker, [Engine v28: hardening container networking by default](https://www.docker.com/blog/docker-engine-28-hardening-container-networking-by-default/) (unpublished ports dropped from outside the network); Docker, [Bridge network driver](https://docs.docker.com/engine/network/drivers/bridge/) (containers on different bridge networks only through published ports; `com.docker.network.bridge.name`); moby, [bridge driver](https://github.com/moby/moby/blob/master/daemon/libnetwork/drivers/bridge/bridge_linux.go) (`"br-" + id[:12]`). | 2026-11-13 |
| D-397 | **The box's own TLS certificate follows `-hosts` (`VEDETTE_HOSTS`) at start.** At every start of core, when the box's own self-signed leaf (organization `Vedette (self-signed)`) lacks an entry of `-hosts` or the box's name (a DNS name compared without case, an address by value; the container's own addresses of `localNames` do not count), core issues a new leaf for the same key, **from the same box CA**, that keeps every name and address the old leaf had and adds the missing ones, and logs `the self-signed certificate was re-issued for the names of -hosts or the box name it did not cover` with them. On a container-only install a name dropped from `-hosts` stays in the certificate but gets 421 (the Host allowlist is `-hosts`); on an appliance the address-driven re-issue of `selfSignedRenewer.Check` (D-139) may drop it again, which is equally harmless. A certificate the owner supplies (`-tls-cert`, or another organization in the box's files) is never touched. Like the upgrade under the CA (D-262), it is optional: a CA that cannot be read or a directory that cannot be written keeps the leaf in use, with a warning. `cmd/vedette/tls.go` `reissueSelfSigned`, `uncoveredHosts`; `TestEnsureCertReissuesForANewHostsEntry`. | Mac walk 4 (2026-11-13): INSTALL-CONTAINER §2 says to change `VEDETTE_HOSTS` and run `up -d`; the new name then passed the Host check but its TLS failed (curl "no alternative certificate subject name matches") and so did the pinned osquery installer, since the leaf kept the names of the first start. The CA stays so that agents pinned to it (D-262, agent-intake) keep working. Sources: Caddy's internal issuer keeps its local root and issues a leaf for each name it is asked to serve (https://caddyserver.com/docs/automatic-https#local-https); kubeadm adds SANs to the API server by issuing a new serving certificate from the same cluster CA (https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/administer-cluster/kubeadm/kubeadm-reconfigure/). Not chosen: a doc line "delete the certificate in the volume" (a hand step the next owner forgets; a new key would also break nothing but is not needed); a new CA (every enrolled agent would need its install command again); dropping removed names (a bookmark would break for no gain: the allowlist already refuses them). | 2026-11-13 |
| D-398 | **The first update check of a box that never checked runs within minutes, and the page never guesses why none ran.** (1) A box with no stored check at all (`last_check` and `last_check_error` both null) is due 2 minutes after its core process started (`firstCheckAfter`), and the `core/software-update` job is woken then (`OSConfig.Wake` → `jobs.Scheduler.Wake`); a fresh box, whose setup comes after start, checks at the first tick after setup (within 10 minutes). A box that has a stored check keeps D-388: 6 h ± 30 min after `last_check`, never at the first tick (a box whose checks have only failed has no `last_check`, so, as before this decision, it checks one tick after each start). Off under Privacy or before setup: nothing, as before. Each check logs its result (`core: update check`, or the warning or error of the failure). (2) Settings → Updates on a container-only install says "No check has run yet." and "No release information yet: no update check has run on this install. Vedette checks a few minutes after setup or a restart, then every 6 hours." when both are null, instead of "has never been read … the box cannot reach github.com"; a failed check still says its own reason (D-392). | Mac walk 4 (2026-11-13): 20+ minutes after the first start of a container-only box, with `up -d` restarts in between (each one pushed the first check one tick further), `/core/updates` had no check and the page blamed github.com, whose cause was not in the log because nothing was tried. Sources: update agents check soon after they start and then on their interval with jitter, Fedora CoreOS Zincati (https://coreos.github.io/zincati/usage/updates-strategy/, as in D-388); a status line should report what happened, not a guessed cause (D-392). Restart loops: a never-checked box makes at most one request per process that lives 2 minutes, and from its first stored check on the D-388 rule holds (§12 rate kept). Not chosen: checking at the first tick of every process (a restart loop would hammer GitHub, D-388); a shorter job tick (10 min stays; the wake is one timer per process). | 2026-11-13 |
| D-399 | **Agent intake and the passive sensor after real-user walk 4 (S-INV-4, S-INV-1, S-CORE-8 G6).** (1) **osquery for arm64 Linux servers is served, not just stated as a limit**: the core image ships the official osquery 5.12.1 `osquery_5.12.1-1.linux_arm64.deb` and `osquery-5.12.1-1.linux.aarch64.rpm` next to the three x86_64/Windows files, pinned in `deploy/osquery/PINS` the same way (SHA-256 of the GitHub release file, the same hash from pkg.osquery.io, checked by the core build), served by the mirror (six fixed names) and listed in `SHA256SUMS`; the Linux script picks the package from `dpkg --print-architecture` (the userland, so a 32-bit system on a 64-bit kernel is refused, not handed a package dpkg rejects), else `uname -m`; other architectures are refused with a sentence. Cost: +57 MB on the core image (osquery layer 80 → 137 MB); accepted because Graviton, Ampere and Raspberry Pi servers are common in the target SMBs and the alternative (a text "x86_64 only") leaves them with no agent. Windows stays x64 MSI only. (2) **No script pinned to a placeholder**: when the box knows no address other machines can reach (opened as localhost/127.0.0.1, no configured address), `GET /install/osquery.sh` and `.ps1` answer 404 `no_box_address` instead of a script whose `BOX=` is `<VEDETTE_BOX_IP>` (it passed its SHA-256 check and then failed on every server); `GET /inventory/agents` keeps the placeholder in `server_url` (PRE-3, never a guess) and the GUI shows, instead of the commands, how to give the box an address (container-only: `VEDETTE_BIND_IP` + `VEDETTE_HOSTS`; appliance: open it at its network address). The token row counts "Machines enrolled" (it never meant reporting). (3) **The passive heartbeat says why the capture does not run**: `capture_error` ∈ {`no_permission` (EPERM/EACCES: no `CAP_NET_RAW`, a rootless container), `no_interface`, `filters_invalid`, `capture_failed`}, set by the sensor when an open or a session fails and cleared when the card opens or no card is wanted; never the error text (it stays in the sensor's log). Core decodes it strictly (a lower-case word ≤ 48 bytes, else 400), shows an unknown word as `capture_failed` (logged once; at most 64 unknown names remembered), keeps it in memory with the last heartbeat and returns it in `GET /inventory/sensors` only while the sensor is online; the GUI shows "Reporting, not capturing" and the reason. Strict decoding means a new field is a new protocol: `X-Vedette-Proto` 3 → 4 (sensor, scan worker and core ship together). (4) Sensors → Configure: the SPAN tick says why it is off under Automatic, and a refused save (400 `bad_interface`) is shown under the field it is about with `aria-invalid`; other answers stay under the form. | Top-tier: osquery publishes aarch64 Linux packages (https://github.com/osquery/osquery/releases/tag/5.12.1), Fleet builds fleetd for Linux arm64 (`fleetctl package --arch=arm64`, https://fleetdm.com/guides/enroll-hosts), Wazuh ships aarch64 agents (https://documentation.wazuh.com/current/installation-guide/wazuh-agent/wazuh-agent-package-linux.html): an agent server that serves only x86_64 is the exception. | D-401 | **WP-08k part B, `make release-gates` (step 3 of D-457): one target that stops a release before anything is signed or pushed when an artifact is not the one the release is about to name.** In order, failing at the first: (0) `release gates -preflight`: VERSION is SemVer and not `-test.`, the tree is clean and HEAD is tag `v<v>` (`checkReleaseTree`, the check of `release-push`); (1) `make vuln-scan` (the `.trivyignore.yaml` reasons and dates first, then trivy on every platform of the four lists tagged `<v>` and on the source) and `make sbom`, both with `RELEASE=1` so `dist/vuln` and `dist/sbom` stay for part C (`supply-chain.sh` now replaces and removes only the output of its own mode: before, `vuln-scan` after `sbom` deleted the SBOMs); (2) `make notices-check`; (3) `release gates`: `check-binaries -release` on the `vedette-host` **read out of each `.deb`** (ar → `data.tar.gz`, stdlib only; any other compression is refused, nfpm.yaml says gzip), not on the loose binary `host-deb` leaves in `dist/host-deb`; the `org.opencontainers.image.version` label of every platform of the four local lists equals `<v>` (the `localPlatforms` reader of `release-push`); (4) **the floor**: core's new label `io.github.knt048.vedette.min-sequence` (set in the final stage from the same `MIN_SEQUENCE` build argument as the `-X` of `/vedette`) must equal the release floor, and **each `.deb` is built again** by `make host-deb VERSION=<v> ARCH=<arch> MIN_SEQUENCE=<floor> DEB_OUT=<temp>` and must be **byte-identical** to the shipped one; the floor is `MIN_SEQUENCE`, which make computes from `RELEASE_PREV_INDEX` with the verifying `release min-sequence` (or `MIN_SEQUENCE=0`, given by hand, for the very first release only, the rule of `host-deb`); because make lets a `MIN_SEQUENCE` from the environment or the command line win over the index, `release gates` (already in `-preflight`, before the scans) verifies `-prev-index` itself and refuses a floor that is not its sequence, and refuses any floor but 0 without an index. The message on a mismatch names the commit of each `vedette-host` when they differ. Closes the two lines of `.ai/deferred/fix-release-preflight.md` at step 3 (the floor compiled into the `.deb` was never compared with `<prev>`; nothing checked what is inside the `.deb`); the gate keeps no record, so a rebuild between step 3 and `release-push`/`release-in` is not caught (deferred line, the same-session rule of the plan holds meanwhile). | **Why rebuild and compare instead of reading the floor**: `MinSequenceText` is a `-X` string in a stripped binary (`-s -w`), and Go records `-ldflags` in the build info only without `-trimpath` (go.dev/issue/52372), so nothing in the binary says which floor it holds; a side file written by `host-deb` would only be another claim. The package is reproducible by design (SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH = commit time, `-trimpath`, nfpm gzip): measured on this Mac 2026-11-13, two `make host-deb VERSION=1.2.3-test.1 ARCH=arm64` builds are byte-identical and the same build with `MIN_SEQUENCE=5` differs (and so, since Go records `vcs.revision`, does one from another commit). Equal bytes prove the binary is this commit, this version and this floor at once, the way reproducible-builds verification works (https://reproducible-builds.org/docs/definition/, Go: https://go.dev/blog/rebuild "Perfectly Reproducible, Verified Go Toolchains"); it costs two cross builds (under a minute each). **Why a label for core**: the core image is built in a container with the embedded web interface, so a rebuild on the maintainer's machine would not reproduce it; the label comes from the same build argument in the same build as the version label the plan already trusts, and custom labels use a reverse-DNS prefix (OCI image spec annotations, https://github.com/opencontainers/image-spec/blob/main/annotations.md). **Order**: the one given for part B (scans first); only the cheap version and tree check runs before them, so a wrong tag does not cost a 1.7 GB trivy run. Line breaks in the description become spaces before the printable check (Cisco writes several lines). The OS observation of the passive sensor is capped at 0.5, the confidence of the description. The device name stays LLDP sysName (0.7) when the switch sends one. (2) **Source of a device seen only by ARP**: the list's `summary` falls back to the current hostname and MAC observations when there is no vendor, model or OS, so "Unknown 192.168.18.1" says Passive instead of "–".
