| D-413 | **How we work now (kien, 2026-11-13 14:10): build + lint locally, changed packages on PR CI, full suite on main and nightly, no merge queue, flaky non-customer tests deleted, "done" = the customer journey passes on the real box.** Replaces the local-check part of D-370/D-373/D-376 and the merge queue of D-245. (1) **Local**: before pushing an agent only builds and lints what it changed (`gofmt -l`, `go build ./...`, `go vet` + golangci-lint `--new-from-rev` of the changed packages, `make generate-check` when contracts/migrations/queries change; `tsc -b` + `pnpm lint` for web); it may run the one test it wrote or fixed. `make check-fast`, `make check` and `make verify` stay, only to reproduce a red CI. (2) **CI**: on a pull request go-static (build, vet, generated code), go-lint and govulncheck stay whole-repo (cached), go-test runs only the packages holding a changed file plus their direct importers (`make test-go-shard CHANGED_BASE=HEAD^1`, `scripts/ci` `Affected`; a Go-side path outside every package, such as `go.mod`, the Makefile, `scripts/`, or a doc or web file a Go test reads, runs every package), web-verify runs `make verify-web-pr` (tsc, lint, `vitest run --changed HEAD^1`, openapi drift, no build; every test when a non-`web/` file the web tests read changed, `webtests=all`). A push to main and the daily schedule run the full suite (Go and web, build included); -race and the skip list stay daily only (D-376). `go` and `web` stay the required checks, reporting on every PR; the `merge_group` trigger is removed. (3) **Flaky tests**: flaky and not checking a customer-visible outcome → deleted, not quarantined; otherwise quarantined in `scripts/ci/skip-tests.txt` as before. (4) **Done** = the customer journey passes on the real box (the project's N100 test box), by the method of `docs/QA.md` §5 "Kiểm như khách" (added here): real box, real integrations with test accounts, a walker without repo or spec, journeys from the product concept per module, outcomes recorded rather than screens, health sweep, scale pass, every release candidate. (5) **Merge**: no merge queue; the supervisor merges a PR with green CI by `gh pr merge <n> --squash`; if main goes red after a merge the supervisor reverts or fixes at once. The supervisor removes the merge-queue ruleset on GitHub after this PR merges. | kien's beta hour found ~26 problems the AI tests missed while agents spent their time on local suites and queue waits: test time went to screens and fakes, not to customer outcomes. Speed of the loop moves to CI (free, parallel), and the full suite still guards main on every merge and nightly, so a gap in the PR selection (a test reading another package's files) shows on main within one run and is reverted. Top-tier practice: presubmit runs the affected tests, postsubmit/continuous runs everything (Google TAP, https://testing.googleblog.com/2016/05/flaky-tests-at-google-and-how-we.html ); a merge queue is for high-traffic repositories where PRs collide (GitHub docs, https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/configuring-pull-request-merges/managing-a-merge-queue ), not a two-person project with one merge captain; a flaky test that guards nothing a user sees costs more than it protects (same Google post: flaky tests are retried, quarantined or removed). Not chosen: keeping `make check-fast` mandatory (minutes per push on a shared Mac, duplicated by CI); running every package on PRs (the test cache already skips unchanged ones, but a change in `core/` re-runs nearly everything). | 2026-11-13 |
| D-414 | **Telegram approvers link their Telegram account by a one-time confirm link opened while signed in to Vedette as themselves; the 2FA setup screen guides Google Authenticator.** kien (beta, 2026-11-13) found the old Telegram link confusing: My account showed "Telegram … Not linked" with a code field and a red "The code is 6 digits" before anything was typed, and the code came only after pressing a button on an approval message. (1) **One mechanism for every chat channel**: Telegram joins Zalo personal in `response`'s confirm-link list (`sendLink`, D-447): when an administrator saves a Telegram approver (or presses **Send again**), notify asks `response.ChatLinkToken` for a token (128 random bits after an 8-hex hint of the person; single use, 10 minutes, hashed with (person, channel, Telegram user ID), one a minute and five an hour per person) and the bot sends ONE message: "<name>: open this link to link your Telegram account to Vedette … <box base URL>/link/telegram?c=<token>". It goes **only privately** to the approver's Telegram user ID, so that only that account receives it: the token never goes into a shared chat (independent review: a link posted in the group would let a Vedette user confirm an ID an administrator mistyped, which is the very mistake the old private code caught). A bot cannot write first to someone who never wrote to it (Telegram 403, or 400 "chat not found"): then the approval chat gets a note WITHOUT the link, addressed to the person by name (an email is masked), asking them to open a private chat with the bot and press Start, then press Send again (My account or the channel dialog); the undelivered token is dropped and Send again answers 502 `send_failed` saying why. The link is bound to the Vedette user: whoever opens it must sign in (normal sign-in with two-step), the page `/link/telegram` asks "Link Telegram account <ID> to your Vedette user <name>?" and only **Confirm** (POST + CSRF) links; another signed-in person is refused before the token is read (403 `other_account`, audit `response.identity_link_refused`), an expired or used link says so and how to get a new one. Opening the page never links; no administrator can link anyone (INV-24). The press-for-a-private-code path of D-191/D-243 is removed (`chat_code` gone), so a press from an unlinked Telegram ID now answers "open the link Vedette sent … or ask your administrator to send it again". The links use notify's `BaseURL` (the box's management address, cmd/vedette `boxBaseURL`), never a hard-coded name; without it the send answers 503 `no_base_url`. (2) **Where the status lives**: the Telegram channel dialog shows each saved approver as Not linked / Sending / Waiting for <name> (sent hh:mm) / Linked, with **Send again**; My account shows the status and the same **Send again** (`POST /response/me/identities/{channel}/code` on a confirm-link channel asks notify to send a new link to the person's own listed ID, `Config.LinkSender`). Audit: `notify.telegram_link_code` per send (never the token), `notify.telegram_unlink` when a save removes or changes a linked approver (their proof is dropped, so naming the old ID again needs a new confirm), `response.identity_link` on confirm. Email approvers keep the mailed code. The code field in My account (email) keeps Confirm disabled until 6 digits are typed: no red error before typing. (3) **2FA setup guide**: under the QR, three steps recommending Google Authenticator (App Store and Google Play links; any TOTP app works): install, tap + then Scan a QR code, type the 6-digit code. No new data flow: Telegram `sendMessage` to `api.telegram.org` already exists for alerts and approvals (PRIVACY.md row unchanged); the store links are plain links the person opens. | Account linking in top-tier chat integrations is a link sent to the chat account that the person opens while signed in to the product: Slack apps' "Sign in to link your account" (https://api.slack.com/authentication/sign-in-with-slack, GitHub for Slack `/github signin` https://github.com/integrations/slack#authorization), PagerDuty user linking for Slack (https://support.pagerduty.com/main/docs/slack-user-guide#link-your-slack-and-pagerduty-accounts) and Telegram's own guidance for linking a bot user to a site account via a one-time token (https://core.telegram.org/bots/features#deep-linking). A code shown in the chat proves who holds the chat account but not which product user they are; the signed-in confirm proves both when the message reaches only that account, which is why the link goes only by private message (a Telegram bot cannot start a conversation with a user who never wrote to it, https://core.telegram.org/bots#how-are-bots-different-from-users, so the person presses Start once, as with every Telegram bot that links accounts). Google Authenticator first with store links follows GitHub's 2FA setup ("we recommend … Google Authenticator / Microsoft Authenticator", https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/securing-your-account-with-two-factor-authentication-2fa/configuring-two-factor-authentication) and Google's own steps (https://support.google.com/accounts/answer/1066447: tap +, Scan a QR code). | 2026-11-13 |
| D-416 | **The audit log is kept by time, not by a small row count; automatic lines stay but can be left out; devices and findings are shown by name** (supervisor, 2026-11-13, customer walk 1 W1-34; S-CORE-3, core INV-17, INV-37). (1) **Retention**: `core_audit` keeps the lines of the last **365 days, at most 200,000 lines**; the oldest run goes first. Before this, the screen said "The box keeps the latest 1000 lines" but the box kept everything forever (the 1,000 was the preview's browser-storage cap, `mocks/stores.ts`), so the trail had no bound on a real box and the screen told the customer something untrue. Core job `core/audit-prune` (every 6 h; `audit.Log.Prune`) deletes only a contiguous prefix, never the newest line, moves `core_chain_anchor` and lowers `core_chain_head` in the same transaction (`chainhead.Prune`), and writes one `audit.pruned` line by `system` ("N lines: older than 365 days (before …) or beyond the newest 200000"); the chain verifies after every prune. The append-only trigger stays: migration `0011` lets a delete through only for lines at or before the line the anchor names, so the prune must move the anchor first and nothing else can delete (the purge still drops the triggers for its wipe). 200,000 lines is about 80 MB at the size of today's lines and covers a year at the walk's day-one rate (≈330 lines/day) many times over; past it the oldest go even if younger than 365 days. **Clock guard** (Opus review): if the age cut would remove more than half of the lines in one run, it removes nothing by age (the count ceiling still applies) and the job reports `audit.ErrClockSuspect`, so a clock that jumps ahead (bad RTC, wrong manual time, spoofed NTP on the LAN) cannot erase the trail in one run; in steady use a run removes a tiny share. Not configurable (ponytail: nobody asked; the AI log's own `retention_days` is a different log). (2) **Automatic lines stay in the audit log**: "Finding created" and the other lines by `system`/`system:<part>` record what the box changed by itself and are kept (GitHub's audit log also records automated events such as Dependabot alerts); they are no longer what pushes people's lines out, because retention is by time. They can be hidden: `GET /core/audit` and `/core/audit/export` take `actor=people`, which leaves out `system` and `system:<part>` (a person, the console and an MCP token stay); the Who filter offers "Not the system (people and tools)". The default view still shows every line (nothing hidden by surprise). (3) **Names**: `GET /core/audit` returns `names` (id → display name) for the device (`a-…`) and finding (`f-…`) ids in the page's targets and details, through an optional `core.AuditNamer` that `cmd/vedette` implements over inventory (`DeviceRefs`: host name, else IP, else what the box knows) and findings (`Get`: "<CVE> on <device>"); core imports neither module. The page shows the name with the stored text in small type below; an id the box no longer has stays as it is. The CSV export keeps the stored text (it is the record). Not chosen: writing names into the lines when they are written (would change findings and inventory, and a renamed device would keep its old name in a hash-chained line); dropping system lines from `core_audit` (loses what the box changed). | Top-tier admin audit logs keep by time: GitHub's audit log lists the last 180 days (https://docs.github.com/en/enterprise-cloud@latest/admin/monitoring-activity-in-your-enterprise/reviewing-audit-logs-for-your-enterprise/accessing-the-audit-log-for-your-enterprise; Enterprise Server: https://docs.github.com/en/enterprise-server@3.20/admin/managing-accounts-and-repositories/managing-users-in-your-enterprise/auditing-users-across-your-enterprise); Microsoft Purview Audit (Standard) 180 days, Premium one year (https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/audit-solutions-overview, https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/audit-log-retention-policies). Vedette keeps one year because a small office looks back rarely and late, and the box has the disk; DATA_MODEL §5.3 had already proposed 365 days for `core_audit`. Walk 1: 332 lines on day one, 22 from one "Add software", targets shown as ids. | 2026-11-13 |

(1) **One switch, `CREDENTIALED_IN_UI = false` in `web/src/lib/credentialed.ts`** (the shape of D-403's `SPAN_IN_UI` and D-408's `BUNDLE_IN_UI`): while false the scans page has no Credentialed scan tab, and Settings → Modules and the setup wizard's module step do not list `scan-credentialed` (the title counts only what is listed). Kept as they are: the tab, the contract and the mock (`/scans/credentialed*`), the manifest, the module's row in the backend's `GET /modules`, and the tests, which run the tab with the switch on; one test per page runs v1. (2) A box that already has the module on keeps it on (it does nothing); it is just not shown. (3) e2e: `e2e/qa/scan.spec.ts` skips the credentialed walk; the module-dependency walks in `e2e/qa/core.spec.ts` and `e2e-real/modules.global.spec.ts` now use AI response (needs AI assistant) instead. Post-v1: build the backend (Greenbone container, D-55), set the switch true, recheck S-SCAN-5. | A feature a build cannot run must not be offered as a working path (D-408 for the offline bundle, same reasoning); an honest "not available" after inviting the customer to prepare a target is still a dead end (walk 1). | D-418 | **Reinstalling after `install.sh --uninstall --yes --keep-data` brings Vedette back with its data, and a re-run bootstraps even while vedette-host runs (customer walk 2, W2-9 and W2-10).** What was wrong: `--keep-data` removes the Quadlet units and the images but keeps `/var/lib/vedette-host`, so `containers/versions-core.json` was still there and the next run said "already bootstrapped", skipped the bootstrap and failed on "vedette-core.service not found" (exit 7, N100, n4 over n3 data); after the records were moved away by hand, `vedette-host -bootstrap` refused with `daemon_running` (exit 6) because an earlier run (or the package's restart on upgrade) had started the host. (1) **The bootstrap is skipped only when core has both its record and its unit** (`versions-core.json` and `vedette-core.container`); a missing unit is installed again. (2) **Kept data with no unit of any container** (records in `containers/versions-*.json`, none of `vedette-{core,sensor,scan,honeypot}.container`) is what `--keep-data` leaves: the run clears the host's container records (`versions-*`, `pulled-*`, `transition-*`, `containers/units/`; never the data, the backups, the release index or the host's package records) and bootstraps its own release, same or newer, over the kept data, then records what runs. The records are cleared by the install, not by the uninstall, because until then they say which release last ran on the data. (3) **An older release than that is refused in preflight, before any change** (`dpkg --compare-versions` on the SemVer with `-`→`~`): core's migrations are forward-only and an older core would run on a newer database. Before the records are cleared the release is noted in `/var/lib/vedette-install/kept-release`, removed only once the bootstrap wrote core's unit, so a run that stops half way keeps the guard. A newer release is allowed with a warning: unlike Settings → Updates this path takes no `pre_update` backup, so the way back is a backup made before the uninstall (RUNBOOK §1.3). (4) **The installer stops a running vedette-host before `-bootstrap`** and starts it after (`start_and_wait`), and again from `cleanup` when the run fails, with the honeypot when it ran (it `Requires=` the host and stops with it): the bootstrap stays a one-owner operation (D-142) rather than going through the socket, which the installer cannot use (not core). Not chosen: (a) the uninstall clears the records: it loses the downgrade guard; (b) the host re-renders missing units from its records at start: the images are removed by the uninstall, so it would still need the network, and it is new host behaviour for a state only the installer makes; (c) keeping the images on `--keep-data`: the uninstall promises to give the space back and the customer path downloads the package anyway, so a keep-data reinstall needs the network like a first install. Known limits: `min_upgrade_from` of the new release is not checked against the kept data (the bootstrap has never checked it), and there is no automatic backup before a newer core migrates kept data (deferred). Reviewed by an independent Opus reviewer (round 1: the guard lost after a failed run, the honeypot left stopped, `RELEASE` read from the environment, no backup on the newer path; all fixed or written down; round 2: three LOW, two fixed, the third written down: the honeypot restart is checked by hand on the box, not by install-check). Verified by effect in `scripts/dev/install-check.sh` (setup through the API, `--keep-data`, older release refused, reinstall: setup still complete and the administrator signs in; then core's unit removed with the host running) and `TestInstallSh_KeepDataReinstallReadsAndClearsTheHostsRecords`. Like the leaders: GitLab's Linux package keeps the data on uninstall and a reinstall picks it up (https://docs.gitlab.com/install/package/); Grafana migrates its database forward at start and does not support running an older version on it, restore a backup instead (https://archive.grafana.com/docs/grafana/v8.4/installation/upgrading/, https://grafana.com/whats-new/2026-04-14-unified-storage-for-folders-and-dashboards/). | 2026-11-13 |
| D-419 | **Customer walk 2 small fixes (W2-2, W2-3, W2-6, W2-7, W2-8).** (1) The osquery one-line command downloads the script to a new `mktemp` file each run (`(f=$(mktemp) && curl … -o "$f" && echo "<sha256>  $f" \| sha256sum -c - && sudo sh "$f" --token …; r=$?; rm -f "$f"; exit $r)`, a subshell so a failed download, check or install still exits non-zero), still checks the SHA-256 before running and removes the file after; Windows uses `%TEMP%\vedette-osquery-<GUID>.ps1` and removes it. A fixed `/tmp/vedette-osquery.sh` left by another user cannot be overwritten under Ubuntu's `fs.protected_regular=2` (curl error 23 on the re-run as root). (2) The installer sends `dpkg`/`rpm` output (osquery's own package script prints a bare line of numbers, "1981590 5597 1" on Ubuntu) to a temporary log shown only when the package install fails, and enables the service with `systemctl enable --quiet`. (3) New sensor status `starting` on an appliance: not online while core's OnGuard is still bringing the `sensor` container up (`startWatch` in cmd/vedette: the start is being retried, for at most 10 min, or the host confirmed a start or a running unit less than 3 min ago); the GUI shows "Starting…" with why and re-reads every 10 s; past those bounds a sensor that never reported is "Not connected yet" with what to check (Settings → Modules off/on, `journalctl -u vedette-sensor` / `vedette-core`). The guard's state is not persisted: after a restart of core the first look at a running unit counts as a confirmation. Container-only never says `starting`. (4) Box network shows one role per row: the management port is the Management chip, another card is never offered Management (the box refuses it: `management_fixed`/`management_count`), and with SPAN hidden (D-403) an unused card's role is the text "Unused" (only a card that is still the SPAN port keeps a select). (5) `/setup` step 1 has no Back; `RequireSession` asks `GET /me` only once `/setup` says setup is complete, so a fresh box logs no 401 on its first load. | Found by the supervisor's direct test of the N100 (0.0.1-test.n3, 2026-11-13). Sources: `mktemp` per run as Homebrew/rustup-style installers do (`curl … -o "$(mktemp)"`), Ubuntu `protected_regular` (https://www.kernel.org/doc/html/latest/admin-guide/sysctl/fs.html#protected-regular); a transient "starting/provisioning" state before "disconnected" as UniFi ("Provisioning", "Adopting") and Home Assistant add-ons ("Starting") show; `systemctl --quiet` (systemctl(1)). Not chosen: `rm -f /tmp/vedette-osquery.sh` first (the `rm` runs as the user, who cannot remove another user's file in the sticky /tmp, and a fixed name stays a collision); a time window on `enabled_at` for "starting" (a default-on module's `enabled_at` is the install time, not the end of setup); hiding the 401 in JS (the browser logs it whatever the page does). | 2026-11-13 |
| D-420 | **Feeds: địa chỉ bị cấm thì từ chối ngay lúc lưu, địa chỉ trùng thì từ chối và nêu tên feed kia, trạng thái kéo hiện một giá trị bị loại thật; bản chỉ container nói thật về credentialed scan, MCP và "Honeypot touches" (lượt đi Mac 2026-11-12 w2, nhóm G10).** (1) **SSRF lúc lưu** (thay D-208 (4)): `POST /feeds/custom`, `PUT /feeds/custom/{id}` và `PUT /feeds/sources/{id}` (địa chỉ mirror) trả 400 `blocked_host` với đúng câu của lượt kéo ("Vedette does not pull feeds from itself or from loopback, link-local or cloud metadata addresses.") khi host là **IP viết thẳng** mà lượt kéo từ chối (loopback, link-local, metadata đám mây, unspecified, multicast, kể cả dạng IPv4-mapped/NAT64/6to4/IPv4-compatible, và địa chỉ của chính hộp: giao diện của container, gateway, địa chỉ vedette-host báo) hoặc là `localhost`/`*.localhost` (`feeds.CheckDest`, cùng hàm `refusedAlways`/`destGuard.refused` của bộ quay số). **Không phân giải DNS trong request**: tên khác qua được lúc lưu, bộ quay số vẫn chặn ở mỗi lượt kéo (INV-17, chống DNS rebinding), nên lớp kiểm lúc kéo giữ nguyên. Mã `blocked_host` giống SIEM của `logs` (cùng lớp lỗi). Hộp thoại kiểm trước ở trình duyệt (`blockedFeedHost`, cùng luật) và hiện câu dưới ô Address; mock trả cùng mã/câu. Spec e2e-real dùng tên `e2e-loopback.lan` (bộ `e2eOffline` gửi về 127.0.0.1) thay vì 127.0.0.1. (2) **Địa chỉ trùng**: feed riêng có địa chỉ trùng địa chỉ hiện tại của một feed khác (có sẵn hoặc riêng; so scheme và host không phân biệt hoa thường, bỏ cổng mặc định và `#fragment`, đường dẫn và query phải khớp) → 400 `duplicate_url` "The feed "<tên>" already uses this address.", kiểm **cuối cùng** (sau mọi lỗi của chính thân request, như `duplicate_name`). Từ chối chứ không chỉ cảnh báo: feed thứ hai kéo lại cùng danh sách và đếm mỗi chỉ báo hai lần như hai nguồn. Mirror của feed có sẵn không bị kiểm trùng (admin có thể trỏ hai feed có sẵn vào cùng mirror nội bộ có chủ đích). Các phần nhỏ: tên feed đã có trần 60 ký tự ở cả hợp đồng (`max(60)`, OpenAPI) và `CheckName`; ô Name có `maxLength=60` nên dán 300 ký tự bị cắt im lặng, nay ô ghi "Up to 60 characters."; feed bật chưa kéo lần nào ghi "Fetched at the next scheduled check (every 5 minutes), or now with Fetch now." (job `pull` mỗi 5 phút, `PullEvery`; không tự kéo ngay sau khi lưu: handler sẽ phải giữ request tới 60 s hoặc chạy goroutine ngoài `core/jobs`); dòng WARN "feed pull failed" ghi thêm `name`. (3) **Mẫu giá trị bị loại** (thay phần "trạng thái che giá trị" của walk 2 trong INV-3): câu trạng thái của lượt kéo ("Most often: …", "All N rows were rejected: …") dùng dòng đầu tiên của lý do thường gặp nhất với giá trị hiện ra qua `quoteVal` (≤ 40 đơn vị UTF-16, ký tự không in được thành dấu cách, trích dẫn kiểu Go; văn bản thuần, GUI vẽ như text) để admin biết dòng nào bị loại. `reasons[]` của API vẫn che (`"…"`), nhóm theo mẫu như cũ. (4) **Bản chỉ container** (cùng tín hiệu D-381: `GET /modules` `available`/`install`): `ModuleOff` (dùng chung) của module `available:false` nói "<tên> is not on this install" và lý do, không mời bật, không liên kết Modules — áp cho tab Credentialed scan; trang MCP nói cổng MCP không được publish nên không công cụ nào ngoài container `vedette-core` tới được, SSH tunnel tới máy cũng không (đóng gói là `.ai/deferred/feat-mcp-server.md:3`), `docs/INSTALL-CONTAINER.md` ghi như vậy. (5) SIEM: ô "Honeypot touches" bị khoá, không tick, kèm lý do khi honeypot `available:false`, và không gửi trong thân lưu; API không đổi (honeypot không có trên bản này nên không có sự kiện nào để chuyển, nhận `honeypot` là vô hại). (6) **Tên dành cho tài liệu/thử nghiệm** (lượt đi 3): `example.com`, `example.net`, `example.org` và mọi tên dưới chúng (RFC 2606 §3) cùng lớp với `.example`, `.test`, `.invalid` và nay cả `*.localhost` (RFC 6761 §6.3): chỉ báo là tên miền trần bị loại với lý do "is a reserved example or test name" (trước là "local, reserved or public-suffix name", và `bad.example.com` còn được nhận), URL trỏ vào chúng "points at a reserved example or test name"; `Judge`/`IOCKey` cũng không coi chúng là IOC (`localName`), nên logs/honeypot/response không bao giờ khớp chúng. `localhost` một nhãn vẫn là "local or private host". (7) **Địa chỉ của chính máy chạy Vedette** (lượt đi 3: feed riêng ở `http://172.18.0.1:18070/ioc.json`, cổng mặc định của mạng compose = máy chạy Docker, dải riêng mà hộp thoại cho phép): vẫn từ chối (an toàn SSRF trước: đó là hộp hoặc máy của chính người dùng, Vedette không kéo từ nó). Lúc lưu, IP viết thẳng là địa chỉ hộp/gateway (không loopback) → 400 `blocked_host` với câu "This address is the machine Vedette runs on (its own address, or the computer that runs its container). Vedette does not pull feeds from itself: serve the feed from another machine."; lúc kéo (tên phân giải ra địa chỉ đó) `ErrOwnAddress` (bọc `ErrBlockedAddress`) cho cùng câu thay vì nói "loopback". (8) Gợi ý "Records path" của feed IOC dạng JSON đưa ví dụ IOC (`$.data[*]`, mặc định của nó), feed lỗ hổng giữ `$.vulnerabilities[*]`. | Lượt đi Mac 2026-11-12 w2 (G10) và w3. RFC 2606 §3 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2606#section-3 ; RFC 6761 §6.3 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6761#section-6.3 ; Tham khảo: OWASP SSRF Prevention Cheat Sheet (kiểm danh sách chặn ở đầu vào, và kiểm lại địa chỉ đã phân giải lúc kết nối) https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Server_Side_Request_Forgery_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.html ; GitLab webhooks (URL tới mạng cục bộ bị từ chối lúc lưu trừ khi admin cho phép) https://docs.gitlab.com/ee/security/webhooks.html ; MISP feeds (nhập feed bỏ qua feed trùng URL đã có) https://www.circl.lu/doc/misp/managing-feeds ; Drupal Aggregator `FeedUrlConstraint` (từ chối feed trùng URL) https://api.drupal.org/api/drupal/core%21modules%21aggregator%21src%21Plugin%21Validation%21Constraint%21FeedUrlConstraint.php/class/FeedUrlConstraint/9 . Không chọn: phân giải DNS lúc lưu (chậm, trả lời có thể đổi trước lượt kéo, đã có kiểm lúc kết nối); chỉ cảnh báo khi trùng (vẫn kéo đôi, đếm đôi); tự kéo ngay sau khi lưu (xem (2)); ẩn hẳn ô honeypot (người dùng không biết vì sao thiếu). | 2026-11-12 |
| D-421 | **Syslog from an undeclared sender stays dropped, but the Sources page names the sender (S-LOG-1, walk 3; replaces "no GUI" of logs open question 2).** (1) **Why**: on a container install, syslog sent from the machine that runs the containers reaches core from the container network's gateway (172.18.0.1 in walk 3), so a source declared with the device's address got nothing and nothing said why; the listener already counted the sender (`listen.Stats.UnknownSender`). (2) **What**: `GET /logs/unknown-senders` (operator and up: addresses of senders that are not sources) returns the 10 senders seen most recently with the protocol of the last message, the count and the last time; a sender that a source now declares with the protocol it used is left out, so adding the source clears the hint at once. The page says "<ip> sends syslog over UDP, but no source has this IP, so the box drops its lines (N times, last …)", or names the source when the IP is declared with another protocol; admins get **Add as source** (form pre-filled with the IP and protocol) or **Edit <source>**; on a container install a line explains the gateway. (3) **Bounds and trust**: in memory only (the 256-entry LRU of the listener), counted since the listener last started, which the page says; the address comes from the socket, never from the line text; nothing from such a sender is stored (FORBID-5 unchanged). | Syslog servers that filter senders say so where the admin looks: rsyslog's `$AllowedSender` logs the disallowed sender it discards, Wazuh `remoted` logs "Message from '<ip>' not allowed" for an IP outside `allowed-ips`. Both put it in a daemon log the Vedette user never reads (single page, no shell), so the same fact goes on the Sources page, next to the action that fixes it. Not chosen: accepting and storing lines from unknown senders for review (FORBID-5: a spoofed or stray sender would fill the store); a persistent table (the hint is about now; a restart re-learns within one message). Sources: https://www.rsyslog.com/doc/configuration/global/options/rsconf1_allowedsender.html ; https://documentation.wazuh.com/current/user-manual/reference/ossec-conf/remote.html ; D-203, D-214 | 2026-11-12 |
| D-422 | **On a container-only install the OpenAI-compatible profile starts with an empty address and the hint says to use the machine's LAN IP; Ask names the box apart in its inventory citation (ai, S-AI-1, S-AI-5, walk 3; follows D-226).** (1) **Address**: walk 3 (Docker 29 on Linux) showed the D-226 default `http://host.containers.internal:11434/v1` failing Test ("Could not connect to host.containers.internal:11434") while the LAN IP connected. The box cannot tell Docker from Podman truthfully through what the API already says: `GET /modules` gives only `install` (`appliance` | `container`, D-381), and reading `/.dockerenv` or `/run/.containerenv` inside the container would be a new field for one hint. It does not need to: on `container` no name works everywhere. Docker Engine on Linux resolves `host.docker.internal` only with `extra_hosts: host-gateway`, which the shipped compose does not have and `deploy/compose/compose_test.go` keeps out (D-226, Kiên's packaging; not changed here), so a `host.docker.internal` default would fail the same way; rootful Podman resolves `host.containers.internal`, rootless Podman reaches nothing on the machine. The LAN IP is the one answer that works on Docker and rootful Podman. So: `appliance` (install.sh, rootful Podman Quadlet) keeps the D-226 default; `container` leaves the address empty with the placeholder `http://LAN-IP-of-the-machine:11434/v1` and its own hint (LAN IP; Docker on Linux knows neither name, `host.docker.internal` only on Docker Desktop; rootless Podman cannot reach the machine). While `install` is still loading the appliance default stays (the page shell has already read `GET /modules` by the time a dialog opens). **D-226 follow-up**: its point (1) now holds for the appliance only; points (2) and (3) stand; adding `extra_hosts: host-gateway` to the container compose stays out (a deploy change for Kiên's area, and the LAN IP works on every runtime that can reach the machine at all). (2) **Ask's inventory citation**: the box itself is a row of the inventory (D-53) and `search_assets` searches it (a question about the box's own software is a fair question), but Devices says "Only the Vedette box so far" and Reports counts no device, so "Inventory: 1 device searched" contradicted both. The citation now names the box apart: "Inventory: only the Vedette box searched", "Inventory: 3 devices and the Vedette box searched"; the `search_assets` result line and Explain's "Inventory: … matching" citation count the same way; the model's data is unchanged. Not chosen: leaving the box out of `search_assets` (Ask could no longer answer about the box). References: Docker `--add-host` and `host-gateway` (https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/container/run/#add-host); Docker Desktop `host.docker.internal` (https://docs.docker.com/desktop/features/networking/#i-want-to-connect-from-a-container-to-a-service-on-the-host); Podman `host.containers.internal` and pasta (https://docs.podman.io/en/latest/markdown/podman-run.1.html); Open WebUI tells Docker users to add `--add-host=host.docker.internal:host-gateway` or use the host's IP (https://docs.openwebui.com/getting-started/quick-start/). | 2026-11-12 |
| D-423 | **Alert channels and its History: tables that fit the ~730 px content column, cards under 768 px, the running test and its failure shown in the row; Ask keeps its 500-character limit; the token table counts Calls, failed ones included (notify, ai; S-NOT-1, S-AI-4, S-AI-5; walk 3 G13).** (1) **Channels table**: at 1280 px the Actions column ran past the right edge and on a 412 px phone it was off-screen. At 1280 px the page's content column is only ~730 px (app sidebar + settings nav), so the desktop table must fit that, not the viewport: Alert channels has three columns (channel with where it sends and from which severity under it; status with the last test under it; actions stacked) and History three (time with channel and recipients under it; what; result with its reason and Send again under it), checked at 1280 and 1024 px. Under 768 px both use the repo's `DataTable` `mobileRow` cards (one layout at a time) as Feeds and Incidents do. Not chosen: a kebab menu (hides Send test and Remove one tap deeper and adds a menu component for one table). (2) **Send test**: the API stays as it is (`POST /notify/channels/{type}/test` answers when the far end does, up to 30 s); the row says "Sending test…" with a spinner while that request is open, a failed test shows its reason as text under "Tested …: failed", and a channel that is on with a failed last test says so. The channel is not turned off on a failed test: a far end that is down for a minute must not silently stop alerts. (3) **Ask length**: the walk asked for a 2,000-character cap; the box already refuses more than 500 (`askQuestionMax`, `invalid_question`, contract `max(500)`), so the limit stays 500 and the GUI now says it (counter from 80 %, reason under the field, Ask off) even when a fill skips `maxLength`. (4) **Runs**: the per-task count is `COUNT(*)` of `ai_activity` rows (less hook-blocked and response-module rows), so a failed Ask and a profile's connection test are counted; that matches the run log below it and S-AI-4 (failed calls are logged, cost no tokens), so the count stays and the column is named **Calls** with a line saying it counts every call, answered or not. Not chosen: splitting answered/failed (an API change for a number the run log already shows per call). | Tables to cards on narrow screens: Nielsen Norman Group, "Mobile Tables" (https://www.nngroup.com/articles/mobile-tables/). Test notifications report in place: Grafana contact points, Test button (https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/alerting/configure-notifications/manage-contact-points/). Request counts include errors: Cloudflare AI Gateway analytics counts requests and errors together (https://developers.cloudflare.com/ai-gateway/observability/analytics/). | 2026-11-12 |
| D-424 | **An AI profile keeps its last connection test, as the row of an alert channel does (S-AI-1).** (1) Only a test of the saved profile **exactly as saved** counts (same provider type, API style, address, model and key): the Test button of a row, or Test in the edit dialog with the address, model and key unchanged. A test of a draft, or of a key typed but not saved yet, is not that profile's test, so a profile saved after a failed draft test reads "Not tested yet", never "success". (2) A change of the address, model, provider type or key clears it ("Not tested yet"); a new name, location or cap keeps it. A cancelled request records nothing; a test stopped by the token cap sent nothing and records nothing. (3) Stored as `{at, ok, detail}` per profile id in `ai_setting` key `profile_tests` (no migration: a column on `ai_profile` would also need a line in the export policy of `modules/core`, and a column with `CHECK` is not add-only under D-164); `detail` is the box's own sentence (`probeFailure`), which may name the server's host but never the key or the provider's raw text, at most 300 characters; returned as `last_test` on every profile of `/ai/profiles`. (4) The row shows "Tested <time>: success" / "Tested <time>: failed: <reason>" as text; the page header says "AI profiles are set up, but the last connection test of each one failed…" when every profile's last test failed. | Same shape as `notify_channel.last_test` in this repo (INV-11 of notify: the saved channel is tested, saving clears it) and as Grafana's data sources, where "Save & test" tests the saved settings and the status belongs to them (https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/datasources/#add-a-data-source). Not chosen: keeping a draft's result and attaching it on save (needs the key or a hash of it held between two requests; the user can press Test on the row); a migration-added column (above). | 2026-11-12 |
| D-425 | **A hit through a listed parent stores and shows the listed name, and dedupes on it; the parent walk runs only while a feed that lists subdomains is on (S-LOG-4, logs L4; closes lines 4-6 of `fix-logs-hagezi-subdomains-mlee.md`; reverses "not stored" of D-228 (3)).** (1) **Stored and shown**: `logs_ioc_hits.listed_as` (add-only `volume/0007`, no CHECK so an older binary's writes never fail, '' = listed for itself) and `IocHit.listed_as` (null = listed for itself) in the digest, `IocHit`/`IocHits`, `logs.ioc_hit.detected` and the `known_bad` export. The Logs row keeps the name asked for (what the device did) and adds "listed as bad.example"; Look up goes to the listed name, the one Feeds holds (before, Look up on `a.b.bad.example` found nothing). `logs.bad_address.detected` is unchanged (notify already keyed it on the parent). (2) **Dedupe on (device, listed name)**: `recentHitSQL` matches `dest = name OR listed_as = name`, and `matchIOC` keeps one pair per batch, so a device asking for many random subdomains of one listed name (DGA-like) is one row in 24 hours, as it is one incident; the listed name asked for itself joins the same row. No count or last name is kept: the row shape has neither, and adding an UPDATE on every repeat is write work on the hot path for a number the incident (`count` in notify) already carries. (3) **No walk without a subdomain feed**: `logs.Feeds.Subdomains` (adapter: `feeds.Store.IOCSubdomainsOn`, a switched-on built-in source with `Source.Subdomains`, today only hagezi TIF), asked once per batch and only when an unlisted name needs its parents; an error walks as before (a failed question must not lose a hit). | Security tools that match a wildcard list say which entry matched, not only the name queried: AdGuard Home's query log shows the rule that blocked a request (`\|\|example.org^` for a subdomain), Pi-hole marks a regex/wildcard block with the rule; so the listed name is what a person looks up. Grouping repeats per (device, matched entry) follows the incident key notify already uses (`ioc:<parent>`). Sources: https://adguard-dns.io/kb/general/dns-filtering-syntax/ ; https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdGuardHome/wiki/Configuration ; https://docs.pi-hole.net/regex/overview/ ; D-151, D-227, D-228 | 2026-11-12 |
| D-426 | **The ai specs on the real backend answer from a stand-in model on loopback; only the fetch half of CVE news stays `test.fixme` (D-171 (2)).** (1) `web/e2e-real/fake-ai.ts` is an OpenAI-compatible server (Chat Completions) on 127.0.0.1 that the spec starts and stops itself. The profiles point at it as "inside your network", which may reach loopback (`provider.IsInternalAddr`), so the box dials it exactly as it would a local Ollama: no product seam, no key of anyone, nothing leaves the machine (PRIVACY flow 3). It answers by what the box asks for (the `response_format` schema name, one read-only tool call when tools are offered, else text), the model `m-fail` answers 500 for the fallback case, and it keeps every request so a test counts calls and reads what was sent (memory, passages, masked text). Explain with its cache and fallback, Ask your data with tools and hooks, the log digest, memory suggestions and the knowledge base (MD and DOCX) are real tests now. (2) CVE news is not: the box fetches NVD, GitHub, a vendor page and six blogs over HTTPS on port 443 to global unicast addresses only (INV-6, D-281), and the e2e box has no seam to serve them on loopback. The spec tests what fetches nothing (unknown CVE 404, malformed ID 400, skill off 409, viewer 403: no call, no activity row) and keeps the fetch-and-summarise flow as `test.fixme` naming this decision; `TestContract_S_AI_3_TheBoxFetchesAndTheAISummarises` and the `TestNews*` tests carry it with a fake transport. (3) No PDF in the spec: the e2e box registers no `pdftext` child (`.ai/deferred/feat-pdftext-child.md`, L-b), so a PDF would end with 0 chunks; MD and DOCX exercise the same index and retrieval. | Hermetic end-to-end tests: a dependency outside the system under test is replaced by a fake the test controls, never by the real service on the Internet (Google Testing Blog, "Hermetic Servers", https://testing.googleblog.com/2012/10/hermetic-servers.html). Playwright's own network mocking (`page.route`, https://playwright.dev/docs/mock) only reaches requests of the browser, not the server-side fetches of the box, so the news sources need a seam in the box (a test-only transport in `cmd/vedette/e2ebox_test.go` plus an exported hook in `modules/ai`); that is product code for one spec while the Go contract tests already cover the flow, so not done now. Not chosen: letting the e2e box fetch the real sources (sends data out, results change every day), or a proxy (the news transport refuses proxies by design, D-281). | 2026-11-12 |
| D-427 | **e2e-real: the scan worker and the TLS syslog listener run on the box of the run; what stays out is accepted under D-171 (2).** (1) **Scan**: `POST /sensors/scan` of the control server (cmd/vedette/e2escan_test.go) starts the REAL worker of sensor-active in the box process, on the box's real sensor link with the active sensor's credentials, in the slot of the active sensor (one worker per link), with a FAKE nuclei (`match`, `nomatch`, `hang`, `dead`; it reads template ids from the `-t` paths and targets from `-u`, logs its argv, sends nothing). Its pack is the committed index (`content/nucleipack`) with the same version and hash, so the Dispatcher's and the worker's pack checks pass as in production, and a stand-in file per template whose hash the worker's index carries, so the worker's file check runs for real. While the worker runs, the spec turns active discovery off and restores it only after the box sees the worker gone (90 s heartbeat), so no sweep is queued for it and the sensors spec's nmap and probe-log counts stay its own. The four scan fixmes are real tests: a run to the end with a match that confirms the finding, Stop now, auto-stop, and the new-KEV rescan log (`skipped_off`, and `pick_only` for a matching device declared by hand). (2) **Not in e2e: a KEV rescan that runs.** Every device a spec can make is declared by hand (`origin manual`), which INV-1 keeps out of automatic scans; the only other origin is a sensor discovery, which would change the device set `sensors.global.spec.ts` counts. (3) **Logs TLS**: `syslogTestTLS` (cmd/vedette/logs.go) stands in for `deps.SyslogTLS` when the box serves no TLS; nil in production, set only by `TestE2EBox` to a self-signed certificate for 127.0.0.1; ready.json gives `syslog_tls_port` (syslog port + 1, as the listener maps it) and `syslog_tls_cert`. The TLS test is real (a line sent over TLS is stored, the presented certificate is the one in ready.json, the socket opens with the first TLS source and closes with the last). On that box `tls_unavailable` cannot happen, so the refusal is carried by `TestASourceOverTLSIsRefusedOnCreateAndEdit`, `TestWithoutATLSConfigTLSIsRefusedAndNothingListens`, `TestContract_INV3_SourceValidationFollowsTheMock` (modules/logs). (4) **Logs digest after the 24 h warm-up** stays `test.fixme`, accepted for good: a box cannot skip the warm-up; carried by `TestContract_INV6_WarmUpIsSilent`, `TestContract_INV6_SpikeMaths`, `TestContract_INV6_BaselineOverTenFakeDays`. | Same shape as the fakes the run already has in the box process (D-163 fake host, slice 7 sensors with a fake nmap): the real product path end to end (core plan → probe log → Dispatcher → mutual-TLS link → worker → core/exec) with only the program that would touch the network replaced; no network scan (rules/agent-safety). The vedette-sensor binary cannot be used: it reads the pack from the fixed path of the scan image (`nucleiargv.TemplatesDir`); `worker.Config.TemplatesDir` is the existing test seam. Not chosen: a production flag for the template folder (widens the shipped binary for a test); a fake `scan.Engine` in core (skips the Dispatcher, the link and the worker, which is what a run tests); a discovered device for the rescan (couples two global specs). The TLS seam follows `syslogHost` and `testBaseURL` (D-173): a package var only the e2e test sets; serving the whole box over HTTPS on loopback would change every spec's base URL. | 2026-11-12 |
| D-428 | **AI v1-left round (module ai): where a secret finder, a device link and a cut `Remember:` line stop.** (1) block-pii finds secrets by where the vendor's syntax puts them, still RE2 and linear: ` password x` in an indented `line con|aux|vty|tty` block, IOS `snmp-server host <ip> … version 1|2c <community>`, lower-case YAML keys (`password:`, `snmp_community:`), the `Private-Lines:` body of a `.ppk`, FortiGate `set name` inside `config system snmp community` (lines indented deeper than the header; one pass, linear); each has a leave-alone case and a hostile-size case in the table tests. Over-masking one word (`password 3 times` at the start of a lower-case line, `The password authentication encrypted`) is kept: the value shape is all a finder can tell, and a leak costs more than a word Capitalised `Password: x` is masked too (a ticket or form pasted into a question says it that way; prose that starts with it costs one word); `pass` and bare `community` keys only in lower case, so `Community: OpenWrt forums` stays. The FortiGate and `line` blocks read blank lines as part of the block and stop at the first line at the header's indent, with no line count (each line is read by one header at most, so the work is linear; a cap would let the rest of a long block through). A YAML or environment value that is unquoted and holds spaces is masked up to its first space only (`wpa_passphrase: correct horse battery`): a finder cannot tell where prose begins, the limit stays. (Cisco IOS and Fortinet documents give the syntax; no vendor parser: ponytail, upgrade path when a customer needs it). `ntp server|peer … key 1 prefer` is no longer masked: 1 is a key id. (2) Digest items get `asset_id` from the box: an item that names exactly one device among the bad connections sent links to it, never one the model wrote; Datadog and Sentry link every issue to its host the same way, from their own ids. (3) A `Remember:` line that does not end like a sentence is a reply cut at the token limit: it is removed and suggests nothing, instead of a stop-reason field in every provider adapter (the administrator reviews every suggestion anyway, INV-8). (4) The question kept as evidence of a pending suggestion stays: it is what the administrator judges by, it goes with the row when it is accepted or rejected, and `ai_memory` has no evidence column. (5) Two POST /ai/logs/digest with the same inputs: one slot, the second waits and reads the stored result (single flight, as Go's `singleflight` and every cache stampede guard). | Sources: Cisco IOS XE `snmp-server host`, `line vty`/`password`; FortiOS `config system snmp community`; PuTTY `.ppk` format; Datadog/Sentry issue-to-host links. | 2026-11-13 |
| D-430 | **A broken hash chain of the AI activity log raises one incident through notify; the check runs daily as an ai job.** Job `activity-verify` (24 h, offered only when `Config.Alert` is wired, not housekeeping: it calls out to notify) runs `VerifyActivity`; when the chain is broken it publishes one `incident` notice of severity high (`notify.Publish`, the same door `response` uses for its messages): the count and the first bad row, never row content. The same break (its first bad row, or "tail" when rows are missing at the end; rows added after it do not make a new break) is raised once per process, not every day; a restart raises a break that is still there once more; a chain that verifies again forgets it. A notify module that is off makes the job fail and try again at its next run (the alert is not dropped). Why: S-AI-8 promises a tamper-evident log; an unattended box needs someone told. Source: the usual alert pattern of telling once and repeating only on an interval, as Prometheus Alertmanager does (`repeat_interval`, https://prometheus.io/docs/alerting/latest/configuration/); here the interval is "until the box restarts" (ponytail: no stored state; upgrade path: an `ai_setting` key with the last alerted break). Limits: the notice goes through `notify.Publish` as a message to the channels, not as a row of the Incidents page (a new `IncidentKind` would touch notify's table, the API contract and the GUI); and when notify is on but no channel takes a high notice, the notice is lost and is not raised again until a restart. Chosen over a Home banner (new screen, no story). | 2026-11-13 |

| D-432 | **Logs IOC and storage: five decisions that close the open L1/L4 lines.** (1) **Writer and search at 5 million lines, measured once (2026-11-13, one run of `TestMeasureFiveMillionLines`, `VEDETTE_MEASURE=1`, Ubuntu box, 5,000,000 rows of about 200 bytes over 6 days; the table fills in 44 s):** `Ingest` of 500 lines takes 7.9 ms per batch with the table full (the writer is not slowed by the table size); `GET /logs/events` with no keyword 5-7 ms (the `ts` index, `total` capped at `CountCap`); a common keyword 45 ms (1 h) to 108 ms (24 h, 7 d: 200 lines found at once); a keyword that is rare or matches nothing is a scan of the window: 106 ms (1 h), 2.3 s (24 h), and past the 5 s `SearchTimeout` for 7 d (503 `server_busy`, with the message that says to choose a shorter range or a more specific keyword; at most `MaxSearches` = 2 at once). **Decision: `logs_events` stays in `logs.db` (no own SQLite file)**: the writer cost does not grow with the table and a search runs on the reader pool, so a second file would buy nothing; the bounded scan with its 503 is the designed answer at the byte cap (D-200). Upgrade path if a customer needs full-text search over days: an FTS5 index (`unicode61`), a migration with its own review. (2) **The device of a hit is resolved from the inventory by `src_ip` when it is read** (INV-7): kept. After a DHCP change an old hit shows the address's new holder; storing the device id at write time breaks INV-7 (a renamed or deleted device would show the old name) and the inventory itself keeps the address-to-device history only as far as it knows. Grafana and Elastic security events likewise show the asset resolved at view time with the raw `source.ip` beside it; the hit row always shows `src_ip`, so the person can tell. (3) **The `alert`/`block` verdict of `feeds.Judge` is not used for hits**: logs keeps the highest listing confidence of the enabled feeds and the incident severity follows it (>= 0.7 high). The verdict adds two things, a whitelist and "two independent sources", and the customer whitelist does not exist in the product (`feeds` handlers call `Judge` with an empty `Whitelist{}`), so nothing is lost; a `block` floor would repeat what the confidence of a block-class feed already says. When a whitelist ships, the adapter (`cmd/vedette/logsioc.go`) asks `Judge` and drops a whitelisted name. (4) **No cache across batches for the feed lookup**: the lookup is a point read on the indicator table's primary key and a batch asks each value once; with the 50-hit cap per batch and 5 s budget a chatty device costs one indexed read per batch, far below the cost of the batch itself (8 ms above); a cache would add staleness (a feed switched off must stop matching at once) for no measured gain. (5) **A lookup that runs past the 5 s budget says "the threat feeds answered too slowly"** (a separate warning from "could not be read"). | Why: every open line was a "decide with the story" or "measure" line; each is closed by a number or a reason. Sources: Elastic ECS `source.ip` and asset enrichment at read time (https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/ecs/current/ecs-source.html); Grafana Loki is not indexed by line text and warns that a line-filter over a long range is a scan, which is the same trade (https://grafana.com/docs/loki/latest/query/). Not chosen: a second SQLite file (no measured gain), FTS5 now (a migration that doubles the disk of the largest table for a search nobody asked for), storing `asset_id` (INV-7). | 2026-11-13 |

(2) **Summary event**: when a batch's hits go past `IocEventsPerHour` (100) the first such batch of the clock hour also publishes one `logs.anomaly.detected` event (`target` `ioc:more bad connections <hour>`, severity medium, "At least N more connections to known-bad addresses this hour, not announced one by one"; N is what that batch ran over, "at least" because later batches are not counted); notify opens a `log_anomaly` incident from it. It is not a `logs.bad_address.detected` event: that one means one connection and feeds the SIEM `ioc.hit` and response. Same shape as the anomalies' flood summary. (3) The GUI sample of the SIEM page now shows exactly what the formatters write (a `finding.created` record, box name `vedette`), and a Go test (`TestSiemSampleOfTheGuiIsWhatTheFormattersWrite`) fails when the sample and the formatters differ. | Why: the lines were a documented-format change and an upgrade path that the owner asked to decide now. | D-434 | **The Sources page shows what a device must trust for syslog over TLS: on a default box the box's own CA (with its SHA-256 fingerprint, expiry and a PEM download), not the server certificate (S-LOG-1; closes the deferred line of `feat-logs-syslog-tls.md`; corrected after review r1).** Facts read first (D-262, D-351, `cmd/vedette/boxca.go`, `tls.go`): the 8443 certificate the syslog TLS port also serves is a leaf signed by the box CA (`CN=Vedette box CA`, 20 years, made once, kept in `core_secret`); the leaf is re-issued on renewal and on an address change (D-139), the CA is the stable part, and an owner's `-tls-cert` replaces both. So a device that imports or pins the leaf breaks at the next renewal, and a leaf has `CA:false`, so a FortiGate importing it as a trusted CA fails chain verification. Decision: `GET /logs/sources` carries `box.tls` = `{ kind, issuer, port, fingerprint_sha256, subject, not_after, pem }` (null/absent when the box serves no TLS, i.e. when `tls_unavailable` applies); `pem`, fingerprint, subject and expiry describe the certificate to import. `kind` is `box_ca` when the leaf is signed by the box CA (the PEM is the CA's, the same certificate `GET /intake/ca.pem` serves; cmd/vedette hands it in as `logs.Config.TrustAnchor`, the agent-intake trust anchor, so no core package changes), `self_signed` when the leaf is its own issuer (the PEM is the leaf), and `issued` when another authority issued it (the PEM is the chain the owner gave the box; the card names the issuer). Only CERTIFICATE blocks are ever kept (an owner's combined file may hold a key). While the leaf is being re-issued under a new CA the trust anchor answers 503: the card is then hidden for a minute rather than wrong. `port` is the port a device sends to (6514 on a default box, p+1 for another `-syslog-port`). The service asks the same `GetCertificate` a handshake would, so a renewed leaf shows at once; the PEM is public data, so no new route is needed and the GUI builds the download from it in the browser (no new outgoing flow, nothing for PRIVACY.md). The card tells the admin to import the CA as trusted and not to pin the server certificate; the device setup dialog of a TLS source points to it. Not done: a separate download of the leaf. | Fortinet documents that the FortiGate verifies the syslog server's certificate against a CA certificate imported on the device during the TLS handshake, and that a client certificate is only needed when the server requires one (community tips, from search summaries, pages not opened: https://community.fortinet.com/t5/FortiGate/Technical-Tip-Send-Syslog-over-TLS-to-a-rsyslog-server/ta-p/248101 and https://community.fortinet.com/t5/FortiGate/Technical-Tip-How-to-send-encrypted-logs-to-Syslog-server/ta-p/240995), so the admin must be able to fetch the CA; syslog-ng's default network source uses 6514 for TLS (https://syslog-ng.github.io/admin-guide/060_Sources/005_Default-network-drivers/000_Default-network-drivers_options, search summary). D-214 (the TLS listener), D-139 (renewal), D-262 and D-351 (the box CA). | 2026-11-13 |
| D-435 | **A TLS log source may pin its sender's client certificate by SHA-256 fingerprint (RFC 5425 section 4.2.1 mutual authentication, optional per source; closes the deferred line "mutual TLS is not built").** Before: a TLS source was known by its IP like TCP (D-214 (2)). Decision: `SourceInput.client_cert_sha256` (optional, 64 lowercase hex characters, only for `proto: tls`, else 400 `bad_client_cert`; over HTTP a malformed fingerprint is refused first by the generated validator as 400 `invalid` with `field: client_cert_sha256`, the GUI normalises before sending so it never meets it); stored in `logs_sources.client_cert_sha256` (config migration 0004, `''` = none, every existing row), returned as `LogSource.client_cert_sha256` (null = none). The listener asks for a client certificate only from a sender whose source pins one (`GetConfigForClient` by the remote IP, `RequestClientCert`, session resumption off for that handshake), then requires the first presented certificate's SHA-256 to equal the pin (constant-time compare); no certificate or another one closes the connection and is counted in `Stats.CertRejected` with one Warn per 10 s. A pin is a pin, not a chain check: whoever holds that certificate's private key is the sender (like rsyslog's x509/fingerprint mode), so no CA, revocation or expiry logic is built and a device may rotate its certificate by editing the pin. Changing or removing the pin, or removing the source, ends the live connection (the connection remembers the pin it was accepted with). The IP check stays: the pin is in addition to it, never instead. A device with no certificate configured is unaffected (the request is made only for a pinned source). The GUI field is optional, shown for TLS only, and accepts a fingerprint as tools print it (`AB:CD:...`, spaces, upper case), normalising before sending. Rejected: requiring client certificates for every TLS source (FortiGate and others send one only when configured; the default would break every existing TLS source), a CA-based mode with name matching (a certificate authority UI and revocation for a LAN syslog port; ponytail), and a global trusted-CA setting. | rsyslog's gtls driver offers per-peer modes anon (no peer authentication, advised against), x509/fingerprint ("The fingerprint must be provided as the SHA1 or the SHA256 hex string of the certificate"), x509/certvalid and x509/name (opened: https://docs.rsyslog.com/doc/concepts/ns_gtls.html); the mode is chosen per input (https://docs.rsyslog.com/doc/reference/parameters/imtcp-streamdriver-authmode.html, default none); syslog-ng makes it a per-source `peer-verify()` choice (default required-trusted, `optional-untrusted` turns client authentication off: https://syslog-ng.github.io/admin-guide/100_TLS-encrypted_message_transfer/004_TLS_options, from a search summary, page not opened); FortiGate sends a client certificate only when one is configured and the server asks for it (Fortinet community tip on mutually authenticated TLS syslog: https://community.fortinet.com/t5/Support-Forum/Configuring-Syslog-for-Mutually-Authenticated-TLS-Transport/td-p/97555, from a search summary, page not opened). All three make client authentication optional and per receiver or source; fingerprint pinning is the lightest mode that needs no CA. RFC 5425 section 4.2.1 and 5.3 (D-214). | 2026-11-13 |
| D-436 | **TLS handshakes are rate-limited per declared sender: 20 a second, burst 100 (`Limits.HandshakeRate`, `HandshakeBurst`); a connection above it is closed before its handshake and counted in `ConnRejected`. Measured first, on the Ubuntu lab box, loopback only (closes the review L5 line and the 1,000-connection measurement line).** Measured once (`VEDETTE_MEASURE=1 go test -run 'TestMeasureLimits/(1000_idle_TLS|handshake)' ./modules/logs/listen`, through the heavy lock, ECDSA P-256 certificate, client and server in one process so every figure counts both sides): 1,000 idle TLS connections (4 senders x 250) completed their handshakes in 0.32 s wall using 1.06 s CPU and held about 35 MiB of heap plus stacks (about 36 KB each, the clients' share included, 2,000 goroutines more; plain TCP is the same MaxConns 1,000 limit); 1,000 sequential connect-handshake-close from one sender took 1.12 s (892 a second) and 1.42 CPU-ms each for both sides, so roughly 0.5 to 0.7 ms of server CPU per handshake with ECDSA (an RSA box certificate costs more). Conclusion: 1,000 TLS connections fit the box (the MaxConns 1,000 and 10 s handshake limits stay; nothing to change). The cost that matters is churn: before this change one declared sender could ask for several hundred handshakes a second up to MaxConnsIP, which is a core of CPU taken from the Ingest path. 20 a second per sender is far above what a device does (it keeps one connection open and reconnects after a failure or a box restart) and takes at most a few percent of a core; the burst of 100 lets a fleet behind one NAT address, or a device after a box restart, reconnect at once. The bucket is per sender IP, asked after the declared-sender check and before a slot or a handshake is paid for, kept only for declared TLS senders (SetSources drops the rest), so its memory is bounded by the sources. A SetSources close (a source removed, its protocol or pin changed) is no longer counted as a failed handshake (review L3). Not rate-limited: plain TCP (no handshake to pay). | A per-source-address connection rate that is refused before the work of the connection is done is how a proxy protects a TLS front: HAProxy's configuration manual has the `src_conn_rate` sample and the `tcp-request connection` rules for it (opened: https://docs.haproxy.org/3.0/configuration.html; only its keyword index was read through the fetch tool, not the semantics, so the design here rests on our own measurement, not on a copied number). The figures above are ours; the limit is a ceiling for a LAN device, not tuned to the box. | 2026-11-13 |

| D-438 | **The local-use NAT64 block `64:ff9b:1::/48` (RFC 8215) is read in every RFC 6052 layout a sub-prefix of it can have (/48 /56 /64 /96; never /32 or /40) by `addrForms` in notify, feeds and logs, and each decoded IPv4 address is judged; a lookup of the user directory or link store that fails on a resend is 503 `approver_check_unavailable` (retry), not 409 `approver_not_ready`.** (1) The operator's prefix length inside the /48 is not knowable from an address, so all four readings are checked and the address is refused when any of them is forbidden (fail closed); a reading inside 0.0.0.0/8 is dropped (a translator never forwards to "this network"; it is what the zero suffix of a shorter prefix looks like), so `64:ff9b:1:808:8:800::` and `64:ff9b:1::808:808` (8.8.8.8) are allowed; the standard `64:ff9b::/96` stays a /96 read only. Byte 8 is the reserved u octet, skipped as RFC 6052 §2.2 says. (2) Example now refused: `64:ff9b:1:1:64:6464:c800::` (100.100.100.200, a cloud metadata address) under a /64 layout. (3) The resend change is the same fail-closed idea applied to the right class: "the directory could not answer" is a transient error, "the approver does not qualify" stays a 409. | RFC 6052 §2.2 table of IPv4-embedded layouts; RFC 8215 (local-use prefix may be any length /48 or longer). The only cost of reading all layouts is refusing a few addresses that embed an allowed IPv4 only in one reading, inside a block nobody should expose to a webhook, a feed or a SIEM. Not changed: `modules/response/webhook.go` and `modules/ai` (other owners). | 2026-11-13 |
| D-439 | **A finding whose device no longer matches its entry stays open and says so once in its history; Vedette does not close it (findings, S-MIT-1).** Case: CISA changes the vendor or product of a KEV entry, or the device's software changes, so the matcher no longer produces the pair `(device, CVE)` although the finding exists (the matcher only adds, INV-6). Decision: when a match run judges a CVE (it is in the list matched) and a `suspected` finding (basis version or product) is no longer produced, findings writes one history row `no_longer_matches` ("The device no longer matches this entry ... Close it yourself if it does not apply.") and one audit row; status, severity and notifications do not change; a row is not written again while it is the latest one; when the pair matches again and that row is the latest, one `matches_again` row follows (inventory flaps: an observation replaces declared software, a hand edit), so the newest line never tells a person to close a finding that matches; a CVE missing from the list is never judged (a partial list says nothing), a scan-confirmed finding is not judged by the version matcher. Migration 0002 adds the action to the history CHECK. Leading products close such findings by themselves: Tenable sets a vulnerability that no longer appears on the host to Fixed (and Resurfaced if it returns), and Defender Vulnerability Management drops the entry when the software is updated or removed; both rest on a fresh authenticated scan or agent inventory. Not followed: Vedette's matcher reads an inventory that can be stale or partial (passive discovery, hand-declared software), and its FORBID-2 (kien, findings contract) says nothing closes without a person because a wrong auto-close hides a vulnerability that is being exploited; a rescan that no longer matches already only writes `rescan_clear` the same way. The history row gives the person the same signal with no hidden state; a person closes it with "patched" or "not relevant". Rejected: a new status `no_longer_matches` or auto `not_relevant` (changes the status enum in the API, the mock and every GUI filter, and breaks FORBID-2); doing nothing (the finding keeps asking for action on a device that may not have the product). | Sources: Tenable, [Vulnerability States](https://docs.tenable.com/web-app-scanning/Content/WAS/GettingStarted/VulnerabilityStates.htm) (Fixed: once present and no longer found; Resurfaced when it returns); Tenable, [Vulnerability Mitigation](https://docs.tenable.com/vulnerability-management/Content/Explore/Findings/VulnerabilityMitigation.htm); Microsoft Tech Community thread on stale Defender TVM data after a remediated application ([link](https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/discussions/microsoftthreatprotection/tvm-still-showing-outdated-vulnerabilities-despite-applications-being-up-to-date/4427813), community text, not official); Vedette `modules/findings/CONTRACT.md` FORBID-2. | 2026-11-13 |
| D-441 | **Log keyword search: a time-budgeted newest-first scan that answers with what it found, how far back it looked and a cursor to continue; no FTS5 index.** Measured once (2026-11-13, `TestMeasureFiveMillionLines`, `VEDETTE_MEASURE=1`, 5,000,000 rows of about 200 bytes over 6 days, Ubuntu box, through `~/vedette-wt/heavy`): before, a keyword that matches nothing was 106 ms (1 h), 2.3 s (24 h) and 503 `server_busy` past 5 s (7 d). After: 1 h 76 ms, 24 h 1.7 s (whole window, no match), **7 d: 5.0 s, answers 200 with an empty list, `searched_back_to` 2026-11-06 10:28 (about 2.6 of the 5 million lines) and a `next` cursor**; a common keyword fills the page of 200 in 8-9 ms with a `next`; no keyword 5-7 ms (unchanged); `Ingest` of 500 lines 10 ms per batch (unchanged, nothing was added to the write path). **How it works:** `GET /logs/events` with a keyword walks the `ts` index from the newest line back in steps of 20,000 rows, filters each step with the same `instr(lower(line), ?)` as before, and stops at 200 matches, at the start of the window, or when `SearchTimeout` (5 s) is spent. The last two cases that did not reach the window start answer 200 with `searched_back_to` (time) and `next_cursor` (an opaque `<ts>_<id>` cursor, `null` = the window is done; paging convention of API_CONVENTIONS section 4); `cursor=<next_cursor>` continues strictly below it, so no line is answered twice or missed. The GUI says "N matching lines found so far, searched back to <time>. Older lines are not searched yet." and shows **Search older lines**, which appends the next step. A search that could not finish even its first step is still 503 `server_busy`. `total` for a keyword search is the matches found so far (at most 200 per answer); the count to `CountCap` stays for a search with no keyword. A full page always carries a cursor (the step reads one line more than fits): a quiet box with 1,234 matches in a short window is paged, never cut at 200. The cursor is **not signed** (API_CONVENTIONS section 4 says HMAC): a viewer can already read every row, so a forged cursor only moves the search to another place in rows they may see, and it is only ever a bound argument. The cursor is untrusted input: only the exact `2006-01-02T15:04:05.000Z_<id>` form is accepted (else 400 `bad_cursor`) and it is only ever a bound argument. One trap found while measuring: with two lower bounds on `ts` SQLite takes the first (the window start) and each step read the whole window (700 ms for a step of 18,000 rows); the step now carries only its own lower end (14-25 ms). **Why not FTS5 (now):** the trigram tokenizer is what gives substring search like today's `instr`, and its index is larger than the text it indexes; on a 5 million line table that is a second multi-GB structure on the largest table, an extra write on every `Ingest` (the writer is the part of logs that must not slow down, D-432), a migration that has to index existing rows, and the byte-cap purge (D-200) must delete from it row by row (for external-content tables a delete re-tokenizes the stored text and stale tokens stay if the text differs); substrings under 3 characters (a port, `10.`) fall back to a full scan anyway, so the slow case would remain for short keywords. The honest scan gives the person an answer and the means to go on with no storage cost; FTS5 stays the upgrade if a customer needs "all matches over weeks in under a second". | Why: a customer's log search must not end in an error on a normal-size box; leading log tools tell the person how much was searched instead of failing. Sources (pages opened 2026-11-13): SQLite FTS5 trigram tokenizer, index-size and LIKE fallback below 3 characters, external-content delete caveat (https://www.sqlite.org/fts5.html); Grafana Loki line filters are a "distributed grep" over the selected streams and the answer is to narrow the selector and range, not to index the text (https://grafana.com/docs/loki/latest/query/log_queries/); Elasticsearch returns partial results by default when shards time out, `allow_partial_search_results` (https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/current/search-search.html); Graylog scopes a search by a time frame the person can scroll (https://go2docs.graylog.org/current/making_sense_of_your_log_data/search_your_log_data.html). Not chosen: FTS5 now (above), raising `SearchTimeout` (holds a reader longer for the same wall), a background search job with polling (a new job type and screen for what a cursor does). | 2026-11-13 |
| D-442 | **The NAT64 guard learns the network's own prefix length (RFC 7050) and judges only that layout; when it cannot, it keeps judging every layout.** `nat64Local` (modules/notify/channel/webhook.go, modules/logs/siem_send.go, modules/feeds/dial.go; three identical copies) read an address of 64:ff9b:1::/48 (RFC 8215) in every RFC 6052 layout (/48 /56 /64 /96) and refused it if any reading was forbidden, so a legitimate operator prefix such as `64:ff9b:1:a00::/64` (reads as 10.0.x.x in the /48 layout) or a /64 starting 0x7f (reads as 127.x) was refused for every address. (1) **Learning**: the first time a 64:ff9b:1::/48 address is judged, the box asks the system resolver for the AAAA of `ipv4only.arpa` (2 s limit). An answer inside 64:ff9b:1::/48 whose u octet (byte 8) is zero and that carries 192.0.0.170 or 192.0.0.171 in exactly one layout gives a prefix and its length (`learnNAT64`); answers that are IPv4, outside the /48, ambiguous or without the well-known address are ignored. (2) **Judging**: an address covered by a learned prefix is read in that layout only; an address outside every learned prefix, or nothing learned (no DNS64, lookup failed or timed out), is read in all layouts exactly as before, so the forbidden-IPv4 check is never weaker than the fail-closed reading for any address the learned prefix does not cover. A reading inside 0.0.0.0/8 is dropped as before. (3) **Cache**: 6 hours when something was learned, 10 minutes when not (one lookup per 10 minutes at most, only while 64:ff9b:1::/48 addresses are being judged; the common path never queries). The three copies each keep their own cache. (4) **Data flow**: this is one DNS query for the fixed public name `ipv4only.arpa` to the resolver the box already uses for every host name it resolves (feed, webhook and SIEM names); it carries no customer data, no box identity and no configured name, goes to no new party, and is not a new outgoing data flow, so `PRIVACY.md` and `rules/legal.md` ask for no row and no Settings text. (5) **Trust**: the answer is not authenticated (RFC 7050 section 3.1 says to validate with DNSSEC; the system resolver gives no such guarantee here) and RFC 7050 section 7 warns a forged answer can steer the host, so a forged answer is treated as hostile. IP-literal URLs never touch DNS, so DNS must not be able to weaken the guard: the classes a guard never allows (loopback, link-local, multicast, unspecified, broadcast, cloud metadata) are judged in every layout, learned or not; the learned layout (all learned prefixes that cover the address) only narrows the network-dependent checks (private ranges, the box's own addresses); a learned reading inside 0.0.0.0/8 falls back to every layout. The review's example, a forged `64:ff9b:1:a9fe:a9:fe00:c000:aa` teaching a /96 so that `...:0:1` reads 0.0.0.1, is still refused (metadata reading in the /48 layout). Accepted cost: a legitimate operator prefix whose first byte after the /32 is 0x7f (or another always-forbidden first octet) still reads as loopback in the /48 layout and stays refused. A forger can still make the guard stricter, never looser. (6) **Lookup**: one at a time, not under the cache mutex; a caller that finds a lookup running gets what is known (nothing at first, meaning every layout).
