| D-464 | **One page frame for every main-menu page (S-UI-1; kien beta feedback item 6, 2026-11-13).** Order: `PageHeader` (title about 20 px with the short description on the same line, wrapping under it when there is no room) → optional `KpiStrip` (at most 4 cells: number, label, link; one bordered strip split by rules, not loose cards; only when the number answers the page's question, FRONTEND §3) → `PageTabs` when the page has more than one area: horizontal ARIA tab row, the open tab in `?tab=<id>` (other query parameters kept), an unknown tab or one the role may not see opens the first, one area left draws no row, a tab whose content needs the user carries a red count with a spoken label (tab name "Requests 3 waiting for a decision": it holds the visible text, WCAG 2.5.3); red because the badge is only for work that needs the user now, which keeps FRONTEND's "red = urgent" (a Response request expires 15-30 min after it is sent, so a pending one is urgent), and a count of things that can wait gets no badge. | D-465 | **Box address: Settings → Box network has one "Box address" (a host name or IPv4 address the LAN reaches the box at), default = the management IPv4 vedette-host reports (`state/net`); every link the box makes carries it, and the fixed name `vedette` is never used for a link (S-CORE-8, S-NOT-1, S-RESP-3; kien's N100, beta item 8, 2026-11-13).** (1) **Before**: the appliance starts core with no `-hosts` (`host/ops/quadlet.go`), its self-signed certificate listed `localNames()` first, which holds the fixed name `vedette`, and `baseURL` took the first certificate name that was not loopback, so every notify link (finding, incident, approval `/approve/<token>`, sign-in mail, test message), the block list URL and the agent fallback read `https://vedette:8443`, which nothing on a LAN resolves; URL honey tokens used the box's OS host name and a fixed 8443; `TestBoxNameKeepsVedetteFirstAndTheBaseURL` locked it in and the mocks used the box IP, so no GUI test saw it. Validated at the edge (mock `boxAddressProblem` = Go `checkBoxAddress`): trimmed, lower case, trailing dot dropped; a unicast IPv4 (`unicast4`) or a host name by the NTP rule (`hostName`: RFC 1123 labels, 64 characters, not all-number); a URL, port, path, space, IPv6, loopback, `localhost` or `*.localhost` (RFC 6761: always the machine itself) is 400 `bad_box_address`, so the value can go into a link, a certificate and an install command as is. (3) **Use**: `cmd/vedette` `boxAddr` reads `NetworkHandlers.BoxAddress` (saved, else the management IPv4 through the page's 6 s state cache) for 30 s, keeps the last answer when a read fails, and is dropped by `AddressesChanged` (a save, or an apply/confirm/revert of the management address); `deps.BaseURL` is now `func() string` and notify (`Config.BaseURL`, only how it reaches notify changes: its templates and logic do not), response (block list URL), honeypot (URL token: Box address, else the box IP on 8443, else 409 `no_box_address`, never the host name) and agent-intake (`BoxURL`, now **before** the request's Host: the install commands carry the Box address) read it at every use, so a save applies to the next link without a restart. Without a host (container-only, D-168) the Box address is the first usable `-hosts`/`VEDETTE_HOSTS` entry; with nothing known there is no link and approvals are refused, as on loopback (notify PRE-4). (4) **Certificate and Host**: the self-signed renewer adds the Box address to the certificate (SAN) and re-issues it when it lacks it (a save kicks the renewer, ≤ 10 s); an owner's `-tls-cert` is never touched. The Host allowlist also answers to the Box address in memory (an administrator typed it, like `-hosts`, so it is no DNS-rebinding hole; a DHCP-given host name in a public domain still is not, `defaultAllowed`). `vedette` stays in the certificate and the default allowlist, so old bookmarks keep working; it is just never put in a link. **Changing the address does not break what used the old one (review M1)**: the saved address a change replaces joins `previous` (setting, survives restarts, at most 8), and the box keeps answering to it (Host allowlist, certificate SAN) until an administrator presses "Stop answering to …" (`POST /core/network/box-address/forget`, audited); the page asks before a saved address is replaced and says what keeps using it; the management IP stays always allowed. The page shows the link base the box computes (`link_base`) and says who must put the address in the certificate (`self_signed`); the agent setup says which address the install commands use (no DNS lookup). (5) **Not done**: no IPv6 Box address (the management form is IPv4 only); no port field (the link port is `-listen`'s). | Every top-tier self-hosted product has one explicit "this is my URL" setting used for links and callbacks, and the one that defaults it does so from the detected network address: **Grafana** `root_url`, "the full URL used to access Grafana from a web browser", needed for OAuth callbacks (https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/setup-grafana/configure-grafana/); **GitLab** `external_url`, needed "to display the correct repository clone links", and an IP is allowed (`external_url "http://10.0.0.1"`) (https://docs.gitlab.com/omnibus/settings/configuration/); **Home Assistant** uses the internal URL the user set, else "one detected from the network settings", and raises `NoURLAvailableError` when none fits rather than guess (https://contributors.home-assistant.io/core/integrations/instance-url/) (Vedette: no link rather than a guessed one); **Jenkins** "Jenkins location" URL, "important for proper communication with agents and external tools" (https://www.jenkins.io/doc/book/managing/system-configuration/) (Vedette: the agent install commands use it). | D-466 | **Trap IPs are profiles (S-HP-1; kien beta feedback items 2, 3, 4, 2026-11-13).** (1) One list "Trap IPs" replaces the secondary IP (`hp_config` key `config`, global switches `hp_trap`) and "Decoy personalities" (`hp_decoys`): table `hp_trap_ips` (name, IP, preset, vendor, services, enabled). (6) Form errors sit under their own field (name, IP, services; a form-level alert for the rest); an empty name says "Enter a name"; placeholders read "e.g. …". (8) **Upgrade** (migration 0003, forward only): the secondary IP becomes the first profile (services = the traps that were on; none on → the File server set, switched off); each decoy becomes a profile of its personality's preset with services = the preset's ∩ the traps that were on (empty → the preset's set, switched off); a decoy without a secondary IP is switched off (it never listened), and so is one whose address or whose secondary IP is not in the old core's `applied` record (the secondary IP clashed or the host refused it: the migration cannot see the inventory, B2 review). | D-469 | **Blocklist honesty: a block on an address the list can never publish is refused when it is planned (code `not_publishable`), and the empty Block list says what fills it (S-RESP-3, INV-17; beta feedback item 7, 2026-11-13).** (1) **Before**: the published list already dropped every non-public address (`publishable`, table `notPublishable`, INV-17), but `blocklist_add` on 192.168.x was accepted, approved, reported "Added to the block list … Read back: the entry is present" and never published; no `refused` line was written. (2) **Now**: `planAction` refuses a `blocklist_add` whose address is not publishable with **`not_publishable` (409)**, right after the never-touch check (the gateway or the box still answers `never_touch`), using the same `publishable` table (no new list; the IPv4 documentation blocks stay publishable as INV-17 already says, because the sample data uses them; IPv6 2001:db8::/32 is refused). A new code, not `not_public`: exposure already uses that (400) for the box's own address with another meaning. `planAction` is the one planner of every path, so all refuse the same way and log `refused`: rule runs and manual runs (`fire`), AI proposals (`Propose`), requests from AI plans (`RequestProposal`, and the stored proposal shows the state `not_publishable`, not `tool_unavailable`), AI plans when stored (`savePlan`: `plan_invalid … (not_publishable)`); the simulation shows the error on that step. A fixed (literal) address that is not publishable is refused when the rule is saved or simulated (400 `not_publishable`); a value from the trigger is known only when the rule runs. `carryOut` refuses an older pending item again before it runs (item `failed`, `refused` line), so "Added" is never said for an address that is not published. (3) **A no-op refusal, not a safety refusal (review round 1, M4)**: in a rule only that block action is dropped, with its `refused` line, and the rule's other actions go ahead (a trap rule "block the source + tell me" still sends the message); `never_touch`, `invalid_target` and the other refusals still refuse the whole run. (4) **AI plans**: the plan job offers `blocklist_add` for a finding only when the device's address is publishable (`offeredFor`); `aboutTheDevice` makes every value the device's own address, so for a LAN device the action could only make the whole plan fail and back the finding off. (5) **Old rows**: entries already in `resp_block_entries` on addresses that are not publishable (they were never served) are removed once when the module starts (`dropUnpublishable` in `ensureSeeded`), with one `refused` line and a `response.blocklist.cleanup` audit row giving the count. The publish-time filter stays as the last layer and stays silent: a line per firewall pull (every 5 minutes) would flood the append-only log; spec §5 says so. Mock: the same checks in `engine.ts` (`planAction`, `checkRule`, `fire`; IPv4 rows of the table). (6) **GUI**: the empty Block list says that only approved "block" actions fill it, that only public addresses are published, that the ready-made rule "Known-bad connection: add the destination to the block list" ships off, with a link to the Rules tab (template gallery); the address row stays so the firewall can be set up first. **Why refuse at the producer, loudly**: firewalls take whatever the feed holds (FortiGate's IP threat feed is one IP/range per line, private examples included, no filtering of its own), so the producer must keep the customer's own networks out; pfSense documents blocking private networks only on WAN because on a LAN it "can potentially block required local traffic"; pfBlockerNG's IP suppression drops RFC 1918 and loopback entries from downloaded feeds. Vedette did the filtering already, but silently; a person must learn at plan time that the block will do nothing, and that isolating a LAN device is a device action (blocklist-format §1). Sources: https://docs.fortinet.com/document/fortigate/7.4.9/administration-guide/9463 , https://docs.netgate.com/pfsense/en/latest/interfaces/configure.html , https://forum.netgate.com/post/730480 , https://www.iana.org/assignments/iana-ipv4-special-registry , https://www.iana.org/assignments/iana-ipv6-special-registry | 2026-11-13 |
| D-470 | **The box covers itself: real packages from dpkg, and a person may scan it (kien beta feedback items 9 and 12, 2026-11-13).** (1) **Box packages:** vedette-host gets one read-only endpoint, `GET /v1/state/packages` (host-api §5, host INV-9; no lock, no audit line, over the existing peer-checked socket), which runs one fixed `dpkg-query -W -f=${Package}\t${Version}\t${Architecture}\t${source:Package}\t${db:Status-Status}\n` through the allowlisted runner (no shell, nothing from the request, 8 MiB output bound) and parses its structure fail-closed (a line without 5 fields, an unknown dpkg status, a cut output, a non-zero exit, no installed package or more than 20 000 → 500, never half a list; one installed package whose own name, version or architecture breaks dpkg's rules is left out, counted and logged, so it cannot hide the rest). It keeps the packages whose files are on the box (`installed`, `triggers-awaited`, `triggers-pending`). A package half-way through dpkg (`half-installed`, `unpacked`, `half-configured`: apt running, or an interrupted run) means the list is no snapshot of the box, so the read answers 409 `packages_changing` with no list and core keeps the last good one until a later run (otherwise findings of the packages apt is replacing would close and reopen). Caps: the host sends at most 20 000 packages; core never cuts the mapped list (an osquery agent's snapshot is cut at 5 000 rows, the box's is not), and the inventory stores at most 5 000 items per device, so a longer box list is refused whole and the stored one stays, never a part of the box. core maps the list exactly like an osquery `deb_packages` snapshot (`agentintake.MapDebPackages`: `pkgmap.json`, upstream version) and stores it as the box device's software (source `agent`, confidence 1.0) every hour (job `inventory/box`) and right after a successful OS update (`OSConfig.Installed` wakes the job). A host older than this answers 404 and a failed read changes nothing: the stored list stays, it is never emptied. Findings code is unchanged: the box matches KEV like any device. This finishes D-53 / S-INV-5; until now `Config.Box` was never set, so a real box had no packages while the page said "exact". Container-only: no host, no list, and the page says so. (2) **No osquery on the appliance:** dpkg already gives the exact list with no extra daemon on the box. Enrolling osquery on the box itself is not promised in the GUI until the lab confirms agent-intake sees the box's own address (not podman's gateway) on that connection; the mapping is the same, so the rows would agree (same mapping, so the rows agree). (3) **Self-scan:** `inventory.VulnScanPolicy` refuses the box only when the run is automatic (`explicit=false`: schedules, KEV rescans); a person's pick in Scan now passes the same checks as any device (scope, exclusions, `regular_scan=never`) at the normal rate. In the list the box is `selectable` and `pick_only` with `ScanTarget.box=true`, so "Select all" never ticks it; the scan reason `box` is removed from the list. Discovery is unchanged: `ScanPolicy` (sensor-active nmap device scans) and `ProtectedIPs` (sweeps) still skip the box and every decoy IP, and sensor-active has no person-picked path, so nmap never probes the box. The old block (WP-12 review round 2, PR #66, commit `830c3ad9`) had no D and no recorded reason; its implicit reason, "the box is covered by its own package list", was false on a real box (point 1). (4) **Lock-out check:** scanning the box from its own scan container (`Network=host`) cannot lock an admin out. The sign-in limit of core/auth is per (client address, email), and the public-request limit is per client address, so it only touches requests from the box's own address. The sensor link (8444) checks the client certificate before its per-role rate bucket. Nuclei runs only the CVE templates of the box's open findings, never `dos`/`intrusive`/`fuzz` and never default-login sets. Vedette installs no fail2ban; an OS fail2ban would ban the box's own address only. The honeypot listens only on decoy IPs, which are never targets. | **Why a person may pick it:** the box is a Linux server on the LAN with an exposed web console and SSH; a network view of it is the same evidence a customer wants for any server, and a per-device pick is already Vedette's consent model (D-126). Automatic runs stay off because a sweep of the box's own published ports and decoys would trip its own honeypot and request limits, and the package list covers the box hourly anyway. **Why dpkg and not osquery:** exact and cheap, one fixed read-only command on the root side, no new daemon, no new dependency, no new outbound flow (PRIVACY unchanged). **Sources read 2026-11-13:** Tenable treats the scanner's own host as an ordinary target: "Except in particular circumstances, such as scanning localhost, remote authentication must first be successful before local checks can be enabled" (https://docs.tenable.com/cyber-exposure-studies/vulnerability-management/Content/vuln-assessment-scanning.htm). | D-473 | **Exposure: an administrator's Scan now is the authorization (kien 2026-11-13 via the supervisor; beta item 15; amends D-26, keeps D-5's record).** The separate confirm step (a tick box and `POST /exposure/targets/{id}/commitment`) is gone. The notice text of each version is pinned by a hash test. | D-475 | **OpenCode is the first AI preset; the Add AI profile dialog asks in the order a person thinks (S-AI-1, beta walk item 17).** kien tried to add OpenCode: no preset, "Custom" opened as cloud with that choice last so he hit the https rule, no model list, a blank required name, and the Gemini preset address ended in `/v1beta` while the client adds `/v1beta` again. **Dialog order:** provider → where it runs → key → model → name (auto-filled, editable) → Test → Save; address, API style and the daily token cap sit under **Advanced** (open by default only for Custom). **Preset:** OpenCode Console pay-as-you-go over Chat Completions, base `https://opencode.ai/inference/openai/v1` (the Console documents Chat Completions at `/inference/openai/v1/chat/completions` for GLM, Kimi, MiniMax, DeepSeek, Qwen and Mistral; Anthropic Messages at `/inference/anthropic/v1/messages` and Responses at `/inference/openai/v1/responses` for Claude and GPT), cloud only, `glm-5.3-flash` as the suggestion (USD 0.15 / 0.50 per million tokens in and out, the cheapest chat-completions model that supports tools). It is a dialog preset on kind `custom` with style `openai`: no new kind, no migration; a saved profile is an ordinary Custom profile. Claude, Gemini and GPT through OpenCode are **not** offered: they use other API families and the auth header per family needs a live test with a real key first. Free OpenCode models refuse clients that are not OpenCode, so they are not suggested; OpenCode Go is for coding agents. **Model list:** `POST /ai/profiles/models` (admin, CSRF as every POST) makes the box GET the provider's model endpoint (`{base}/models` for OpenAI style, except on the host `opencode.ai` only, where the family segment drops: `/inference/openai/v1` lists at `/inference/v1/models`, while Groq and Azure list under their chat path; `/v1/models` for Anthropic; `/v1beta/models` for Gemini). It goes through the **same connection guard** as an AI call (own address D-446, forbidden and private-vs-cloud rules at dial time, no redirects, no environment proxy for an internal profile), the same save-time address checks and stored-key rule as Test, 15 s, 1 MiB; the answer is untrusted JSON of which only ids matching the model-name rule are kept, de-duplicated, sorted, at most 300; at most 10 calls a minute per admin (429 `rate_limited`, so it is not a LAN port-scan oracle); the call is audited as `ai.models` with the host, and the profile id when a saved key is used (never the key). The list is a suggestion in a combobox: free text stays possible (a provider whose list call fails, or that lists models the chat style cannot use, still works). The model hint says small and cheap for batch jobs (log digests, CVE news), stronger for explanations, Ask and response plans. PRIVACY.md row 3 and Settings → Privacy gain the list call (a new outgoing GET, carries the key only as the provider's header, no data of yours). **http://:** still allowed only for "Inside your network", now with a visible "not encrypted" warning below the choice; INV-3 and D-446 unchanged. **Gemini:** the preset address is the bare host; the client drops a trailing `/v1beta` from any Gemini base, so profiles saved with the old preset call the right path. | D-480 | **Email user sign-in without a redirect to the box: Microsoft 365 / Outlook.com by device code, Gmail by the customer's own Desktop OAuth client with the loopback address pasted back; app password stays Gmail's default (notify; S-NOT-1; kien 2026-11-13).** (1) **Microsoft** (presets "Microsoft 365 (sign in as the user)" and "Outlook.com"): OAuth 2.0 device authorization grant (RFC 8628) against the customer's own app registration (no project client ID ships): `POST https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant>/oauth2/v2.0/devicecode` with `client_id` and scope `https://outlook.office.com/SMTP.Send offline_access openid profile email`; the dialog shows the user code and `https://microsoft.com/devicelogin` (a verification address on any other host is replaced by that one); the box asks the token endpoint (`grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code`) only when the admin's page checks and never before Microsoft's `interval` (`slow_down` adds 5 s, RFC 8628 3.5); states waiting / signed in as <mailbox> / expired (`expired_token`, `bad_verification_code`, or 15 minutes) / declined (`authorization_declined`). Tenant: a GUID, a domain, `organizations`, or `consumers` (the Outlook.com preset; its SMTP server is `smtp-mail.outlook.com:587`). The app needs **Allow public client flows** and the delegated Microsoft Graph permission **SMTP.Send** (no admin consent needed, personal accounts may consent); the guide in the dialog says so. The mailbox is read from the id_token Microsoft returns with the tokens (`preferred_username`, else `email`); it came straight from the token endpoint over TLS, so the claims are read without a signature check (OpenID Connect Core 3.1.3.7). (2) **Google** (preset "Gmail (sign in with your own Google client)"): the customer's own **Desktop app** OAuth client (client ID and secret typed in; no project secret ships); consent address `https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth` with `redirect_uri=http://127.0.0.1:<random port 49152-65535>`, PKCE S256, a 256-bit `state`, `access_type=offline`, `prompt=consent`, scope `https://mail.google.com/ openid email`. The admin approves; the browser fails to load the loopback address; the admin pastes that whole address. The pasted text is untrusted: at most 4096 characters, parsed as a URL, only `http` on `127.0.0.1` or `localhost` at this sign-in's port with an empty path, the `state` compared in constant time, then only `code` (printable, ≤ 2048) and `error` are read; an `error` means declined. The code is exchanged with the verifier at `https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token`. The guide tells the admin to publish the app (In production): Google ends the sign-ins of an External app in Testing after 7 days. (3) **Secrets**: the refresh token (and Google's client secret) is the channel secret, JSON, through `core/secrets`; the browser never sees it: the start and check routes keep the sign-in in memory (15 minutes, one per admin, at most 8, only the admin who started it can read or save it) and the save sends only its id; SaveChannel takes it once, sets the mailbox that signed in as the username, and refuses a sign-in for another provider, client or tenant. The access token is refreshed before expiry (D-449's cache); a refresh token Microsoft rotates is kept at once in memory and written back to the saved channel on a goroutine (a send can run inside another module's write transaction), only if the saved secret is still the one the sender started with; Microsoft does not revoke the previous refresh token, so a failed write loses nothing. `invalid_grant` on a refresh says to sign in again (Google adds the 7-day Testing cause). The SMTP side is D-449's: XOAUTH2, else OAUTHBEARER, only after TLS, only to the preset's own server. (4) **Kept**: the app-only Microsoft 365 preset (client credentials, D-449) as the second Microsoft option, the Workspace service account as the other Google option, and the Gmail app password as Gmail's default preset. New routes `POST /notify/email-signin`, `POST /notify/email-signin/{id}` (admin); new codes `bad_state`, `signin_refused`. | Microsoft device code: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/v2-oauth2-device-code ; public client flows: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/scenario-desktop-app-configuration ; SMTP OAuth (Microsoft 365 and Outlook.com, `https://outlook.office.com/SMTP.Send`, device code supported): https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/exchange/client-developer/legacy-protocols/how-to-authenticate-an-imap-pop-smtp-application-by-using-oauth ; SMTP.Send in Microsoft Graph permissions: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/permissions-reference ; refresh tokens replace themselves on each use, the old one is not revoked: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/refresh-tokens ; OIDC scopes with other scopes: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/scopes-oidc ; Outlook.com SMTP: https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/pop-imap-and-smtp-settings-for-outlook-com-d088b986-291d-42b8-9564-9c414e2aa040 ; RFC 8628. Google installed apps (loopback IP redirect, PKCE, Desktop apps are public clients): https://developers.google.com/identity/protocols/oauth2/native-app , loopback still supported for desktop apps: https://developers.google.com/identity/protocols/oauth2/resources/loopback-migration , 7-day Testing expiry and refresh token limits: https://developers.google.com/identity/protocols/oauth2#expiration , unverified apps for personal use: https://support.google.com/cloud/answer/13464323 , https://support.google.com/cloud/answer/15549945 ; RFC 7636. rclone remote setup (`rclone authorize` on a machine with a browser, copy the config, or an SSH tunnel to port 53682): https://rclone.org/remote_setup/ ; Mutt's mutt_oauth2.py (authcode, localhostauthcode, devicecode; the user's own client ID, Microsoft needs public client flows): https://github.com/muttmua/mutt/blob/master/contrib/mutt_oauth2.py.README ; msmtp (XOAUTH2/OAUTHBEARER with a token from an outside helper via passwordeval): https://marlam.de/msmtp/msmtp.html ; getmail6 (own Desktop client for Gmail, own app registration for Microsoft 365): https://github.com/getmail6/getmail6/blob/master/docs/getmailrc-examples ; Thunderbird (built-in client IDs, browser sign-in on the same machine): https://source-docs.thunderbird.net/en/latest/backend/oauth.html . | D-481 | **An AI call says what really happened, and its answer has room to be whole (beta 0.1.0-beta.1, kien: Explain, mitigation and Ask all failed on Claude Haiku 5.5 with "No AI profile is assigned"; Ask feedback item 19).** (1) **Output limits** sized for the answer plus what the model thinks first (Haiku 5.5 thinks by default and the thinking counts toward `max_tokens`; OpenAI reasoning and Gemini thinking tokens count the same way): explain-finding (CVE and finding brief) and mitigation-config 6,000 (answer about 1,000), ask-my-data 6,000 a turn (answer about 800), cve-news 4,000 (answer about 600), log-digest 8,000 at med/max and 4,000 at min (answer up to about 2,500), weekly-report and pdpl-assessment 4,000 (about 1,200), response-plan 6,000 (about 1,500). The meter still counts real usage, the per-day caps stay; the limit only sets the hold of a call in flight. (2) **A cut answer** (provider stop reason `max_tokens`) is sent once more to the same profile with twice the limit, at most 16,000 (`MaxAnswerTokens`), held against the caps and checked against the privacy rule like any request, with **twice the call timeout** (180 s by default; chosen over capping the retry's limit to fit 90 s, because the speed of a slow or local model is not known in advance; the caller's context, such as Ask's 2 minutes, still bounds it); both answers' tokens count. Cut again: 502 `ai_cut_off` "The AI's answer was cut off at the output limit (N tokens)…", never the format message. A cap that leaves no room for the retry is 429 `daily_cap` that says the answer was cut and which cap ran out; a provider failure of the retry is that failure's own code. A tool-loop turn cut at the limit runs none of its tool calls. (3) **The stop reason** of the last answer is kept in `ai_activity.stop` and a sent retry in `ai_activity.retried` (migration 0008; outside the hash like `outcome`), so a limit that is too small shows in the log. (4) **One code per failure**: `ai_unavailable` 409 only when the AI cannot be used (module off, no profile, none assigned, privacy rule, skill off, no tool support); `blocked_by_hook` 409 (names the step: the question, the data from a named source, or the answer); `ai_cut_off` 502; `ai_bad_format` 502 (also an Ask loop that never answers); `provider_error` 502 with the profile, kind, HTTP status and the provider's own words, scrubbed of anything key-shaped and cut to 200 characters (this replaces "kind only" for job calls; the connection test keeps its own sentences); `unreachable` 502 when every request could not reach the provider; `ai_timeout` 504 when every request or the question ran out of time; `daily_cap` 429 unchanged. `mitigation` passes the ai module's error on as it is (it replaced every one with "No AI profile is assigned"). Replaces D-148 (2). (5) **Structured output** was already asked of every job with a schema on all three providers (Anthropic `output_config.format` json_schema, OpenAI `response_format` json_schema strict, Gemini `responseJsonSchema`); forced `tool_choice` is not used: it is a 400 on Claude Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Fable 5.1. The tool loop still asks for JSON in its task (D-223). (6) **Ask hooks name their step** (`hooks[].step` question, tool_call, tool_result, answer, and `tool`): only a stopped question reads "The AI was not asked"; a held-back tool result says which tool and what kind of data, and the AI's answer is shown; the page says an administrator can adjust the hooks. (7) **The ID-number detector** blanks the forms the box's own data is full of before it reads digit runs: a link's scheme, host and path segments (never its userinfo, query string or fragment, nor a path segment that is only 9 or 12 digits: https://x.vn/u/079201234567), UUIDs, record ids (`dev-…`), CVE ids written with `CVE-`, dates and timestamps, hashes and long hex ids with a letter a-f (never one starting with `cccd`), Cisco MAC addresses with a hex letter, AS numbers written as one word (`AS13335`); addresses were already blanked. A bare 2023-36844 and an all-digit 0790.1234.5678 stay ID-shaped. **After an ID label** (read on the text with addresses and UUIDs blanked, before any other form; `/` and `@` count as separators) a 9- or 12-digit number in one group or in groups of three or more is blocked: after a strong label (CCCD, CMND, căn cước, chứng minh, số định danh, hộ chiếu/passport, with or without diacritics) whatever letters it is glued to, after the weak label "ID" only when it ends at a word boundary (so `Request ID <UUID>` and `build id 10.0.19045.3693` pass and a hash id after "id" is not read as a person's ID; a trailing boundary for strong labels too would have let `CMND 123456789abcdef0` through again), and after a passport label a Vietnamese passport number (a letter and 7 digits) too; without the label that shape is a part number. Tightened after two rounds of the Opus review, whose probes (`CCCD079201234567`, `CMND 2012-34567`, `CMND AS 201234567`, an ID in a link's query, path or userinfo, `CMND AS201234567`, UUIDs after "id") are in the tests. Known cost: a vendor knowledge-base link whose path segment is exactly 9 or 12 digits (Salesforce article numbers such as /s/article/000087042) now reads as an ID. (8) The inventory tool also returns first seen, how the device was added and which source saw it (never its notes); PRIVACY.md flow 3 says so. | Anthropic: `max_tokens` caps the whole output including thinking, and `stop_reason: "max_tokens"` means the answer was cut and must be retried or continued (https://docs.anthropic.com/en/api/handling-stop-reasons, https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/extended-thinking); structured outputs constrain the format but not the length (https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/structured-outputs). | D-487 | **Repeated failed logins raise an incident from day 1 (S-LOG-1, walk finding W1-22).** A customer sent 3 × "Failed password for invalid user admin from 45.155.205.233" and nothing was raised: the signature path never repeats one signature (every account name is its own), and the anomaly job waits for a 7-day baseline and a 24 h warm-up. New rule in `modules/logs/authfail.go`, fed by the lines the counters already read (the remote address of D-210, so never the log sender or the box): **5 failed attempts from one remote address within 10 minutes on one source = one `logs.anomaly.detected` event** (target `auth:<address>`, notify opens a `log_anomaly` incident), naming the source, address, count, the account names tried (at most 5, plain text, 32 characters each) and what to do. Lines read: sshd "Failed password for", "Invalid user", PAM "authentication failure"; Windows 4625 (and 4624 as the success). sshd writes up to three lines per attempt, so an attempt is the largest of the three counts, not their sum. Dedupe: one incident per (source, address) per hour; a login "Accepted …"/4624 from the same address after failures raises severity to high (the first incident when the acceptance came before the threshold, else a second incident `auth:<address> accepted`). A LAN address counts and the text says "on your own network". Bounds: 2048 pairs followed (new pairs ignored while full), 32 timestamps per class, 20 incidents an hour, state in memory (a restart forgets at most 10 minutes). Thresholds: fail2ban's default is maxretry 5 / findtime 10m (the number a Linux admin already expects); Wazuh rules 5710/5712 ("sshd brute force") fire at frequency 8 in 120 s, a tighter window for an active attack; CrowdSec's `ssh-bf` scenario leaks one failure per 10 s with capacity 5 (about 5 in under a minute, slower attackers drain); Elastic's prebuilt "Potential SSH Brute Force Detected" and Graylog's authentication-failure-count alerts use a count per source address over minutes. We take 5 in 10 minutes: low enough that a customer testing with 5-6 wrong logins sees it, and wide enough to catch a slow guesser that a 2-minute window misses; a customer's own typos (1 to 3) stay quiet. Hardening after review: a line counts only when the syslog program is sshd/sshd-session (PAM "authentication failure" also from login, su, sudo) and the phrase starts the message, or by a shipped Windows event id; the words inside a web log or an account name never count. The incident that says a login was accepted is never cut by the 20-an-hour budget (medium ones are, and a cut one opens again at its next failure); a table that is full evicts the oldest pair that never opened an incident; such pairs go after 10 minutes; IPv6 counts per /64 (sshguard does the same); any incident with an accepted login has the target `auth:<address> accepted`. Not done: a login that succeeds on the 5th try after 4 failures raises nothing (the threshold rule's limit: the incident opens at the 5th failure, and an acceptance only escalates after it); correlation is within one log source only; account names are plain text but some clients may render a name as a link; Windows only counts when the profile finds the address (Source Network Address); FortiGate admin-login failures are not read (their lines carry no "from" the same way); no blocking (Vedette is not inline). Two small engine additions, both data-driven: `conn_patterns` (anchored whole-line readers with a `blocked` flag; the "exactly one `->`" guard of `conn_pattern` is MikroTik-specific) and `apps` (a profile reads only lines of the listed syslog programs: filterlog, kernel). Anti-framing: every pattern starts with `^`, every field before the addresses is a strict class that excludes the comma, text the user wrote (URL, user name, rule or ACL name, User-Agent) comes after the addresses or inside quotes the kv reader treats as one value; lines of another program, text in front of the record, a second record inside a field, inbound or reversed direction, private destinations and IPv6 make no connection (`TestFirewallProfilesInjection`, `TestFirewallProfilesRefuse`). A Linux host keeps the D-487 failed-login path: sshd lines are not read by the profile (`apps`), so the generic remote reader still finds the address (`TestLinuxKindsKeepTheirLoginLines`). Not done: Draytek, Zyxel, WatchGuard (formats not documented well enough or not cheap), UniFi switches/APs (controller logs, not firewall), IPv6, ASA inbound, SonicWall and Cisco FTD denies. Sources: pfSense raw filter log format (https://docs.netgate.com/pfsense/en/latest/monitoring/logs/raw-filter-format.html), Cisco ASA syslog messages 302013, 302015, 106023, 106100 (https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/td/docs/security/asa/syslog/asa-syslog.html), PAN-OS traffic log fields (https://docs.paloaltonetworks.com/pan-os/11-0/pan-os-admin/monitoring/use-syslog-for-monitoring/syslog-field-descriptions/traffic-log-fields), Sophos Firewall syslog log fields (https://docs.sophos.com/nsg/sophos-firewall/ - Log viewer and syslog guide), SonicOS log events reference (https://www.sonicwall.com/support/technical-documentation/), UFW and netfilter LOG (https://help.ubuntu.com/community/UFW), EdgeOS firewall logging prefixes. Top-tier check: Wazuh and Elastic integrations ship per-vendor decoders for the same formats (https://github.com/wazuh/wazuh/tree/master/ruleset/decoders, https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/integrations). Review round (Opus): (1) parse3164 now takes a first token shaped `tag[pid]:` or `tag:` as the program, not the host, because pfSense's default BSD lines carry no hostname and the `apps` gate rejected every line; (2) the `iptables` profile also requires syslog facility kern (`facilities: [0]`), so `logger -t kernel` from a user process cannot frame a device; (3) replies are no connection: pfSense TCP needs flags `S` (with E/W), ICMP is not read, UDP is; Sophos needs log_component Firewall Rule (Firewall) or HTTP/DNS (Content Filtering), so Invalid Traffic, Local ACL and DoS Attack are not read; (4) SonicWall accepts single-quoted values and refuses a line with a second ` src=` or ` dst=` (`conn_refuse`); (5) `conn_patterns` are compiled as `^(?:...)`, `conn_blocked` means any listed key holding a listed value (Sophos: status Deny/Drop or log_subtype Denied). Caveat on sources: the field layouts of Sophos, SonicWall and Cisco ASA were built from documentation as remembered and are not verified against device output; pfSense (action field 7, direction 8, source 19, destination 20) was checked against https://docs.netgate.com/pfsense/en/latest/monitoring/logs/raw-filter-format.html and PAN-OS (source 8, destination 9, action 31) against the PAN-OS 11.1 traffic log fields page. | 2026-11-13 |
| D-490 | **The weekly report says what to DO this week, with the fixed version, and what happened (S-REP-1, customer walk 1 follow-up to D-485/D-487/D-488).** Page 1 and the email gave a product and a count ("Update or apply the vendor's temporary fix to FortiGate"), not the step a person takes. Now (1) **Top risks are lines of work, not products**: open findings are grouped per device and product (the unit of an upgrade), and groups that need the same action merge (same product, same fixed release), so one upgrade that closes several CVEs is one line: "Upgrade FortiGate (FortiOS) on FortiGate-HQ from 7.4.1 to 7.4.3 or later — fixes 3 exploited vulnerabilities" (several devices: "Upgrade Apache to 2.4.52 or later on web-1 and 2 more — fixes 3 exploited vulnerabilities"; some findings of the line not closed by it: "fixes 2 of 3"). The release is `findings.FixedInFor` (D-488, NVD ranges) read through the `reports.Remedies` port wired in `cmd/vedette/reports.go`, never recomputed in reports; the release is the nearest end bound ABOVE the device's version, taken from every range of every finding of the same installed software on the device (a software row, not CISA's product name: one phone's CVEs carry several names), that is outside the affected range of all of them (`findings.FixedInForAll`; golden: iOS 18.2 -> 26.7.1, FortiOS 7.2.5 -> 7.4.11), never the highest of the per-finding fixes (26.3 fixes one iOS CVE and is inside the range of another); "fixes N of M" counts only the findings the release closes, and when no release in NVD's ranges clears them all the line says so ("NVD names no single release that fixes all N") and sends to the vendor advisory; a distribution caveat ("if you installed it from Ubuntu's packages, install its security updates instead") is carried. Fallbacks stay honest and are the words the page already had: a distribution package -> install the distribution's security updates; NVD names no fixed release (only a last affected version) -> check the vendor advisory and use the vendor's temporary fix; confirmed but no range -> update or apply the vendor's temporary fix; version unknown -> check the version to confirm or rule out. The same sentence is `TopRisk.action` (page) and `ActionItem.text` (to-do list, email). Ranking is unchanged and by product (confirmed first, worst severity, most open findings over all devices, name): a product whose devices need different steps gets one slot, the biggest step, and "N more devices need another step"; fixed releases are read only for the products the page names. (2) **"What happened this week"** from notify incidents through the `reports.Incidents` port (never notify tables; off when notify is off, then the section and the "incidents" source are absent): counts per kind (`notify.IncidentsSince`, in SQL, so a busy week is counted whole and not cut at the 500 of the list) of the incidents last seen in the week (honeypot touches, failed-login attacks from D-487, **logins ACCEPTED after failed attempts**, connections to known-bad addresses, other log anomalies; new-device incidents are left out because the Devices count says them), one sentence for page and email, and up to three lines ordered accepted login, trap, failed logins, bad connection, then severity and recency. (3) **The email leads with the work**: subject "Weekly report: N things to do this week, M open findings"; first the incident sentence and its lines, then the first action as "What to do first", then the other actions, then the figures and the link to /reports (the notify mail layout puts "What to do first" after the opening text). Page heading "To do next week" becomes "To do this week": the report goes out on the day the week starts. Old reports (no `action`, `text`, `happened`) still open. A login accepted before the failure threshold now has the accepted title ("A login from X was ACCEPTED after N failed attempts on <source>", authfail.go), and a "failed logins" incident of severity high counts as accepted. Not done: the failed-login and accepted-login incidents are told apart by the title logs writes (notify's API row has no target); a change of those sentences breaks the split (the incident then counts under "other unusual log items"; `TestIncidentsSinceCountsEveryClassBeyondTheListCap` pins it). Sources: Rapid7 InsightVM "Top Remediations" report (https://docs.rapid7.com/insightvm/creating-reports/), Tenable "Remediation Summary" / solutions view (https://docs.tenable.com/vulnerability-management/Content/Explore/Solutions.htm), Qualys "Patch Report" (https://docs.qualys.com/en/vm/latest/reports/patch_report.htm): all list one line per patch or solution with the vulnerabilities it fixes, ranked by how many it closes or by risk, which is the line shape chosen here. | 2026-11-13 |
| D-491 | **Telegram "Find my chat" fills the Chat ID (S-NOT-1, kien 2026-11-13).** Setting up Telegram asked the customer to open `https://api.telegram.org/bot<TOKEN>/getUpdates` in a browser and read JSON; now a **Find my chat** button under Chat ID does it: the customer types the Bot token, sends any message to the bot (or adds it to a group), presses the button and picks the chat (private chats by name and @username, groups by title; newest first, at most 10, one row per chat). Endpoint `POST /notify/telegram/chats` (admin, CSRF like the other channel routes): token in the body, or the saved channel's sealed token when the body is empty (never sent to the browser); one `getUpdates` call through the existing Telegram bot client (fixed `api.telegram.org`, no redirects, 10 s deadline, 1 MiB cap). **It must not eat updates the approval buttons need**: Telegram only confirms updates when a later `getUpdates` carries an `offset` above their `update_id` ([Bot API getUpdates](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#getupdates)), so the call sends no `offset` (nothing is confirmed), `limit=100`, `timeout=0`. It also names `allowed_updates` (message, edited_message, channel_post, my_chat_member) because Telegram keeps the last list given: the approval poller sets `callback_query` only on each call and so re-sets its own list. `my_chat_member` makes a group show up as soon as the bot is added, before anyone posts (a bot in privacy mode sees only commands and mentions in a group). **When the box itself long-polls this bot** (channel on, approvals on, numeric chat, same bot id) the box is the one reader, and a second `getUpdates` would end its poll with 409 and change its update list: the button answers 409 `telegram_busy` with the steps (switch approvals off and save, press the button, switch them on; or type the Chat ID); the poller's own updates are not reused because it asks for button presses only, so they never hold a chat. Telegram's own 409 (a webhook is set, or other software reads the bot) gives the same code with a message for that case; 401 (and 404, how Telegram answers a malformed token) → 400 `bad_token` "The bot token is not valid", shown under the token field; any other failure → 502 `telegram_failed`; no message yet is a 200 with an empty list and the UI says what to do (not an error). Untrusted input: the answer is size-capped and decoded fail-closed; only `chat.id` (a number as written, accepted by the channel's own Chat ID rule), the chat type (private, group, supergroup, channel) and the title, first and last name and username (names cleaned to one line, bidi and control characters dropped, 64 characters; a username must match Telegram's form) are returned; the token is in no log and no error. **No new outgoing destination**: the call goes to `api.telegram.org`, already flow 5 in PRIVACY.md (the bot token already goes there on every send and poll); no field was added to any payload. Chosen over reading the poller's updates (they hold no chats) and over a `setWebhook`/`deleteWebhook` dance (it would change the bot's configuration). **Limits, stated:** without an `offset` Telegram returns the oldest 100 waiting updates, so a very busy group can hide the newest chat from the list (the manual `getUpdates` path remains in the hint). `allowed_updates` also lists `callback_query`, so an approval poller started later loses nothing. The filter is stored by Telegram: a message sent while approvals had it at button presses only was never kept, so the first empty answer for a bot (`fresh: true`, remembered in memory per bot id) tells the customer to send the message again now. The busy guard uses the poller's real condition (`Decisions` wired, channel on, approvals on, numeric chat, same bot id); right after approvals are switched off, the poller's last in-flight long poll can still end this call with 409 `telegram_busy` for up to its 25 s wait: press the button again. Errors use lookup wording (429: "Telegram asked to wait. Try again in a minute."; an answer that is not ok or not readable: "Telegram's answer could not be used…"). Sources: Uptime Kuma's Telegram notification "Auto Get" button, which calls `getUpdates` with the typed token and lists the chats found (https://github.com/louislam/uptime-kuma/blob/master/src/components/notifications/Telegram.vue); Telegram Bot API `getUpdates` (offset confirmation, `allowed_updates` persistence, 409 when a webhook is set or another `getUpdates` runs) (https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#getupdates). | 2026-11-13 |
| D-492 | **External exposure names the device that probably answers the open ports, and what is exploited on it (S-EXP-1, walk finding W1-23).** The page listed "SIP 5060, HTTPS 10443" but never tied them to a device, though in a small business the box on the public IP is almost always the gateway or firewall itself (a FortiGate SSL-VPN on 10443 is the CVE-2024-21762 class), whose exploited CVEs Vedette already holds as findings. `GET /exposure/targets` gains `gateway` (null when no IP target has open ports): `{ip, device_id, name, open_exploited}`. The gateway is the LAN default route vedette-host reports (the same read the logs and response wiring use), matched by IP to an inventory device; `open_exploited` is that device's open findings (confirmed or suspected, every finding is a KEV match). Exposure sees a narrow port (`Gateway`, `modules/exposure/ports.go`) wired in `cmd/vedette/exposuregateway.go`; it reads no other module's tables. Wording never claims the port is on the gateway: "answered by your gateway X (ip), or a device it forwards them to" (NAT port-forwards exist). Honest cases: gateway unknown (no host, or the host cannot read it) says Vedette cannot tell which device answers; gateway not in the device list says so; a gateway with no open findings says Vedette knows of none, not that it is safe. Only the box's own IP targets count, not the subdomains of a domain (those often point at a hosting provider). Device names are untrusted labels: control characters removed and cut to 80 characters on the server, rendered as text. Not done here (deferred): the "reachable from the Internet" mark on those findings and sorting them first, which needs the findings module to learn the gateway device; the link to the device's findings already puts them one click away. Sources: Tenable VPR and Rapid7 Active Risk both raise a vulnerability's priority when the asset is internet-facing (https://www.tenable.com/blog/what-is-vulnerability-priority-rating-vpr, https://docs.rapid7.com/insightvm/active-risk/); CISA BOD 22-01 and the KEV catalog guidance put exploited vulnerabilities on internet-facing systems first (https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/directives/bod-22-01-reducing-significant-risk-known-exploited-vulnerabilities); Censys and Shodan attack-surface products link an exposed service to the known vulnerabilities of its product (https://censys.com/platform/attack-surface-management/, https://www.shodan.io/). | 2026-11-13 |
| D-493 | **"Scan now" returns at once with a run; the scan goes on in the background (S-EXP-1, prerequisite of the nmap/nuclei/ZAP slices of `docs/plans/2026-11-13-exposure-real-vulns.md`).** Today `POST /exposure/targets/{id}/scan` holds the browser for up to 5 minutes, and the next slices add minutes more (service-version probes, template scans, ZAP): a request that long dies at a proxy or a tab close and the person cannot see where the scan is. The gate is unchanged and still answers synchronously with today's errors (not verified, expired, TXT missing, commitment, `ip_not_current`, 409 `busy`, 429 `rate_limited`, 501, 409 `module_off`). When it passes, the answer is **202 `ScanRun {id, target_id, target_value, by, started_at, finished_at, status, phase, snapshot_id, error}`** and the scan runs in a goroutine the Service owns (context of the Service, not of the request; the runner's 5-minute cap stays). `GET /exposure/scan` returns the run that runs now or the last one (`status` running/done/failed/stopped, `error {code, message}` with the same codes and texts as before, `snapshot_id` when done; `null` before the first run); `POST /exposure/scan/stop` (operator) cancels it (nothing saved, 409 `not_running` when none runs). Phases are the steps `execute` really does: queued, probing, saving, done. The run lives in memory only (ponytail: one run at a time, no table; after a restart there is no run, exactly as `lastScan` forgets): the snapshot, the `exposure.snapshot.created` event, the `new_port` bridge and the one `exposure.scan` audit row per attempt are unchanged, and a stop writes `stopped by <who>`. Switching the module off cancels a running scan (`Registry.OnChange`, SYS-5). The page shows a progress row that polls every 2 s only while a run is running. **Top-tier reference:** every scanner that outlives a request does the same: GitHub Actions' "create a workflow dispatch" and "re-run" return 202/201 with a run id that `GET .../runs/{id}` reports as `status`/`conclusion` ([docs](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/actions/workflow-runs)); Tenable's `POST /scans/{id}/launch` returns a `scan_uuid` and the client polls the scan status ([Tenable developer docs](https://developer.tenable.com/)); Detectify's scan-profile API starts a scan and returns its status resource for polling ([Detectify API](https://developer.detectify.com/)). Not chosen: a long-lived request with server-sent events (a second protocol, breaks at proxies, still dies with the tab); a persisted run table (a restart already forgets the 10-minute limit, and a scan that dies with the process has nothing to resume). | 2026-11-13 |
| D-494 | **Greenbone (OpenVAS) stays optional and off; enabling needs 8 GiB RAM and 60 GB free disk; its results never override version-based findings (item 24 slice d, from the 2026-11-13 N100 trial).** Measured on the N100 (4 cores, 7 GB) next to a running Vedette: images 9.2 GB + feed volumes 41 GB ≈ 50 GB disk; first feed import ~2 h with a RAM peak of ~4 GB used plus ~2 GB swap; ~2 GB during a scan; an unauthenticated "Full and fast" scan of lab .181 took 3 min 22 s and found 0 CVEs (3 low hardening notes), while Vedette's agent path found 4 real exploited CVEs on the same host, because Ubuntu backports fixes and a banner check cannot see them. So the preflight follows Greenbone's own recommended sizing (8 GB RAM, 60 GB disk), not the earlier 16 GiB guess (the 7 GB N100 copes but swaps, so it is refused); the feed import is a visible phase; results are imported as "scanner: Greenbone" findings with QoD ≥ 70 and never close or hide a version-based finding; uninstall leaves the Greenbone project alone. It runs as Greenbone's unmodified compose project (separate processes, GPL/AGPL not embedded, rules/legal.md). Value is for hosts without an agent (appliances, Windows without osquery, web apps); the next trial is Windows .49 and a web app. Sources: Greenbone Community Containers hardware requirements (https://greenbone.github.io/docs/latest/22.4/container/index.html), Tenable and Rapid7 both treat unauthenticated network scans as lower-confidence than credentialed or agent checks (https://docs.tenable.com/nessus/Content/CredentialedChecks.htm, https://docs.rapid7.com/insightvm/scan-credentials/); trial log ~/vedette-wt/greenbone-trial.md (supervisor). | 2026-11-13 |
| D-495 | **A finding that becomes more serious, or that Vedette reopens by itself, is told like a new one (S-ALERT-1, S-LOG-3).** After D-500/D-530 a re-match can raise an open finding's severity (findings emits it when the basis becomes a stronger one, in practice product to version with the installed version inside the NVD range, and the severity of that match is higher) or reopen one Vedette had closed as not affected, but findings emitted only `severity_raised` / `status_changed reason=matches_again` and nobody listened: a finding that just became critical stayed silent in Telegram, email, Zalo and the SIEM. notify now turns `findings.finding.severity_raised` into a vulnerability notice `nt-<finding>-raised-<to_severity>` ("CVE-… on NAS-01 is now critical (was medium)" plus a reason from `basis`: the installed version is in the affected range, otherwise "stronger evidence that this device is affected"; nothing the event lacks) and `status_changed` with `reason=matches_again` into `nt-<finding>-reopened-<YYYYMMDD, UTC>` (one per day, so a version flapping between scans does not message each time) ("Vedette reopened CVE-… on NAS-01: it matches again"). Both go through the same path as a new finding (channel severity floor, quiet hours, grouping/digest, "needs a matched device"); in a digest the line says what changed. Putting the new severity in the id makes one raise one notice and a later raise to a higher level a new one; a raise to a level already told is not repeated (the id is unique). A re-match that both reopens a finding and raises its basis emits only the reopening (findings does not emit severity_raised then), so the customer gets one notice. Not sent in the first CISA baseline (D-78). logs forwards `finding.severity_raised` to the SIEM with the new severity as the record severity and fields `id`, `asset_id`, `cve`, `basis`, `from_severity`, `to_severity`; `finding.status_changed` gains `reason`. No new data leaves the box: same channels and SIEM the customer configured, so no PRIVACY.md change. Sources: Dependabot alerts re-notify when an advisory's severity is updated (https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/dependabot/dependabot-alerts/about-dependabot-alerts); Snyk notifies on priority-score and severity changes of an existing issue (https://docs.snyk.io/manage-risk/prioritize-issues-for-fixing/priority-score); Tenable VPR changes and re-opened findings ("Resurfaced") are surfaced as new activity (https://docs.tenable.com/vulnerability-management/Content/Explore/Findings/Vulnerabilities.htm). | 2026-11-13 |
| D-496 | **A trap incident's "Times" is the number of connections the trap saw, read from the honeypot when the page is built (S-HP-1, walk 5 finding M5-190).** A second connection from the same source to the same trap inside the fold window raises `hp_hits.conn_count` and adds a line to the hit but emits no event (honeypot INV-17), so notify's own count (one per `honeypot.hit.created`) stayed 1 and the incident showed "Times 1x". Notify now has a narrow optional port `Config.Hits` (`HitConnections(ctx, []HitRef{ID, At})`, `modules/notify/types.go`), wired in `cmd/vedette/notify.go` over the honeypot's existing public read that carries `conn_count` (`ExportHits`, one window of exactly the hit's time per hit; no other read returns it and notify reads no honeypot table). `GET /notify/incidents` and `/notify/incidents/{id}` show `count + (conn_count - 1)` for a trap incident (the hit its link names counts its connections, not once; each later hit of the same incident is still one). One export per distinct hit time, streamed. Honeypot off, port nil, or a read error: notify's own count, one log line, no error to the page. The weekly report counts incidents, not times, so it is unchanged. Why not an event: `honeypot.hit.updated {id, conn_count}` was asked of the honeypot owner and does not exist yet; reading at render needs nothing from them and shows the right number now. Upgrade path (`ponytail:` at the port): when that event exists, notify keeps the count itself and the port goes. Limit: connections folded into a later hit of the same incident are not counted (only the hit the link names is read). Sources: top-tier alert tools (PagerDuty, Opsgenie, Datadog) show the number of occurrences folded into one alert as the alert's count, so the fold must not hide the repeats. |
| D-497 | **A device deleted in Devices leaves the open new-device incidents (W6-3, S-ALERT; Trưởng's known limit).** The first-discovery summary "N devices found on your network" kept listing (and counting) a device after it was deleted, and the device's own "A new unknown device appeared" incident stayed open with nothing left to approve. notify now listens to `inventory.asset.deleted {asset_id}`: an open summary drops the device from its list and count (resolved when none is left), the device's own open incident is resolved by `system` with the reason in its note and one audit row; no message is sent. Resolved incidents and other kinds (trap hits, findings) keep the device: they are a record of what happened. Sources: Microsoft Defender XDR resolves an alert automatically when its entity is removed or the condition no longer applies ("resolved by system") and keeps the alert history (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-xdr/manage-incidents), UniFi and Fing drop a forgotten device from the client lists but keep past events. | 2026-11-13 |
| D-498 | **A person can accept the risk of a finding until a date; the acceptance ends by itself and the finding reopens (kien's N100 beta list item 14; S-MIT-1).** (1) **Rule** (`modules/findings`): new closed status `risk_accepted`, action `accept_risk` on `POST /findings/{id}/status` and the bulk `POST /findings/status`, with a note (≥ 3 characters, like false positive) and an `until` date from tomorrow to 365 days ahead (the server measures in UTC days and allows one day either side so a person's local "tomorrow" and "365 days" always pass; otherwise 400 `bad_until`). Stored in `fnd_finding.accepted_until` (migration `0005`, a rebuild of `fnd_finding` and `fnd_finding_history` with foreign keys off so the history and mitigation rows that cascade from a finding survive). History `risk_accepted` "<note> (until 12 Feb 2027)"; event `status_changed`. (2) **Expiry** (INV-13): the hourly reconcile job reopens every acceptance once its last day has ended everywhere on Earth (`findings.AcceptanceEnds`: the next day 12:00 UTC, the end of the day at UTC−12; the box has no customer time zone, and ending at UTC midnight took up to 12 hours of the last day from people west of UTC, so it is never early for anyone and at most about a day late), to `confirmed` (scan basis) or `suspected`, history by `system` "Risk acceptance expired (accepted by <who> until <date>)", audit `findings.status`, event `status_changed` with `reason: acceptance_expired`, `accepted_by`, `accepted_until`; notify sends one notice "Risk acceptance ended: … is open again" (notify INV-21), so the finding never comes back silently. No new scheduler. (3) **While accepted** it behaves like false positive: a re-match or a severity raise does not reopen it, a scan records its evidence once and asks a person (POST-2), scans do not probe it, Reopen works. **Top-tier:** Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management exceptions carry a justification ("Risk accepted", "Planned remediation") and a duration, the recommendation leaves the active list and comes back when the exception expires; durations cannot be extended, a new one is made (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-vulnerability-management/tvm-exception , https://learn.microsoft.com/en-nz/defender-vulnerability-management/tvm-exception-overview ); Tenable Vulnerability Management accept rules take an optional expiry and "upon expiration … no longer accepts the risk" (https://docs.tenable.com/vulnerability-management/Content/recast/add-recast-rules.htm ); Snyk `ignore` defaults to a 30-day expiry (https://docs.snyk.io/developer-tools/snyk-cli/commands/ignore ). **Not chosen:** accept forever (the beta box showed people already misuse Not relevant for "we cannot patch until the March window", and a permanent close never comes back: an exploited CVE then stays on the network unseen; every product above makes the expiry the point); an optional date (Tenable's default is indefinite, which is the misuse we are fixing); more than a year (a yearly review is the longest any of them suggests and keeps the list honest); a new scheduler (the hourly reconcile, INV-9, already runs while the module is on). | 2026-11-13 |
| D-499 | **"I updated <software>" on a finding: the person gives the new version once, Vedette re-matches the device, and every finding that version fixes closes by itself; the others stay open and the dialog says how many (kien's N100 beta list item 14; S-MIT-1).** (1) **Where:** the finding page header, and the Findings panel of a device page (one button per hand-added software with findings, so the dialog stays while its findings close; a scanned one is checked by a scan), for the software whose KEV keys give the finding's CVE (`kev_cves` of `GET /inventory/devices/{id}`; none found → no button, the page is as before). (2) **Manual software** (`source = manual`): dialog with **New version**, prefilled with the fixed release D-488 names for this device (`fixed_in.kind = fixed`), else empty; the same version as stored or an empty box is refused before sending (an empty version would remove it, which is the device page's job); it calls the existing `PATCH /inventory/devices/{id}/software/{sid}` (inventory INV-26 (3), which emits `inventory.match.changed` after commit), then re-reads `GET /findings?asset=` until the re-match shows (a finding of this software changed status, `last_seen` or history, or a new one appeared), at most 12 reads 500 ms apart, never a fixed sleep. Outcome: "Version 7.4.5 saved. 12 findings on <device> no longer apply and were closed. 2 still match this version." (closed = open before, closed after; still = open findings of this software's CVEs after), or "Vedette is checking the new version; this list updates in a moment." `bad_version` / `duplicate_software` / `not_manual` map to plain sentences. (3) **Software a scan, sensor or agent reported:** "I updated it" opens the same dialog without a version box: "Vedette reads this version from the device. Run a scan of <device> to check." with the existing Scan link (`/scans?target=`) when the device has an IP. No new route, no backend change: closing is D-530's proof (`not_relevant`, reason `not_affected_version`), reopened by D-530 (3) if a later match says otherwise.
