Each sends one NTLM NEGOTIATE (type 1) with no credentials and reads the CHALLENGE (type 2), which carries the device's Windows version and build and its names; neither ever sends an AUTHENTICATE (type 3), so nothing logs in. rdp-ntlm-info runs only on an open RDP port, http-ntlm-info only on an open HTTP port (a GET of `/`; nmap's http library follows a few redirects, only on the same host, port and scheme, never with credentials). The probe log's `flags` column (INV-9) holds the line with the scripts. They are in `normal` too, not only `versions`: otherwise a device identified as a PC would get the `-O` shape on its next scan and lose its build to the fingerprint guess. **Not chosen**: `smb-os-discovery` (it opens an anonymous, then a guest, SMB session, which is a logon attempt that shows up in the device's security log, and it needs SMBv1, which Windows 10 and 11 turn off); `smb-protocols`/`smb2-capabilities`/`smb2-time` (they give only dialects, capabilities or the clock, never the OS or its build; the Windows answer on 135/445 is already in `-sV`'s banner); `ms-sql-ntlm-info`, `smtp-ntlm-info` and the other NTLM scripts (they work the same way but for services rare on a small office's devices; add one when a walk needs it). **Version skew**: a job carries the shape name, not the argv (D-111 (3)), so a worker from an older release builds its own line for `normal`/`versions`, without the scripts. Core and the scan worker ship in one release, so this lasts only during an update. The probe log then lists scripts that were not sent, never the other way round, and identification works as in D-501. No proto bump and no new shape: a new shape would make the older worker refuse every discovery scan (`invalid_job`). (2) **The NTLM answer is untrusted** (INV-7): only `<elem>` of those two script ids on an open port is read; `Product_Version` must be `major.minor.build` (no revision, e.g. `10.0.22631`), names `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,99}$`, each at most 256 bytes and printable, the first value wins; anything else is dropped, and the XML limits of the parser still fail the whole batch. (3) **What it records**, only when something else on the device says Windows (review M1): `-sV` read a Microsoft product on the port that answered (Microsoft Terminal Services, Microsoft IIS httpd, Microsoft HTTPAPI), or 135 and 445 are open; and no sure non-Windows fingerprint and no non-Microsoft OS CPE of a service (OpenSSH's Ubuntu banner) says otherwise. FreeRDP-based RDP servers on Linux (gnome-remote-desktop) answer 6.1.7601, and proxies pass IIS's NTLM through: without this check a Linux box became "Windows 7". Then: the OS at the top nmap confidence (0.95; it outranks the `-O` guess), its computer name when nmap has none, and one software row (`microsoft`/`windows`, `windows server` for a server). A build only a client has gives that release and type pc (`Microsoft Windows 11 23H2 (build 22631)`); a build only Windows Server has (20348) gives that release and type server; a build both share (14393, 17763, 26100, and the 6.x ones) **names both and gives no type** (`Microsoft Windows 10 1809 / Server 2019 (build 17763)`, review M2: in a small office 14393 and 17763 are mostly Server 2016/2019), unless 88 and 389 are open (a domain controller, so Windows Server); an unknown build is "Windows" with the build, no type ("Windows Server" on a domain controller). Builds map to releases by Microsoft's release tables. **The row has its version but no KEV match keys** (`Guess`, as D-501 does with a fingerprint): the device names its release but not its monthly update revision (UBR), and NVD ends Windows ranges at a revision (`10.0.22631.4317`), so with keys it would mark every Windows flaw fixed since that release as affected: the false-CVE flood of D-501 (3). The identification reason is the new `os_no_patch_level`, whose note says to add the system it runs, Windows or Windows Server (winver shows which), with its full version on the device page, or install the osquery agent. (4) **Port rule**: with no type from NTLM or a sure fingerprint, RPC 135 and SMB 445 open together set the type pc (server with 88 and 389) at 0.4, never an OS or a version, and **only after the versions scan** (review H1). The inventory ranks a value by source before confidence and `nmap` outranks `passive`, so after a gentle or normal scan this 0.4 would beat any passive type: a printer, PLC or camera that passive data typed (Windows-embedded HMIs and print servers have 135 and 445) would become a pc, lose "fragile" and get the full scan. The versions scan is only for a device whose type is still unknown, with no passive, agent or manual type (`pickedPlan`), so there the rule replaces nothing. 445 alone gives nothing: Samba NAS boxes have it. `-O` stays off for unknown devices (`versions`), and fragile types (printer, camera, PLC…) still get only the gentle scan (D-45). (5) **W3-5: an OS banner is not software.** A service whose only CPE is an OS one (`cpe:/o:`) or that has no CPE gives a software row only when `-sV` read its version: "Microsoft Windows RPC" (`cpe:/o:microsoft:windows`) and other versionless banners stay under open services only. An application or device CPE (`cpe:/a:`, `cpe:/h:`) stays a software row even without a version (review M3): a product match on an edge appliance (an SSL VPN or OWA banner) is what the KEV list is about, and dropping it would be a silent false negative; the W3-5 complaint came from OS-type banners. (6) **W3-6: the first scheduled scan of a box runs in the next allowed window**: while no scheduled run has ever started (no `scan_run` with trigger `schedule`; W3-9 below), every window day's slot at the schedule time counts, whatever the weekday of a weekly schedule, and next run says so (Friday 14:40 with the weekly Sunday 23:00 default and 22:00–05:00 every day: "tonight 23:00", not "15 Nov"). Such an extra slot that closed or had nothing to scan is not recorded (no "missed" audit), so the first run is the first window that scans something; from then on the weekday counts. An extra slot counts only when the schedule was saved and the scope confirmed **before** it (review M4, the rule `missSlot` uses for "due"): a box set up at 23:30 inside an open window waits for the next night instead of starting at once. A first run on the night before the weekday is followed by the weekday's run the next night (Saturday, then Sunday): accepted, the first check is what was late. A daily schedule is unchanged. **W3-9 (customer walk 3)**: "no first run yet" means no `scan_run` with trigger `schedule` ever started, not `sched_last` empty: the N100 recorded its first Sunday slot (missed or nothing to scan) before any run, so the rule never applied and Friday still showed "15 Nov". A weekday slot that was missed or had nothing to scan still records `sched_last` (no second try of that slot, no double run) but no longer ends the first-run period; next run and the job use the same rule, and the mock already did. `updated_at` NULL (defaults never saved) does not hold the first run back; the scope confirmation time still does. | runZero fingerprints Windows from the NTLM challenge of SMB, RDP and HTTP without credentials and keeps where each value came from (https://help.runzero.com/docs/fingerprinting/); Tenable reads the OS from SMB "by sending an authentication request to port 139 or 445" (plugin 10785, Microsoft Windows SMB NativeLanManager Remote System Information Disclosure, https://www.tenable.com/plugins/nessus/10785); Vedette keeps only the part that sends no credentials and never completes a logon. nmap: rdp-ntlm-info sends "an incomplete CredSSP (NTLM) authentication request with null credentials" and prints Product_Version (https://nmap.org/nsedoc/scripts/rdp-ntlm-info.html); http-ntlm-info the same over HTTP (https://nmap.org/nsedoc/scripts/http-ntlm-info.html); smb-os-discovery starts "a session with the anonymous account" and has a `smbnoguest` option (https://nmap.org/nsedoc/scripts/smb-os-discovery.html); smb-protocols lists dialects only (https://nmap.org/nsedoc/scripts/smb-protocols.html). Windows builds: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/release-health/release-information, https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/release-health/windows11-release-information, https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/get-started/windows-server-release-info. First run: PRODUCT promises a new box knows its network within an hour, and D-501 (5) already runs discovery's first pass at once; a weekly default must not make the first vulnerability check wait up to a week. | 2026-11-13 |
| D-505 | **A CISA "Multiple Products" entry gives a finding only when NVD names the device's own software, and NVD naming other products never closes one; the box carries its own OS (customer walk 3 W3-7, W3-8; narrows D-500 (2); S-INV-4, S-INV-5; revised after review H1 of #671).** (1) **Matcher** (`modules/findings` `decide`): a "<vendor> \| Multiple Products" entry is still keyed by the vendor, but CISA's text names no product, so only NVD's CPE list can tie it to a software. An NVD entry naming the software itself (its CPE, name or `nvd-cpe.json` alias) is evaluated like any entry (version inside → basis version; unreadable → product, medium). **No NVD data yet → no finding** (was: a vendor-wide product finding); the entry stays on Home as CISA news, and the rematch after `nvd-kev` (and the hourly one, INV-9) picks it up when NVD lists products. **Known gap (review M1):** between CISA adding a new "Multiple Products" entry and NVD analysing it (days), plus up to one day for the daily `nvd-kev` pull, no finding and no alert exist for it; the old vendor-wide guess covered that window with noise. A vendor-level notice without findings is the follow-up (`.ai/deferred/fix-match-multi-products-box-os.md`; needs a story first). **NVD lists only other products → no finding.** An NVD entry with vendor or product ANY (may be this software) → product finding, medium, as before. (2) **An old finding is never closed by this rule** (D-530 (2) "Never" unchanged): NVD's product list for a "Multiple Products" CVE is built from the CVE text and lags the vendor's advisory when the vendor adds products later. Example: CVE-2024-23113 lists fortios, fortipam, fortiproxy and fortiswitchmanager in NVD, while Fortinet's advisory FG-IR-24-029, as the reviewer recalls it (not checked here: no network in this session), also lists FortiWeb 7.4.0–7.4.2: a FortiWeb 7.4.1 would have been closed, and the later reopen (`not_relevant` → `suspected`) sends no alert because notify only alerts on `confirmed` (review H1 of #671; a first version of this decision closed such findings when NVD named the software in another entry: withdrawn). So the old open finding stays open for a person: it takes the product severity (3) and gets one `no_longer_matches` history row with the reason: "NVD lists fusion, horizon client, remote console for CVE-2020-3950, not VMware Tools; check the vendor advisory and close it if it does not apply." (`MatchResult.Unlisted`; the vendor's own products only when NVD lists any; a `no_longer_matches` row is written again only when its sentence differs from the last one, so the N100's earlier generic row is followed once by this one). A person closes the three VMware findings (one by one or bulk, INV-10). **Top-tier:** Tenable and Qualys mark a finding Fixed only when their own per-product check (a plugin or QID written from the vendor advisory) shows it gone, never because NVD's CPE list leaves the product out (https://docs.tenable.com/vulnerability-management/Content/Explore/Findings/VulnerabilityStates.htm , https://docs.qualys.com/en/vmdr/latest/scans/vulnerability_status.htm). (3) **W3-3 reached the findings the matcher no longer produces**: the re-grade to medium ran only for pairs the matcher produced again (`Existing`), so an old product finding the matcher stopped producing kept `high` and its old `last_seen` forever (walk 3: "High", "last seen 49 min ago": it was evaluated, but `last_seen` is the last time the matcher *saw* the pair). Now `noteNoLongerMatching` also lowers an open suspected product finding above medium to medium, once, audit `findings.regraded`. (4) **Box OS (W3-8)**: the box device had no OS, so `osRulesOut` could not apply and CVE-2021-3493 (OverlayFS, NVD lists only Ubuntu releases up to 20.10) stayed a product finding on boxkien while the agent host `byn` (same Ubuntu 26.04) had it ruled out. vedette-host already reads `/etc/os-release` for `GET /v1/info` (`os.distro`, `os.release`); core's box-name reader (`cmd/vedette/boxname.go`, same call, same 10-minute cache) now keeps `boxOS(info.OS)` ("Ubuntu 26.04"; only `ubuntu`/`debian`, the appliance's releases, and a numeric release, checked again in core), and the inventory's `box` job passes it as `BoxInfo.OS` (an `os` observation, source agent, confidence 1, like an agent host's). No answer from the host, or container-only → the row's OS is kept / stays unknown. No host API change (the field exists since the first host), no new data flow. The finding closes at the next findings pass (start of the module, then hourly, INV-9). **Top-tier:** vulnerability managers match vulnerabilities to installed software per product, never per vendor: Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management maps the software inventory to CPEs and lists a CVE only for software it is mapped to (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-vulnerability-management/tvm-software-inventory); Wazuh's detector matches packages against per-product CTI data (https://documentation.wazuh.com/current/user-manual/capabilities/vulnerability-detection/index.html); GitHub Dependabot alerts only when the repository's dependency is a package named in the advisory's affected list (https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/dependabot/dependabot-alerts/about-dependabot-alerts). CISA's catalog itself only lists "Multiple Products" and points to the vendor advisory (https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog); NVD's configurations are the machine-readable product list (https://nvd.nist.gov/developers/vulnerabilities). Not chosen: keeping the vendor-wide guess until NVD lists the product (walk 3: noise the customer had to close by hand); closing old findings when NVD lists only other products, even for a software NVD names in its own entries (review H1: NVD lags the advisory, and the reopen is silent); a new `resolution_reason` such as `not_listed_by_nvd` (moot without the close; it would also need a rebuild of `fnd_finding`, the parent of `ON DELETE CASCADE` keys, inside goose's transaction, https://www.sqlite.org/lang_droptable.html , https://www.sqlite.org/foreignkeys.html); reading os-release inside the container (the container's OS is not the box's). **Narrowed by D-506 (2026-11-13):** an old open product finding of a "Multiple Products" entry that CISA added at least a year ago, whose NVD list names none of the device's software of that vendor, now closes by itself (`not_relevant`, system, reason `not_affected_version`, note "Closed by Vedette: …"); recent entries keep (2), and version, scan, confirmed and person-reopened findings are never closed. The three VMware Tools findings of the N100 close at the next reconcile pass. | 2026-11-13 |
| D-506 | **An old product finding of a CISA "<vendor> \| Multiple Products" entry closes by itself when NVD names none of the device's software of that vendor and CISA added the entry at least a year ago (customer walk 3 W3-7, n16; narrows D-505 (2) and the "Never" list of D-530 (2); S-INV-2).** (1) **Rule** (`modules/findings` `MatchAsset` → `MatchResult.Retired`, `Service.autoResolve`): a **suspected** finding of basis **product** (never version, scan, confirmed, or a finding a person closed or ever reopened) whose CVE is a "Multiple Products" entry closes as `not_relevant` by the system user when (a) NVD has data for the CVE and every readable entry names another product than each of the device's software keyed to that vendor (D-505's "Unlisted" outcome for **every** such software: one software that NVD names, ruled out by range or not, keeps D-505) and (b) the entry's `dateAdded` is at least 365 days before the pass (`findings.SettledKEV`; read through the existing `Feeds.Vulns`, `Vuln.DateAdded`; an unknown date is never settled). Same path as D-530: history `not_relevant` with the sentence, audit `findings.auto_resolved` (detail names D-506), event `status_changed` suspected → not_relevant, reopen by itself (`matches_again`) when NVD later names the software and the version matches. `resolution_reason` stays `not_affected_version`: migration `findings/0004` has `CHECK (resolution_reason IN ('not_affected_version'))`, and a new value needs a rebuild of `fnd_finding`, the parent of `ON DELETE CASCADE` keys (D-505), so the note says why: "Closed by Vedette: CISA lists CVE-2020-3950 for several VMware products; NVD names fusion, horizon client, remote console, not VMware Tools (settled: CISA added it over a year ago). Vedette checks it again whenever NVD's data for it changes." Recent entries keep D-505: open at medium with the "check the vendor advisory" note. (2) **Why it is safe enough:** the current matcher never creates this finding on a fresh device (D-505 (1)), so closing a row a retired rule made leaves the customer exactly where a new device is; the round-1 worry of #671 (NVD's list lags the vendor advisory) is a lag of the months after publication, and an entry a year old has had its analysis. **Residual risk, accepted:** NVD rarely re-analyses an old CVE, so a product the vendor added to its advisory and NVD never added stays unnamed for good. Example from review H1 of #671 (as the reviewer recalls Fortinet FG-IR-24-029, not checked here: no network in this session): CVE-2024-23113 (KEV 2024-10-09) lists FortiWeb 7.4.0–7.4.2 in the advisory but not in NVD; an old FortiWeb product finding for it now closes. A fresh FortiWeb device already gets no finding for it (D-505), so this is the same gap, not a new one; the reopen when NVD adds the product is silent until notify alerts on `reason: matches_again` (`.ai/deferred/fix-multi-products-old-rows-close.md`). (3) **Why it did not close on the N100 (n16):** the findings were evaluated: the start and hourly reconcile pass (INV-9) reaches every suspected finding whose CVE is in the list through `noteNoLongerMatching`, which is how they turned Medium and got the D-505 note. Nothing closed because D-505 after review H1 never closes; `last_seen` only moves when the matcher produces the pair; and the job's own "job finished" line is debug, so the core log showed nothing. Reconcile now logs one info line per pass ("findings: reconcile pass done", with `closed_multiple_products`), and a device that closes any logs "findings: closed (D-506)…" with the count. Golden test `TestGolden_VMwareToolsMultipleProducts` (real NVD data: the three close at the first pass, a 100-day-old entry stays open with the note, a version finding and a person-reopened one stay open, a second pass changes nothing, NVD naming Tools reopens it), `TestMultipleProducts_RetiresOnlyWhenNoSoftwareIsNamed`. **Top-tier:** vulnerability managers do not raise vendor-wide findings at all; they check per product, so a vendor-wide guess never exists to be closed: Tenable writes one plugin per product and advisory and marks a finding Fixed when that check no longer fires (https://docs.tenable.com/vulnerability-management/Content/Explore/Findings/VulnerabilityStates.htm , https://www.tenable.com/plugins); Qualys detects per QID, each written for named products, and sets Fixed when the detection is gone (https://docs.qualys.com/en/vmdr/latest/scans/vulnerability_status.htm); Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management lists a CVE only for software its inventory maps to the CVE's CPEs (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-vulnerability-management/tvm-software-inventory). CISA's `dateAdded` is the catalog's own field (https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog); NVD's configurations and analysis status: https://nvd.nist.gov/developers/vulnerabilities , https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/vulnerability-status . | D-507 | **A URL honey token fires when its link is opened: core answers `/t/<id>` itself, records a real token hit through the honeypot's hit path, and every `/t/<anything>` gets the same plain 404 (customer walk 1 W1-28, P0; S-HP-2, honeypot POST-2/POST-4).** (1) **Before**: nothing served `/t/`. The link a URL token hands out (D-465: Box address + `/t/<10 characters>`) fell through to the interface (D-149), so opening it from a laptop returned the Vedette app's index page (200) and recorded nothing: only "Test token" ever fired one. (2) **Route** (`cmd/vedette/honeytoken.go`, `topHandler`): any method on `/t/{id}` and `/t/{id}/{rest...}` (a trailing slash or a path a link checker added fires on the id; punctuation an auto-linker or a sentence glued to the id, `.,;:!?'")]}>*`, is dropped; `/t/` alone stays the interface's), with no session, no CSRF check, behind the same Host allowlist (421 first) and Envelope as everything else. A well-formed id (10 of `a-z0-9`, `honeypot.ValidURLTokenID`) is handed to `honeypot.Service.OpenURLToken` with the connection's peer address (`RemoteAddr`; never a forwarded header) and the User-Agent. **The box itself** never fires its own token: loopback, the box's address in the inventory (INV-3, as the trap log), and on the appliance every machine address (`machineAddrs`, D-446: what vedette-host reports and the bridge gateway its host's own requests arrive from). **Source on a container-only install** (review L3): the rootful DNAT of D-167 keeps the visitor's address only on the appliance; without vedette-host a port proxy may stand in between, so an open from a machine address (the gateway) is recorded with the source `unknown (container-only port proxy)` (stored `src_ip` `unknown`, which response skips), never naming the gateway as the machine to unplug; a LAN address that does reach core is named. An IPv6 visitor fires too: `hp_hits.src_ip` is IPv4 only, so the row stores `unknown` and the event, its line and the incident carry the address. **Budgets** (review M2): the record is detached from the request (a visitor who hangs up does not cancel it) and carries no request write wait limit; the write has 5 s and the publish a fresh 30 s (the bus still gives each handler its own 5 s), so a slow write never eats the time notify needs to open the incident. (3) **Hit** (`modules/honeypot/urltoken.go`): the token is found by the **path alone** (`value` ends in `/t/<id>`), so a link made before a Box address change still fires; only a URL token that still exists counts (INV-10); module off, loopback (the box itself) or no address → nothing. The hit goes through the same `upsert` as a bait account or file seen in the trap log: kind `token`, label `URL token <name>`, the source IP, the time, the User-Agent cleaned and cut to 200 characters (INV-12), one hit per token, source and 10-minute window (later opens add a line and `conn_count`), the per-hour cap, and `honeypot.hit.created` after the commit, so notify opens the **Critical** incident (now titled for tokens: "<ip> opened the URL token <name>"; a credential token reads "used") and Telegram/e-mail send it, and response sees its trigger. (4) **Answer**: always `404 page not found` (text/plain, `no-store`, the Envelope's headers): the token, an unknown id, a malformed id, a deleted token, module off, over the limit. The visitor sees a dead link, never the app (which would name Vedette and give the trap away), and a guessed id cannot be told from a real one. (5) **Limit** (review M1): the first open of a token from a source in a 10-minute window **always** records; it is bounded by the upsert dedupe (one row per token, source and window) and the 2,000-per-hour cap shared with the trap log. Only a **repeat** open of an existing hit asks the limit, 10 per address and minute (`server.AddrLimiter`, the sliding window of D-320, IPv6 per /64, loopback not counted); past it the same 404 and no write. The limit is never asked for a made-up id, so ten fake opens cannot silence the real link (before review M1 they could, and an IPv6 /64 is often the whole LAN). (6) **DNS tokens cannot fire**: the box has no DNS server, so no lookup of `<name>.vedette.internal` reaches anything that records it, even with the zone forwarded to the box (the old hint said to forward it). The GUI now says so in the type hint, on the token's card ("nothing yet…") and in the coverage guide, and **Create token** is disabled for the DNS type; building a DNS listener is not part of this decision. | Thinkst Canarytokens' web bug / URL token alerts on any fetch of the URL and answers a harmless response (by default a 1×1 GIF, or a redirect the owner sets) so the visitor sees nothing alarming (https://docs.canarytokens.org/guide/http-token.html); a link a person opens and that answers with an image or a blank page looks odd, so here a plain 404 is the answer: an intruder following a wiki link sees a dead link, the commonest thing a stale wiki link does. Canarytokens' DNS token fires only because Thinkst runs the authoritative server of its domain (https://docs.canarytokens.org/guide/dns-token.html); a box with no DNS server cannot, so the GUI says so rather than offering a token that never fires. Not chosen: a fake login page (a page to maintain, and it invites typing a real password into the box); a 200 SPA-like page (shows Vedette); 429 past the limit (tells the visitor the path is special); a forwarded-for header as the source (any client can set it). | 2026-11-13 |

Rootless storage under `/home` is never read nor touched, as before. Names from podman are untrusted: cut to `[A-Za-z0-9_.:@/-]` (anything else becomes `?`) and 64 bytes before they are printed. (2) **What stays** (`podman_stays`, `purge_added_packages`): podman and the packages it runs with (`podman_pkgs`: podman, crun, runc, conmon, netavark, aardvark-dns, catatonit, containers-common by name, every installed package podman Depends on down the tree and the installed ones it Recommends, from the local apt cache) are neither candidates nor purged; the ones the script asked for by name are marked manual again (`apt-mark manual`), so a later `apt autoremove` keeps them too; every other package the installer added is handled as before. The D-463 wipe of `/var/lib/containers`, `/run/containers` and podman's folders is skipped (`[ -z "$KEEP_PODMAN" ]` in its gate). When the foreign things include containers or pods (or podman did not answer), IP forwarding and netavark's nft tables also stay: they carry those containers' NAT and port forwards. (3) **`--keep-data`** (repair, redeploy) always keeps podman and its storage, foreign or not: the customer chose to keep things and the next install runs Vedette on the same runtime without downloading it again. The kept packages stay on `asked-packages` and `installed-by-us` (every other line is cleared as before), so a later `--uninstall` without `--keep-data` on a podman that holds nothing else still purges podman and its storage (D-463's clean uninstall). A plain range bound is NVD's version alone: "before 20.4" holds every 15.1 and no 20.4 update (NVD lists those as entries of their own); an X train against a bound of its own release, or a bound in another train type, is Unknown; a Junos row NVD writes in another form is Unknown. NVD lists Junos updates one by one, with gaps (CVE-2020-1631: 15.1R7 to R7-S5 but not S6, Juniper's fix being S7; 12.3R12-S8 and -S11 but not -S9/-S10; 17.3R1-S1 but not 17.3R1), and Juniper fixes per maintenance branch ("22.3 before 22.3R2-S2, 22.3R3-S1": NVD lists up to 22.3R2-S1, then 22.3R3), so when every row rules the version out the exact rows of the device's own branch (release, train and R/F number, or X train) decide (`junosListed`): between its first and last listed update → affected; before the first → Unknown; after the last → no finding but no proof (22.3R2-S2, JSA11021's fixed builds 18.4R1-S7, 17.4R1-S8…); a branch NVD skips between or before listed ones → Unknown, after every one → no finding, no proof; a release NVD skips between listed ones (21.3 between 21.2 and 21.4; a range's end release counts as listed) → Unknown; the range's end release itself, a release listed only in rows Vedette does not read ("15.1:f", "15.1:a1"; "15.1:-" → Unknown) or only in other trains, or one before every listed release → no finding, no proof; only a version after every release NVD lists is proved not affected (D-530 may close a finding). This applies only when a Junos row decided. **Ceiling (ponytail):** a build after the last listed update of its branch is taken as fixed, so a build NVD forgot is missed (CVE-2020-1631: 15.1R7-S6, Juniper's fix being R7-S7); Unknown there would flag every patched build. Upgrade path: read Juniper's "versions prior to Y" list from the NVD description / JSA text for each branch's exact fixed build, which also settles skipped branches. Before, ".9" was read as Ivanti's "R2.4" (a release of its own) and an X train or an X entry was unreadable, so 15.1R7.9 against CVE-2020-1631 was "not checked". (3) **Series** (`findings.otherSeries`): CISA's entry names the Juniper series a Junos flaw is about ("… EX Series and SRX Series …", "… SRX Series …"; the NVD rows Vedette keeps name only the OS). | D-530 | **A suspected finding (basis version or product) that the matcher proves outside every affected range of its CVE closes by itself; it reopens by itself when a later match says the device is affected (walk 3 W3-2; narrows FORBID-2 of findings).** (1) **Rule:** status `not_relevant`, `resolved_by` the system user, new column `fnd_finding.resolution_reason = 'not_affected_version'` (migration `0004_resolution_reason.sql`, export policy updated), the matcher's sentence as resolution note and history row ("Not affected: version 3.5.5 of OpenSSL is outside every version range NVD lists for CVE-2014-0160. The list's default filter (Unresolved) no longer shows it; nothing is deleted. (2) **Only a positive proof closes** (`MatchResult.NotAffected`): every software of the device keyed to the entry has a **readable** version (`versionKnown`) outside every applicable NVD entry with nothing undecidable, or the entry lists only releases of the device's own distribution and the device's release (readable) is not one of them (CVE-2021-3493 on Ubuntu 26.04). (3) **Reopen:** a finding with that reason that the matcher produces again goes back to `suspected` (resolution fields cleared, history `matches_again` "…so Vedette reopened it…", audit `findings.matches_again`, event not_relevant → suspected); a scan confirmation reopens it as `confirmed` (like patched). A person's own `not_relevant`, `false_positive`, `patched` or `mitigated` is never reopened by the matcher (INV-6 unchanged for them). A finding Vedette closed that a person then reopened (their `reopened` history row after the last system `not_relevant`) is never closed by the matcher again: the person overruled the proof (review M-b of #663; no new column, the history is the marker). (4) **Why `not_relevant` and not a new status:** the CHECK of `fnd_finding.status` would need a table rebuild and every status consumer (GUI filters, reports, SIEM, export) would change; "does not apply to this device" is what `not_relevant` already means, and the reason column says who decided and why. | D-531a | **Review of #688 (2026-11-13), three additions to D-531.** (1) **"Used up" only when the tokens spent reach the budget** (`Meter.UsedUp`): when the spent tokens are below it and the holds of calls in flight cover the rest, the call is refused with 429 `rate_limited` ("Other AI calls running now are holding the rest of this month's AI budget … Try again in a few seconds.", `retry_after` 15), never with "used up", so the message never disagrees with Home below 100 %. (2) **Scheduled AI jobs pause at 80 %** (`scheduledPausePct`, every `RunJob` with Actor `system`, today the response plans): from 80 % of the month's shared budget spent, and when it is used up, they get 429 `budget_reached` before anything is done: no provider call, no `capped` row every 5 minutes, one box log line a month; Ask, Explain and every job a person starts keep the last 20 %. (3) Every 429 `budget_reached` carries `retry_after` (seconds to the renewal, API_CONVENTIONS §8); the budget watch with notify off waits quietly (`ErrAlertOff`) instead of failing every 5 minutes; a hold taken before the month turns and settled after it no longer lowers the new month's holds. | **Sources:** GitHub Copilot and Actions budgets stop paid usage only when the spent amount reaches the budget, not on in-flight work (https://docs.github.com/en/billing/concepts/budgets-and-alerts); the OpenAI and Anthropic rate limits answer a temporary refusal with 429 and `retry-after` (https://docs.anthropic.com/claude/reference/rate-limits); Kubernetes and cloud schedulers give interactive work priority over batch work under a shared quota (https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/scheduling-eviction/pod-priority-preemption/). **Not chosen:** a per-job token quota (D-531 (4): a real incident must not be skipped because a job used its share; the pause applies to scheduled jobs as a group); pausing at the 80 % warning for every job (a person's question is what the reserve is for). | 2026-11-13 |
| D-540 | **My account là mục của Settings; kiểm cập nhật không có gì mới là 200 "You're on the latest version", không tới được nguồn thì nói host và lý do (W1-26, M5-181; S-CORE-3, S-CORE-2).** (1) `/settings/account` là mục Settings (`core`, mọi vai, thứ tự cuối, nơi liên kết My account cũ nằm); menu tài khoản trỏ tới đó; `/account` chuyển hướng (giữ `?` và `#`, nên liên kết `/account#two-step`, dấu trang và `next` của SSO vẫn đúng); tiêu đề tab "My account". (2) Nguồn trả 404 cho chính tệp index (không phải `.minisig`) **và hộp chưa từng lưu index nào** (chưa công bố bản nào) = lần kiểm tốt không có gì đề nghị: 200, `last_check` dời, lỗi cũ xoá. Đã lưu index rồi mà nguồn trả 404 (nguồn rút bản, proxy chặn), hay chỉ thiếu chữ ký → 503 `update_source_unreachable`, `last_check` giữ nguyên, lỗi được lưu, nên chế độ tự động không cài đề nghị cũ (review Opus của #709); mã `update_not_published` (D-407) không còn gửi, giữ trong enum `UpdateCheckError.code` chỉ để bản ghi của bản cũ vẫn đọc được. Toast "You're on the latest version (X)." (3) `update_source_unreachable` (503 giữ nguyên) nói "Could not reach the update source (<host>): <lý do>. Try again later; …", lý do là chữ cố định theo loại lỗi (`unreachableReason`: DNS, không trả lời kịp, chuyển hướng tới host không cho phép, …), host từ cấu hình; không chép chữ hay mã trạng thái nhận từ mạng (INV-34). | Home Assistant: kiểm cập nhật không có bản mới nói "You're running the latest version" (https://www.home-assistant.io/common-tasks/os/#update), không báo lỗi; Grafana hiện "You are running the latest version"/phiên bản ở trang Help (https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/upgrade-guide/); GitHub REST trả 200 `[]` cho danh sách rỗng (https://docs.github.com/en/rest/releases/releases#list-releases): không có bản phát hành là trạng thái bình thường, không phải lỗi máy chủ cổng 502. Lỗi mạng thật giữ 503 (RFC 9110 §15.6.4) nhưng nói lý do cụ thể như Home Assistant "Unable to reach …"/Grafana "Failed to check for updates" kèm nguyên nhân. Hồ sơ cá nhân trong Settings: GitHub Settings → Public profile/Account ở cùng menu dọc (https://docs.github.com/en/account-and-profile), GitLab User settings → Account; tách ra ngoài khung (cách cũ) làm người dùng rời menu Settings khi bấm mục trong chính menu đó. Không chọn: đưa My account lên đầu (đổi trang mở mặc định của Settings mà quản trị viên đã quen); bỏ hẳn mã `update_not_published` khỏi enum (bản ghi đã lưu trên hộp thật sẽ làm GET /core/updates hỏng khi kiểm kiểu) | 2026-11-14 |
